dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theore.technical:
At a tame corank-one wall $\Sigma$ the cometric on covectors acquires a one-dimensional radical $\mathcal{L}$, spanned by a covector $k$. The Clifford sheaf continues across the wall, and the physical metric has a simple pole along $\mathcal{L}\otimes\mathcal{L}$ with $\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sigma$, so the dying line is a square root of the conormal bundle. Exactly there the completion adjoins a Witt partner $k^*$ of the radical covector, with $kk^* + k^*k = 1$, that is $\ip{k}{k^*} = \tfrac12$; rescaling $k^*$ to $\ip{k}{k^*} = 1$ changes nothing.

The imported sphere theorem adds that the transverse sphere is carried by the bilinear matrix algebra of the boundary modes through the principal embedding, so every angular operator of the lift is a boundary-mode bilinear under the adjoint $\mathfrak{su}(2)$. This clause is derived under the Indifference principle (a construction may not carry distinctions that nothing in the framework determines), which its source declares a premise and not a theorem, so it holds only conditionally on that premise.
dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theore.lay: Where geometry degenerates in the mildest, tame way, along a wall where one direction stops being measurable, the algebraic description of geometry does not break but carries on through the wall. The metric blows up there in a controlled way, and the completion adds exactly one partner to the dying direction. A further imported result, which rests on an assumed principle (the Indifference principle) rather than a proof, says that the sphere of directions around the wall is built from pairings of the wall's boundary modes.

__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-position-series:
This paper is T10 of the series. \emph{It relies on eight papers:} the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} for the Clifford and bivector language; the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1} for the standard of proof and the Fact (imported) discipline every result here is held to; the sheaf paper T4 \cite{ButlerT4} for the continuation of the ambient structure across a tame wall and the corank-one radical (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} for the s-wave current algebra and, under the singularity paper's premise (Q), its thermal state (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-s-wave-current-algebra}); the geometry paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6} for the frozen point, the tractor connection and the exterior exactness (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-frozen-point-geometry}, Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.lift-inherits-no-go-steps-itemised}); the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} for the finite-window quantification of the current algebra; the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} for the sphere theorem that carries the sphere step (Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-walls-sphere-theorem}); and, later in the series, the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} for the rescaling argument that the norm is not kinematic (Fact \claimref{standard-model.trichotomy-what-kind-number}), with no circularity, since that argument uses only the conformal class and the pair structure.

\emph{Papers that rely on this one:} the mass paper T11 \cite{ButlerT11} imports the action theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}) for its gravity assembly; the standard-model paper T12 \cite{ButlerT12} shares the two-kinds theorem (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.gravity-pre-metric-forces-degenerate-exactly}), uses the action's single coupling, and reads its classification's initial-data clause against Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws}; the dark-matter paper T14 \cite{ButlerT14} imports the acoustic no-go and the $w = -1$ registration (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}); the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8} and the Hawking paper T7 \cite{ButlerT7} refer the engineering no-go and the lift's dynamics to this paper; and the capstone T17 \cite{ButlerT17} tabulates this paper's claims at their tiers.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-which-wall-sold: Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector} is a theorem about a soldering form with a radical: $g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{ab}e^a_\mu e^b_\nu$ degenerate, the metric on tangent vectors acquiring a null direction. The sheaf paper's tame wall is a degeneration of the \emph{cometric}, the form on covectors, and the two are not the same degeneration. The following proposition records exactly how they differ, what the sheaf paper's wall looks like in soldering variables, and which piece of the completion the wall's extra freedom is.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.what-settles-what-it-re: Two things are settled. The symmetric form $M$ of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector} is the free sector of a wall of the soldering form, the degeneration dual to the sheaf paper's, and it is not the completion's sector at the sheaf paper's wall; the claim that the sheaf paper's wall is a wall of the soldering form is withdrawn. And the completion's ladder pair does appear in the dynamics at the sheaf paper's wall, but as gauge, not as a field: the wall opens exactly one new gauge generator per point, the dilation of the dying line, and that generator is the boost of the ladder plane $\mathrm{span}(k, k^*)$. The half-power weight that the sheaf paper's residue theorem assigns to $k$ ($\mathcal{L}^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sigma$) is a particular gauge choice for this generator, the one that makes the exceptional algebra nondegenerate. What is reformulated is the dynamical question: whether the equations demand the completion becomes, at the sheaf paper's wall, the question of how the MacDowell-Mansouri datum fails to extend, and the section “The interface at the Schwarzschild wall: the datum has a pole, and its residue is the completion's weight” answers it for the Schwarzschild wall: the datum's connection has a simple pole, and the residues of that pole are the weights from which the completion is built.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-interface-schwa: Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}(iv) left one question: whether the MacDowell-Mansouri datum $(\nabla, I, X)$ extends regularly across the sheaf paper's wall. For the Schwarzschild singularity the geometry and sheaf papers between them already contain the answer, and this subsection extracts it and computes what it does to the action.

\emph{Proved in this paper, at the standard of the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1}:} the Stelle-West lemma, with the norm $-3/\Lambda$, the soldering identity $\nabla V = \nabla X = e$, the connection decomposition and the bracket sign (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.stelle-west-vector-frozen-point}); the reduction, the Stelle-West datum and the scalar form of the functional (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(i)-(iii)); the polynomiality and the pole with the vanishing interior variation of the Gauss-Bonnet term (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1)-(2), the expansion itself imported); __notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-interface-schwa: The two remaining qualifications carried by Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-wall-residue-sense} are now discharged in turn: the divergent value, and the variable-exponent class.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.what-three-discharges-l: The residue statement of Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-wall-residue-sense} now holds with $\Lambda$ (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}), with a finite renormalised action whose only ambiguity is a scheme constant (Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm}), and pointwise for the diagonal variable-exponent class (Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are}), where the sheaf paper's variable-order structure \cite[\S 9]{ButlerT4} is the Gram-level counterpart. What is not done: the subleading momentum constraints of the variable-exponent class, which decide which exponent fields $p_i(x)$ the equations admit, and the non-diagonal class, where the frame directions themselves rotate as the wall is approached; both are the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching \cite[Rem.~8.28]{ButlerT4}, and the logarithm in Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} is the first sign of the variable-order structure at connection level.
__notes__.note.dark-energy.setting-successor-probl: Five, the first two the most precisely posed. (1) \emph{The forcing half beyond the diagonal class:} Assembly \claimref{dark-energy.forcing-half-schwarzschild-wall-residue-sense} with Propositions \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}-\claimref{dark-energy.wall-counterterm} and Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} answers it in the residue sense for the diagonal Kasner class with $\Lambda$ and variable exponents. Analyse the subleading momentum constraints, which select the admissible exponent fields $p_i(x)$, and the non-diagonal class, where the frame rotates as the wall is approached; this is the dynamical half of the sheaf paper's connection-level matching, and the logarithm of Lemma \claimref{dark-energy.variable-exponents-residue-pointwise-corrections-are} is where the variable-order structure enters. (2) \emph{The dual wall:} Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.walls-free-sector}'s symmetric form $M$ belongs to walls of the soldering form, metrics on tangent vectors with a radical. Decide whether such walls occur in the series' geometries (the unweighted sphere directions of the Schwarzschild interior are of this type before the sheaf paper's weights absorb them) and, where they do, whether $M$ carries a boundary mode space; the gauge generator the sheaf paper's wall opens, the ladder boost of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}(iii), is the object to compare it with. (3) \emph{Matter coupling at $\Sigma$, and the frozen point off the vacuum region:} extend the polynomial functional by matter in a form that remains defined across the locus, determine what the wall does to minimal coupling, and define the frozen point on a matter-filled region in a way that keeps it parallel, which Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(iii) needs and Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.vacuum-region-registration-condition}(ii) shows the naive scale tractor does not supply. (4) \emph{The Kerr version of the no-go:} the ring's codimension-two exceptional structure replaces the wall; the orthogonality argument needs the rotating current algebra, and the duality monodromy of the geometry paper will enter. (5) \emph{The smallness of $\Lambda$, and the promotion decision:} Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) gives the form of the action for $\Lambda \neq 0$, not a value and not smallness, and the numerical layer is the declared open problem of the matter papers. Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.under-action-written-norm-parameter-laws} places the question exactly: under the action as written $\Lambda$ indexes the theory, and ``why this $\Lambda$'' is a question within one theory only if a modification of the known class of Remark \claimref{note.dark-energy.what-clause-3-requires-what-it}, the Henneaux-Teitelboim promotion being the one used there, is adopted. Decide the promotion; if adopted, recompute the Goldstone count of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.point-infinity-has-no-physical-fluctuation} with the norm mode and its conjugate time, and name the measure over $\Lambda$ on which the Standard-Model paper's entropic and null-endpoint forces act.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-topology-tame-walls-g:
The construction's global inputs, and what obstructs them, are then exactly these:

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The side.} Always available, by Corollary \claimref{sheaf.tame-walls-are-two-sided}; the residual choice is a global sign, a torsor over $H^0(\Sig; \mathbb{Z}_2)$, fixed in the gravitational application by physics (the Lorentzian side).
\item \textbf{Orientation of the radical line.} The spanning section $k$ exists globally iff $\shL$ is trivial, iff $w_1(\shL) = 0 \in H^1(\Sig; \mathbb{Z}_2)$ (Fact \claimref{sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles}). The constructions divide over this class. The ideal sheaf and the residue are quadratic or scale-covariant in $k$, so they descend to the line bundle and need nothing. The \emph{coupling} does not descend: it is of weight $-1$ in $k$ (the transversal $u$ with $k(u) = 1$ is itself a trivialisation of $\shL^*$), so collar data, and with them the completion of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion} in the untwisted plane $\underline{\R}^2$, exist exactly when $w_1(\shL) = 0$, which is why Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} carries that standing hypothesis. For $w_1(\shL) \neq 0$, which is possible and marks walls whose dying direction is globally non-orientable, the residue theorem's conclusion that the partner line is canonically $\shL^*$ dictates the repair: the adjoined plane must be the $\shL$-twisted plane $\shL \oplus \shL^*$ rather than $\underline{\R}^2$. That twisted variant is not developed here and is recorded among the successor problems. The class $w_1(\shL)$ is a genuine invariant of the degeneration, constrained by the residue theorem to satisfy $2 w_1(\shL) = w_1(N^*\Sig) = 0$, which is no constraint mod 2.
\item \textbf{The transversal field and the collar.} Given the global $k$ of item 2, the space of pairs $(u, \beta)$ with $k(u) = 1$ is convex, hence contractible: no further obstruction, and any two choices are homotopic through admissible choices.
\item \textbf{The coupling constants.} Only the product $\mu\nu$ enters (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.only-product-coupling-constants-matters}); the good-coupling condition of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction} is an open condition $0 < |\mu\nu| < 1/(2S)$, contractible at each fixed sign of $\mu\nu$ (as a condition on the product; the set of pairs $(\mu,\nu)$ has one contractible component per sign choice of each factor). The discrete datum is the sign of $\mu\nu$, i.e.\ which side's ascent is performed: combined with item 1 this is the only genuinely binary global choice, and the two options are exchanged by relabelling the sides.
\end{enumerate}
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-schwarzschild-composi:
oindent	extbf{Conventions.} Units $G = c = 1$; to keep the arithmetic exact we write $2M = m^2$ and work in the variable $u := \sqrt{r}$, so that $ eta = m/u$ is rational in $u$. The defining function of the singular boundary is $r = u^2$; ``first order in $r$'' reads ``second order in $u$''. Signature convention $({+},{-},{-},{-})$. Throughout this section $E$ denotes the singular boundary (not the auxiliary bundle of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}); the coupling constants $\mu, 
u$ of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} always appear as the product $\mu
u$, while the angular coframe elements are the subscripted $\mu_1, \mu_2$. One conormal convention, used throughout: on $\Mt_u$ the smooth defining function of $E$ is $u$, and $dr = 2u\,du$ vanishes on $E$ as a $u$-smooth one-form; the boundary data of the tame theory are graded by $r$, so the conormal line in which the transversality datum and the residue lie is the $r$-conormal $N^*_r E := (N^*_u E)^{\otimes 2}$, spanned by the class of $dr$, matching the first-order-in-$r$ clause of (T3$\partial$).
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-transversal-independe:
The coupling of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} uses a transversal, and two questions were left open: whether the completion depends on the choice, and whether the wall admits an equivariant classical value for the dying direction at all, the no-repair theorem of \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1} being proved where the ambient form is nondegenerate and the dying direction has a hyperbolic partner. Both are settled here, at the wall, with the collar constants $\mu, 
u$ and the bump held fixed. Throughout, computations are at a point of $\Sig$ on the inner collar, where $ eta = 1$ and the Gram $G$ of the coframe module has corank one with radical $\R k$; $\alpha$ ranges over covectors, $u, v, \lambda$ over vectors, and $\alpha(v)$ is the pairing. One term is fixed before anything is compared. The \emph{completed structure} at the point is the triple $(T, h_u, k)$: the ambient module with its form and the dying direction, carrying the $\mathbb{Z}_2$-grading of its Clifford algebra and the subalgebra generated by the coframe module (the fibre of the degeneration sheaf). The named frame $(
O, 
Inf)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling} and the ladder partner $k^* = 
O/2
u$ of Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport} are choices made inside that structure, not part of it; had the frame been retained as structure, the transversal would be recoverable from it, $\alpha(u) = 2h_u(\alpha, k^*)$ for $\alpha \in T^*M$, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall} would have nothing to say. __notes__.note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-nu:
Work on an angular chart and set $C := \tfrac12\sqrt{m^2 - u^2}$, $D := -\,m u^2/(2C)$, both $u$-smooth with $C(0) = m/2$. The module $\mathcal{M}'$ with frame
\[
\alpha = du + C\,d\theta, \qquad \beta = \dtPG + D\,d\theta, \qquad \gamma = u^4\,d\theta, \qquad \mu_2
\]
is a locally free rank-four extension in the sense of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.extensions}: its Gram extends smoothly to $E$, with
\[
\begin{gathered} G(\alpha,\alpha) = G(\alpha,\beta) = 0, \qquad G(\beta,\beta) = -\,\frac{u^2}{m^2 - u^2}, \\ G(\alpha,\gamma) = -C, \qquad G(\beta,\gamma) = -D, \qquad G(\gamma,\gamma) = -u^4 , \end{gathered}
\]
all exact. At the boundary the Gram has rank three with smooth radical spanned by $\beta$ (nonvanishing eigenvalues $\pm m/2$ from the $(\alpha,\gamma)$-pair and $-1$ from $\mu_2$), so (T2$\partial$) holds; and $\det G_{\mathcal{M}'} = -\,r/4$ exactly, so the dying eigenvalue is first-order in $r$ and (T3$\partial$) holds. Yet $\mathcal{M}' \neq \shW$: neither contains the other ($\alpha \notin \shW$, its rain component $\alpha(V) = -m/2u^2$ diverging; $\rho \notin \mathcal{M}'$). The mechanism is the null mixing of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.bounded-norm-alone-does-not-characterise}, and it shows the rain-bounded hypothesis of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module} is necessary, not technical. All displayed identities are verified exactly (the section “Machine verification”).
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-smooth-structure-vari: Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data} introduced $\mathcal{A}$ by fiat, and it is natural to ask whether it is the function ring of a variable-order polyhomogeneous structure in the sense of \cite{Melrose1993}. This subsection answers the question. The answer is yes, at the cost of logarithms, and the cost is provably unavoidable: the algebra is stable under the boundary calculus in the radial direction, fails stability in the tangential directions by an exactly computable logarithmic term, and no admissible change of collar presentation removes the failure unless the exponent ratios are constant.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-exponent-collisions-e: Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data} imposes the strict ordering $p_1 < 0 < p_2 \leq p_3$. Mixmaster behaviour is precisely the failure of that ordering: along a bounce the exponents reorder. This subsection settles what a collision can be and what the wall does at one, on the Kasner constraint variety $\sum p_i = \sum p_i^2 = 1$, entirely at the algebraic level; the dynamics of an actual bounce stays with \cite{ButlerT6}.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.what-section-adds: That the family of intermediate algebras in $\Lambda$ is a tame wall at all is generic (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii)). What is specific to the cosmological constant is which objects of the dark-energy paper play the tame structure's roles: the frozen point's null direction is the radical, the Stelle-West line is the dying direction and the Stelle-West norm is the residue; the completion on both sides that the rung provides is the generic one for a family of hyperplanes and is recorded as an instance of the case the conservation theorem excludes, not as a property of $\Lambda$. None of this fixes $\Lambda$, its sign or its magnitude: the family is parametrised by $\Lambda$ and the theory describes the family.
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-machine-veri:
Every computational identity asserted in this note has been verified in exact rational arithmetic by the script \texttt{verify\_T14a.py} \cite{ButlerVerifyT14ext}, which imports the series' shared library \texttt{GA.py} and uses its basis-blade engine; no floating point anywhere. The script indexes generators from zero, so its $e_{0}, \ldots, e_{5}$ are the text's $e_{1}, \ldots, e_{6}$. Eighty-six checks, all passing, in nine parts.

\emph{Part A: the volume element.} Centrality and the sign $\omega^{2} = (-1)^{n(n-1)/2+q}$ on every diagonal signature of dimensions one, three, five and seven; the four signs of Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}; commutation of $\omega$ with the added generator; Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(iii) and the identities behind (i) and (ii), with the specific sign assignment of (i), over every odd signature of dimensions three and five; and the dimension of the centre, two over every odd signature of dimension at most five and one over every even signature of dimension at most six.

\emph{Part B: doubling and complexification.} For the two doubled extensions, the central idempotents $(1 \pm \omega)/2$, the two ideals of dimension sixteen, the action of $e_{5}$ as $+s\,\omega'$ and $-s\,\omega'$ on them with $s = e_{5}^{2}$, and the shadow meeting the even subalgebra exactly in its even part; for the two complexified extensions, the spanning of all thirty-two dimensions by $\Cl(p,q) + \omega\,\Cl(p,q)$ and $\omega^{2} = -1$ central.

\emph{Part C: where the mirror sits.} For all four extensions, the pairwise anticommutation and the squares of the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$, the generated subalgebra equal to the even subalgebra, the shadow of dimension sixteen meeting it in dimension eight, and the squares of $\omega e_{\mu}$ (reversed in the complexified cases, unchanged in the doubled ones); for $\Cl(2,3)$, the intersection equal to $\Cl^{0}(1,3)$.

\emph{Part D: the rung.} In $\Cl(2,4)$, the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(4,1)$ generated by $e_{i}e_{6}$ and $e_{i}e_{1}$, both generating the even subalgebra of dimension thirty-two; $\omega_{6}$ even, $\omega_{6}^{2} = -1$, commuting with every even element and anticommuting with every vector; the copies of $\Cl(1,3)$ and $\Cl(3,1)$ inside the even subalgebra.

\emph{Part E: the clock and the paths.} The residues of the four extensions, of the oriented pair and of the odd towers' representatives; the residue preserved by conformal completion; the centres of the four extensions of dimension two with the signs that separate the reversed pairs, and the centre of the rung of dimension one; the enumeration of sign-change walks from $(1,3)$ to $(3,1)$, exactly one, with $(0,4)$ a dead end.

\emph{Part F: the frozen point and the ascent's pair.} On exact rational instances of $I = a\,e_{+} + b\,e_{-}$ with $Q(I) = 3$, $-3$ and $0$: the orthogonality of the Lorentz frame and $w$ to $I$, $Q(w) = -Q(I)$; the signatures $(1,4)$, $(2,3)$ and $(1,3;1)$ of $I^{\perp}$ by exact congruence; $w = I$ and $I^{2} = 0$ in the null case; the opposite signs and anticommutation of $I$ and $w$; the generation of all sixty-four dimensions by $I^{\perp}$ with $I$ when $Q(I) \neq 0$; in $\Cl(1,3;1)$ the nilpotent generator, its anticommutation with the Lorentz frame, the sixteen-dimensional ideal and its vanishing square; and the signature $(1,3)$ of the Lorentz frame in all three cases.

\emph{Part G: the transport on the wall.} In the projective-to-conformal paper's model of the completion of $(1,3;1)$: the signature $(2,4)$ by exact congruence; the rank-five linear system for the image of the partner and its unique null solution $c = 0$; the norm $2ab$ of $aI + b\varphi$ on instances of both signs and zero; the invariance of the norm under rational boosts and the swap, the image staying orthogonal to the Lorentz frame; the centres of the two intermediate algebras; and the null pair $v, v^{*}$ in the root paper's normalisation, its identification with the canonical frame, and the norms $\pm\alpha\beta$ and orthogonality of $\alpha v \pm \beta v^{*}$.

\emph{Part H: the two negative results.} The canonical null frame in the rung's diagonal basis; $B = I \wedge \varphi = -e_{+}e_{-}$ with $B^{2} = 1$, commuting with the Lorentz bivectors and vectors and anticommuting with $e_{\pm}$; the rational rotor $5/4 + (3/4)B$ unit, fixing the Lorentz frame, scaling $I$ by $4$ and $\varphi$ by $1/4$, moving a frozen point along its hyperbola; the mirror's $I^{\perp}$ signatures $(4,1)$ and $(3,2)$ on the same instances; the two-by-two rule; the common presentation of $\Cl^{0}(1,4)$ and $\Cl^{0}(4,1)$; and the squares and factorisations of the bare fifth generator.

\emph{Part I: the wall in the cosmological constant.} In four dilation gauges and at seven rational values of $\Lambda$ including zero: the Gram $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1,-\Lambda/3)$ of $I_{\Lambda}^{\perp}$ and its corank at $\Lambda = 0$ only; the gauge independence of the dying eigenvalue; the exact crossing slope $-1/3$ in the parametrisation by $\Lambda$; the signatures $(2,3)$ and $(1,4)$ on the two sides; the rescaled dying entries $\pm 1/3$ and the exceptional signatures; $\Lambda\,(G^{-1})_{ww} = -3$ in every gauge with $w_{0} = a\,I_{0}$; the total signature $(2,4)$ on both sides with the complement's sign switching; the five-dimensional span at the wall and the signature of the Lorentz frame with $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$; and the general hyperplane model of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-residue-completion-both-sides}(iii) for five signatures $(p,q)$ and five values of $t$.

What the script does not check: the isomorphism types $\Mat(2,\HH)$ and $\Mat(4,\R)$ of the two oriented shadows (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-representatives-dimension-nearest-four-types}, imported; the note uses that they differ and, in Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.copy-theorems-blind-spot}, which type belongs to which tower), the frozen-point geometry (Facts \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point} and \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point-degenerate-algebras}, imported; the script checks the algebra of a vector of each norm sign in the rung, not that the parallel tractor is that vector), the algebra-map properties of Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.doubling-or-complexification}(i) and (ii) (argued in the text; the script checks the identities they rest on and the four extensions in detail), the identification of the MacDowell-Mansouri translation part with the bivectors $e_{\mu}e_{5}$ beyond the signs of their squares, the reversal of the tractor norm under $g \mapsto -g$ (Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.two-towers-one-curved-universe}(i), argued in the text; Part H checks its consequences from the reversed signature declared as input), and the transitivity of the boosts on each level set of the norm (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(iii), argued in the text; Part G checks invariance under particular boosts).
__notes__.note.odd-extensions.setting-wall-cosmolo: Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed} gives a one-parameter family of intermediate algebras, nondegenerate for $\Lambda \neq 0$ and degenerate at $\Lambda = 0$. The sheaf paper has a theory of exactly such families: tame corank-one degenerations, their exceptional algebras, the residue of the metric at the wall, and a conservation law that says the degeneracy of a wall in spacetime can be displaced but never destroyed. This section runs that theory on the $\Lambda$ line. The family is a tame wall in the sheaf paper's sense, and the rung completes it on both sides, which the conservation law forbids for the completions it covers; the family lies in the case the conservation theorem's proof excludes by hypothesis, a complement whose signature switches across the wall, and that case is generic to any corank-one family of hyperplanes in a fixed nondegenerate space. The section's content is the identification of the dark-energy paper's frozen-point geometry with the sheaf paper's tame structure, and the placement of the $\Lambda$ family in that excluded case.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-blow-up-weighted-modu:
On the flat background of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric} the singular locus of $\hb$ is the worldline $\ell = \{r = 0\}$, of codimension three. Let $\Mt$ denote the real oriented blow-up of the background along $\ell$: concretely, $\Mt = \R_t \times [0,\infty)_r \times S^2$, with boundary
\[
E \;=\; \{r = 0\} \;\cong\; \R \times S^2 ,
\]
which is a \emph{hypersurface}: codimension one in $\Mt$. Polar coordinates realise the blow-up; nothing more sophisticated is needed. Each point of the worldline has been replaced by the sphere of normal directions, exactly as the section “Scope, and successor problems” prescribes.

On $\Mt$ the cometric does not extend to $E$ in the coordinate coframe: some components vanish and others diverge, at different rates, which is the anisotropy problem restated. The resolution is to change not the geometry but the \emph{module of coframes} in which the geometry is expressed. The construction, a rescaled bundle at a boundary, is standard in boundary index theory \cite{Melrose1993}; what is particular here is that the metric itself characterises the rescaling.
__notes__.note.sheaf.bounded-norm-alone-does-not-c:
It is tempting to define $\shW$ as the module generated by \emph{all} one-forms of bounded $G$-norm. That definition collapses: the form
\[
\alpha \;=\; du + \tfrac12\sqrt{m^2 - u^2}\; d\theta
\]
is $u$-smooth with $G(\alpha, \alpha) = G(du,du) + \tfrac14 (m^2 - u^2)\, G(d\theta,d\theta) = \frac{m^2 - u^2}{4u^4} - \frac{m^2-u^2}{4u^4} = 0$ \emph{exactly}: a null mixing of a divergent radial component against a divergent angular one. Both $\alpha$ and its partner with the opposite angular sign have bounded (indeed zero) norm, so the module they generate contains their difference and sum, hence $d\theta$ and $du$ separately, hence every one-form: the bounded-norm module is the full cotangent module, whose Gram does not extend to $E$. Boundedness must therefore be demanded of \emph{components} against a fixed nondegenerate frame, which is what the rain characterisation of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.basic-properties-operational-characterisation} does, and what the uniqueness theorem of the section “Uniqueness of the weighted module” must and does assume. The same phenomenon reappears there as an explicit second boundary-tame extension (Example \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension}).
__notes__.note.sheaf.what-weights-are: In proper time $\tau_{\mathrm{p}} \propto r^{3/2}$ the frame of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.basic-properties-operational-characterisation} reads: $\rho \propto d\tau_{\mathrm{p}}$ at $E$ (weight $0$), the angular generators carry weight $\tau_{\mathrm{p}}^{2/3}$, and the dying generator (below) rescales by $\tau_{\mathrm{p}}^{-1/3}$ in the exceptional regime. These are the Kasner exponents of Fact \claimref{sheaf.kasner-data-interior}; their uniqueness is Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}. The angular weights are exactly the blow-up's tautological rescaling: the normal sphere at parameter $r$ has radius $r$, so the unit-sphere coframe is $r\,d\theta$, $r\sin\theta\,d\phi$. This is the sense in which the blow-up absorbs the angular anisotropy: those two rates were never Kasner data, they were the exceptional divisor's own geometry.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-uniqueness-weighted-m: Proposition \claimref{sheaf.basic-properties-operational-characterisation} characterised $\shW$ operationally and fixed the quasihomogeneous order as the minimal one admitting a smooth frame. What it left open is whether some \emph{other} locally free extension of the interior cotangent module could carry a boundary-tame structure of its own. Within the rain-bounded class the answer is no, and the proof is short. Two explicit examples delimit the theorem exactly: first-order vanishing must be read on the dying eigenvalue, not the dying entry (Example \claimref{note.sheaf.eigenvalue-essential}), and the rain-bounded hypothesis cannot be dropped, because null mixing produces genuinely different boundary-tame extensions outside it (Example \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension}).
__notes__.note.sheaf.kinematic-status-module: At the singular boundary the raw cotangent module is not a carrier: it admits no bounded extension across $E$ (the order-one structure fails the minimality clause of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.basic-properties-operational-characterisation}), and by Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module} the rain-bounded boundary-tame extension is unique. The positive identification is two-tier: what the infalling observer measures finitely is exactly the exceptional module, the nondegenerate rain-dual carrier; its $u$-smooth shadow is $\shW$, the tame carrier of the degeneration sheaf; and the chain's own radial dyad lies in the former with constant unit components. The exceptional algebra of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-black-hole} is, literally, the Clifford algebra of what the rain measures. What remains interpretive is confined to the operator and state level of \cite{ButlerT5}'s chain, and is recorded in the section “Consequences, and what remains open”.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-anisotropic-class-var: The Schwarzschild composite used constant Kasner exponents. The general velocity-dominated case has exponents varying over the singular surface. This section closes the algebraic half of that problem. The principle that makes it tractable is worth stating once: \emph{every tame-wall construction of this paper is $C^\infty$-linear}. The degeneration sheaf, the ideal, the coupling, the completion, the ladder pair, the exceptional rescaling: every construction is algebra-linear in the coefficient functions and never differentiates them. Position-dependent exponents therefore affect only the \emph{function algebra} over which the module is defined, never the constructions performed over it.
__notes__.note.sheaf.eigenvalue-essential:
Fix $c \neq 0$ and let $\mathcal{M}_c \subset \shW$ be generated by $(u\rho,\ k + c\rho,\ \mu_1,\ \mu_2)$, with $k = \rho + m\,\dtPG$ the radical section. Then $\mathcal{M}_c$ is a strict submodule (its boundary evaluation has rank three), it satisfies (T2$\partial$), and its dying \emph{entry} is
\[
G(u\rho,\,u\rho) \;=\; r\,(m^2 - r) :
\]
first order in $r$, with nonvanishing coefficient. Nevertheless its dying \emph{eigenvalue} is second order: $\det A = mu$, so $\det G_{\mathcal{M}_c} = -m^2 r^2$ exactly, while the nonvanishing $3\times 3$ minor at the boundary equals $c^2 m^2 \neq 0$: the off-diagonal entries of order $u$ reduce the first-order diagonal entry to a second-order eigenvalue. So $\mathcal{M}_c$ is corank one with a first-order dying entry and is \emph{not} $\shW$: the entry formulation of (T3$\partial$) would make Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module} false, and the eigenvalue formulation is the correct one. All displayed identities are verified exactly (the section “Machine verification”).
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-contribution:
The paper proves eight clusters of results, at the standard of \cite{ButlerT1} (Tier A of the series: complete proofs, each theorem carrying its own hypotheses).

\begin{enumerate}
\item \textbf{The degeneration sheaf} (the section “The degeneration sheaf”). For a cometric of corank one along a tame hypersurface, the Clifford sheaf $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$ is locally free of constant rank $2^n$ (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank}, valid for arbitrary degeneracy); over the degenerate locus each fibre carries the canonical square-zero two-sided ideal generated by the radical line, with quotient the Clifford algebra of the induced nondegenerate form, and these ideals assemble into a coherent sheaf supported exactly on $\Sig$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}). Resolution is characterised ideal-theoretically: in any fibrewise nondegenerate Clifford completion the radical generates the \emph{unit} ideal (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}); completion turns an infinitesimal into a dimension. The proof given needs no simplicity hypothesis, the hyperbolic partner exhibiting the unit directly, so the statement holds in the split signatures as well.
\item \textbf{One-sided completion} (the section “The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion”). For walls with trivial radical line bundle (the twisted case is posed as a successor problem), a rank-$(n{+}2)$ ambient bundle with a coupled form $h$, equal to $G \perp H$ outside a collar of $\Sig$, is nondegenerate of constant signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ on the closed physical side; the subalgebra generated by $T^*M$ is canonically the degeneration sheaf, globally; and the localised ladder pair exists exactly over $\Sig$.
\item \textbf{The shadow wall} (the section “The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy”). Conservation of degeneracy in two forms. Absolute: \emph{no} completion whatever that is standard outside a neighbourhood of the wall is nondegenerate everywhere, by a pure signature obstruction (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}), which is stronger than any ansatz-level statement. Located: within the coupling ansatz the degeneration lies exactly on the zero set of the determinant factor $F$, displaced to the unphysical side, with the signature passing from $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ to $(p,q{+}2)$; for good couplings the shadow wall is itself tame and the infinite wall sequence iterates unconditionally (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction}, Corollary \claimref{sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence}). The cohomological wall-class question, and its relation to the conservation conjecture of \cite[\S7.4]{ButlerT1}, is posed precisely.
\item \textbf{The exceptional algebra and the residue} (the section “The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue”). The $\sqrt{t}$-rescaled Clifford family through a tame wall converges to a nondegenerate special fibre built from normal-cone data, independent of all choices up to canonical isomorphism; the inverse cometric has a canonical simple pole at the wall whose residue is exactly the inverse of the invariant transversality datum of (T3), identifying $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$: the dying line is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle, the partner line of the normal bundle. The identification fixes the direction of the twist (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.direction-induced-twist}).
\item \textbf{Topology, dictionary and scope} (the section “Dictionary, choices, and scope”). A topological corollary of the residue theorem: tame walls are always two-sided, since $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ makes the normal bundle's $w_1$ zero; the construction's global choices are itemised with their exact obstruction classes ($w_1(\shL)$ the only genuine invariant); the wall class is posed as a precise conjecture whose coarse half Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form} already proves; and the relation to tractor bundles and the Fefferman-Graham ambient metric is developed at assembly level and flagged as such, with the anisotropic, higher-codimension and BKL-weight questions stated as successor problems, the first instance of which the next item executes.
\item \textbf{The Schwarzschild composite} (the section “The Schwarzschild composite”). The two failure modes that keep the Schwarzschild singularity outside the tame class, codimension three and anisotropy, are cleared together for the exact solution: the real oriented blow-up of the worldline absorbs the angular rates tautologically, and on a canonically weighted coframe module the residual degeneration is boundary-tame of corank one, with the Killing-time direction as its radical (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}). The one-sided completion then ascends $\Cl(1,3) \to \Cl(2,4)$ on the whole blown-up manifold with the ladder pair supported exactly on the singular boundary and no shadow wall (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion-singularity}); the weights that achieve this are forced, once the geometrically determined dying direction is named, and equal the Kasner exponents (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}), settling the Kasner-weights conjecture for Schwarzschild in the diagonal class.
\item \textbf{Uniqueness, the rain frame, the matching, and the anisotropic class} (the section “Uniqueness of the weighted module”-the section “The matching with the weighted limit”, the section “The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability”). The weighted module is the \emph{unique} rain-bounded locally free extension of the interior cotangent module that is boundary tame, by a determinant argument whose hypothesis must be read on the dying eigenvalue, not the dying entry, and whose anchoring class cannot be dropped: two explicit modules separate the readings (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module}, Examples \claimref{note.sheaf.eigenvalue-essential} and \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension}). Physically, the exceptional coframe is exactly the dual coframe of the infalling orthonormal frame, with exact Minkowski Gram at every radius, and the gauge field carries the flat radial null dyad onto a physical dyad with constant unit components in it (Propositions \claimref{sheaf.rain-duality}, \claimref{sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite}): the weighted module is the $u$-smooth shadow of what the falling observer measures finitely. The weighted limit of \cite{ButlerT6} is then matched to the present construction, at the fibre and at the connection level: its adapted frame consists of exceptional-module sections, its rates are re-derived here exactly, its limit is the weight one-form of the exceptional bundle, and its surviving matrix is a unit boost precisely by the second Kasner relation (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.matching-fibre}, Theorem \claimref{sheaf.matching-connection-level}). Finally the whole package extends to position-dependent Kasner exponents, over a variable-order function algebra, stably under the relative error structure that velocity-dominated asymptotics deliver, with sharpness exhibited at relative order zero (Theorems \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced}, \claimref{sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagonal-case}); the smooth structure of that algebra is characterised exactly, variable-order polyhomogeneous with unavoidable logarithms measured by the derivative of the exponents (Theorems \claimref{sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-conormality}, \claimref{sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant}); and the mixmaster boundary is closed at the algebraic level by the collision dichotomy: positive-pair collisions pass through the Schwarzschild triple and are interior to the theory, while ordering changes force Taub edges on which the wall ends and across which no weighted module continues (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.edge-wall}, Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.mixmaster-wall-complex}).
\item \textbf{Transversal independence, and the no-value theorem at the wall} (the section “Transversal independence, and the no-value theorem at the wall”). The coupling uses a transversal, and the dependence is resolved exactly: a closed-form unipotent intertwiner identifies the completions built on any two transversals, the identifications compose (a cocycle), and the completion at the wall is canonically transversal-independent, preserving the form, the grading and the degeneration subalgebra though neither the frame nor the ladder pair (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.transversal-independence-wall}). On the same mechanism, the wall admits no equivariant classical value for the dying direction and no canonical ladder partner: the automorphisms of the completed structure translate the candidates freely (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall}), so an analogue of the root paper's no-repair theorem holds at the wall itself, where that theorem's hypotheses fail. This is the boundary no-go the singularity paper imports verbatim.
\end{enumerate}
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-shadow-wall-conservat: The one-sided completion is one-sided by necessity, and the necessity has two layers. The first is absolute: a pure signature obstruction that rules out \emph{every} completion agreeing with the standard form away from the wall, whatever its construction. The second is quantitative: within the coupling ansatz, the determinant factor $F$ of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.only-product-coupling-constants-matters} locates the displaced degeneration exactly, and for good couplings the displaced wall is itself tame, so the construction applies to its own output.
__notes__.note.sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-bound:
Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form} forbids completions nondegenerate on \emph{both} sides of an interior wall; at a boundary there is one side, the theorem's hypothesis fails, and the completion closes with no residue. The degeneracy has not been removed; it has been displaced out of the manifold: the would-be shadow wall is at $r < 0$. There is a sharper way to see that the conservation principle survives with its boundary at exactly the right place. Take the coupling \emph{global}: bump $\equiv 1$ everywhere and $\mu\nu = -\tfrac{m^2}{2}$ (at $2M = 1$, the value $-\tfrac12$). Then, exactly,
\[
\det h \;=\; m^2 \quad \text{at every radius,}
\]
and $h$ has signature $(2,4)$ from the deep interior through the horizon to the far exterior: a \emph{globally} nondegenerate completion of the Schwarzschild degeneration, with constant determinant. This does not contradict Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}, because that theorem only forbids completions that are \emph{standard outside a neighbourhood of the wall}, and this one is not: its coupling never switches off, so it fails standardness at infinity. The example exhibits the conservation theorem's hypothesis as exactly sharp: give up standardness at infinity and the obstruction moves to infinity; keep standardness and, at an interior wall, it moves to the shadow wall; at a boundary wall, it moves out of the manifold. Degeneracy is moved, never destroyed, in all three regimes.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-consequences-what-rem:
\emph{The localisation import of the singularity paper.} The singularity paper \cite{ButlerT5} imports this paper's localisation for a case that failed the tame hypotheses. For exact Schwarzschild this section supplies the missing structure: the ascent and the ladder pair are theorem-backed \emph{at the black hole}, localised on $E \cong \R \times S^2$, in the boundary-tame weighted sense defined here. Separately, the corank ambiguity behind the count of boundary modes at the singularity (corank $1$, $2$ or $3$ depending on rescaling weight) is resolved structurally: with the weights of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}, forced once the dying direction is read off the geometry, the corank is exactly one, so there is one ladder pair per point of $E$, not one per dying coordinate direction. What this section does \emph{not} do is compute the quantitative content of the boundary mode space: the epoch and count analysis belongs to \cite{ButlerT8}, and the aggregation over the sphere factor of $E$ is exactly the slice-to-epoch question assigned to that paper.

\emph{The conservation principle.} The constant-determinant global completion of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-boundary-sharp-example} is the first explicit example exhibiting the sharpness of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-form}'s standardness hypothesis, and the boundary case completes the trichotomy: interior wall, shadow wall; boundary wall, no wall; non-standard completion, wall at infinity.

\emph{What remains open.} Four problems, at the boundary of what this paper's methods reach. \textbf{The analysis of the anisotropic class}: the section “The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability” closes the diagonal class at the algebraic level, position-dependent exponents included, stably under relatively admissible errors, with the smooth structure of the function algebra characterised in the section “The smooth structure of the variable-order algebra” and the collision boundary settled in the section “Exponent collisions and the edge of the wall”; what it does not supply is analysis: the dictionary identifying the connection-level admissibility of \cite{ButlerT6} with Gram-level relative admissibility for genuine velocity-dominated solutions, and the dynamical traversal of the Taub edges, the bounce and era maps themselves, both of which lie in \cite{ButlerT6}'s admissibility class. \textbf{Kerr}: the ring has codimension two and, unlike every case treated here, a lightlike dying direction (see the section “Scope, and successor problems”); the Kerr composite, on a twisted variable-order module over a focal double cover, is the genuine successor problem, and its geometry is assigned to \cite{ButlerT6}. \textbf{The operator and state level}: the section “The rain frame: the physical meaning of the module” answers the kinematic question of what $\shW$ is, the $u$-smooth shadow of what the infalling observer measures finitely; whether the fermionic modes and modular structures of the boundary mode space of \cite{ButlerT5}'s chain, built on the dyad shown there to be rain-finite, define states on the completion at the wall is a question for \cite{ButlerT5}'s framework. \textbf{The variable-exponent weighted limit}: the section “The matching with the weighted limit” matches the weighted limit of \cite{ButlerT6} to the present construction at the fibre and at the connection level; extending the matching to position-dependent exponents is the question posed precisely in Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.what-remains-matching}.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-degeneration-sheaf: This section proves the first cluster: over the degenerate locus, the constant-rank sheaf $\shA$ keeps its constant rank only by becoming non-reduced, and the non-reducedness is canonical.
__notes__.note.sheaf.non-reducedness-singularity-r: The interpretation deserves emphasis, because it is the central idea of the paper. In algebraic geometry, the special fibre of a degenerating family typically acquires nilpotents: the scheme becomes non-reduced, and the nilpotents record infinitesimal directions that no longer correspond to actual points \cite[Ch.~II]{Hartshorne1977}. Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf} exhibits the same phenomenon literally rather than by analogy: the direction along which the metric degenerated survives in the singular fibre only as an infinitesimal, an element all of whose products through the entire algebra square to zero. And $\shJ$ is the direct analogue of the object a blow-up is performed along: a canonical sheaf of ideals supported on the singular locus \cite[\S II.7]{Hartshorne1977}, transcribed from the structure sheaf to the Clifford sheaf. The ideal-theoretic characterisation of what resolution must accomplish is available in one line, and is the next proposition.
__notes__.note.sheaf.fibre-over-null-generator-thi: The structure $(A(x), J(x))$ over the wall is precisely the pattern classified in \cite[Thm.~5.7(2)]{ButlerT1}: a Clifford algebra containing a square-zero two-sided ideal generated by a null generator, with quotient the Clifford algebra of the nondegenerate part. There it arose as the degenerate one-generator ascent, the completion candidate that \emph{never fuses}; here it arises as the special fibre of a geometric family. The two occurrences are one phenomenon: an infinitesimal thickening of a nondegenerate algebra, in which division is impossible, whose repair requires genuinely new pairing rather than more nilpotence. That paper's fibre-level conclusion (the null ascent resolves nothing) is exactly why the ambient sheaf of the section “The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion” must couple the dying direction to the adjoined plane instead of merely adjoining it.
__notes__.note.sheaf.boundary-tameness-stated: Define a \emph{boundary-tame corank-one degeneration} as a pair $(\shW, G)$ on a manifold with boundary $E$ satisfying: (T1$\partial$) $E$ is a smooth boundary hypersurface; (T2$\partial$) $G$ extends smoothly to $E$ with corank exactly one and smooth radical line; (T3$\partial$) the dying eigenvalue vanishes to exactly first order in a defining function. Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame} says Schwarzschild, blown up and weighted, is boundary-tame. The adaptations of this paper's tame-wall results are minor and are itemised here. The fibrewise results (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}, Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}, Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-normal-cone}, Theorem \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist}) use only the form and its one-sided limit and go through in the bundle-valued sense of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.setup-generalises-arbitrary-bundles} applied to $(\shW, G)$, with one convention mirrored: here the dying eigenvalue is \emph{negative} on the physical side ($g_k = -r$), so the quotient signature is $(p, q{-}1)$ rather than $(p{-}1, q)$ and the completion's coupling sign is the opposite branch of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.only-product-coupling-constants-matters}; Proposition \claimref{sheaf.wall-fibre-black-hole} and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion-singularity} carry the mirrored statements. The completion (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion}) used three regions, wall, collar physical side, exterior, all of which exist here, and never used the far side to prove nondegeneracy on the physical closure. Only the shadow-wall analysis of the section “The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy” genuinely concerns the far side, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.one-sided-completion-singularity} records what happens to it. The sign-crossing clause of (T3), meaningless at a boundary, is replaced by the first-order clause (T3$\partial$).

__notes__.note.sheaf.scope-what-discharges: The statements are pointwise on $\Sig$, every formula rational in the collar data and hence smooth in the point, so they hold over every open piece of the wall; the collar constants and bump are held fixed, their variation being the rescaling of the section “Dictionary, choices, and scope”. Off the wall the two ambient forms $h_u$ and $h_{u+v}$ need not be isometric, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.transversal-independence-wall} does not say they are: by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}, $\det h = \det G \cdot (-(1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s))$ with $s = G^{-1}(e,e)$ depending on the transversal, so the shadow wall of the section “The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy” moves with the transversal, and on a far-side collar point one form can be degenerate while the other is not, or both nondegenerate with different signatures (the script exhibits both, on the model data $G = \operatorname{diag}(\lambda, 1, -1, -1)$ with $\mu\nu = 1$). The transversal independence proved here is a statement at the wall, and nothing off the wall is needed: the value question is a question at the wall. What Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall} discharges downstream is the boundary case that the singularity paper recorded as open in the scope of its no-repair import \cite{ButlerT5}: with the theorem in place, no classical value repairs the dying direction on the approach or at the boundary itself.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-exponent-collisions-e: The first census triple is the Schwarzschild triple of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.weights-are-forced-are-kasner-exponents}; the second is the Taub triple, whose Kasner metric is classically flat space under another name \cite{Kasner1921}. The dichotomy theorem says the two collisions behave entirely differently.
__notes__.note.sheaf.mixmaster-wall-complex: In a family whose exponents traverse the constraint variety with ordering changes, the degeneration locus over $E$ is a \emph{wall complex}: open walls labelled by their dying axis, each carrying its own forced weighted module, tame in the sense of this paper, glued along Taub edges where the structure is momentarily nondegenerate and no module continues across. The transverse wall sequence of the section “The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy” and the tangential edge structure are independent mechanisms, and the method for degenerations with ordering changes is the pair of them.
__notes__.note.sheaf.what-stays-interior-paper: The traversal itself, which bounces occur, in which order, and visiting which edges, is dynamics: the Kasner map and its era structure lie outside \cite{ButlerT6}'s admissibility class, whose integral diverges on the oscillatory approach, and belong to its billiard-invariant successor problem; the section “Consequences, and what remains open” records it among the open problems. What this subsection settles is that wherever a flow makes the ordering change, the sheaf-level geometry is as above: the dichotomy, the forced Taub edge, the ending wall, the jumping module. It also yields one unexpected quantitative fact: among all Kasner composites the Schwarzschild triple \emph{maximises} the dying order, so the composite of the section “The Schwarzschild composite” is not merely an example but the interior maximum of tameness in its class, farthest from both collision walls.
__notes__.note.sheaf.what-section-does-does-not-cl: Together, Theorems \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} and \claimref{sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagonal-case} close the sheaf-theoretic half of the anisotropic successor problem for the full relatively admissible diagonal class; for exact Schwarzschild the Gram errors against the frozen Kasner model are $O(r)$ relative (Fact \claimref{sheaf.weighted-limit}'s rates), well inside it. Uniqueness transfers in the qualified form of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.uniqueness-weighted-module}: within a fixed variable-order structure, the determinant argument (with $r$ replaced by the canonical defining element) shows the weighted module contains no second boundary-tame extension; an analogue of the rain-frame anchoring class is not pursued here, and Example \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension}'s mechanism is available in the variable-order setting too. the section “The smooth structure of the variable-order algebra” and the section “Exponent collisions and the edge of the wall” complete the algebraic side: the smooth structure of $\mathcal{A}$ (answered, with unavoidable logarithms) and the mixmaster boundary (the collision dichotomy and the edge of the wall). What is deliberately not claimed is recorded in the section “Consequences, and what remains open”, and it is analysis alone: the dictionary with \cite{ButlerT6}'s admissibility for genuine solutions, and the dynamical traversal of the edges.
__notes__.note.sheaf.blow-up-dictionary: Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-normal-cone} is the deformation to the normal cone \cite[Ch.~5]{Fulton1998} transcribed into Clifford algebra: the exceptional algebra over $x \in \Sig$ is built from the surviving tangential form together with the normal derivative of the degeneration, normal-cone data alone, exactly as the exceptional divisor of a blow-up replaces each point of the centre by its normal directions. The substitution $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$ is the blow-up chart; the ambient description of the section “The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion” and the rescaled description here are its two standard charts; and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist} identifies the tautological bundle of the correspondence: not $\shL^* \otimes N^*\Sig$ but the square-root identity. Since $\shL^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sig$ says that $k$ carries the weight of a half-power of a defining function, the rescaling is exactly the normalisation of a conormal square root by the inverse square root of the defining function: the adjoined dimension is constructed tautologically from the dying direction and the geometry of its degeneration.
__notes__.note.sheaf.answer-smooth-structure-quest: Assembled: $\mathcal{A}^{\log}$ is the variable-order polyhomogeneous ring, and $\mathcal{A}$ is its log-degree-zero part. The logarithms measure tangential differentiation of the exponents, vanish identically exactly in the locally constant case, where the ring is Melrose's \cite{Melrose1993}, and cannot be transformed away unless the exponent ratios are constant. Note where the question matters: the constructions of this paper are $C^\infty$-linear and never differentiate a coefficient, which is why the section “The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability” through the section “Stability under relatively admissible errors” needed only $\mathcal{A}$; the smooth structure matters exactly when one starts to differentiate, that is, at the connection level, which is the half of the anisotropic programme assigned to \cite{ButlerT6} (the section “Consequences, and what remains open”).
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-exponent-collisions-e: The principle stated at the head of this section, that the tame constructions are $C^\infty$-linear, is used by the singularity paper \cite{ButlerT5} as an input to a theorem, so it is given a number and a proof here.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-position-series: This paper is T4 of the series. It uses two predecessors and supplies four successors. It uses the language and fibre computations of the primer T0 \cite{ButlerT0} and the fibre theory of the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1}: the Witt completion, the zero-divisor taxonomy with its transport rules, and the minimality theorem, all used here one fibre at a time. It supplies, downstream: the localised transport (Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport}) is the structure the singularity paper T5 \cite{ButlerT5} imports when it applies the transport principle at the black hole, and the section “The Schwarzschild composite” extends that import from tame walls to the Schwarzschild boundary itself; the wall package of the section “The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion” and the section “The shadow wall: conservation of degeneracy” is what the iteration corollary of the tower paper T3 \cite{ButlerT3} climbs; the support statement, that the ladder pair is supported exactly on the singular locus, is the geometric input behind the no-attic and no-echo arguments of the entropy paper T8 \cite{ButlerT8}; and the tractor-level route to the same singularity, reached here at sheaf level, is the subject of the interior paper T6 \cite{ButlerT6}, whose weighted limit the section “The matching with the weighted limit” identifies as a connection on this paper's exceptional bundle, and whose admissibility class is assigned the analytic half of the anisotropic theory that the section “The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability” closes at the algebraic level. Two further exports go to the singularity paper alone: the no-value theorem at the wall (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall}), which it reproduces verbatim as its boundary no-go, and the function-linearity principle (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructions}), the class-membership input of its hopping exclusion \cite[Facts B.3, B.4]{ButlerT5}.
__notes__.note.sheaf.wall-class-posed: Degeneracy is conserved: it can be pushed off the physical region, never annihilated globally. This is the first geometric instance of the conservation principle conjectured at the fibre level in \cite[Conj.~7.9]{ButlerT1} (obstructions are moved, never destroyed), and the sharpest open question this paper poses is its measure: to construct a cohomological invariant on $\Sig$, presumably a relative class built from the mod-8 residues of the two competing ascents on the two sides of the wall, whose nonvanishing forces the shadow wall's existence, and whose behaviour under the iteration of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction} advances the clock of \cite[\S7]{ButlerT1}. The precise formulation is given in the section “Dictionary, choices, and scope” among the successor problems.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-objects-2: Hypothesis (T3) is usually stated in coordinates: the dying eigenvalue $\lambda$ of $G$ (with respect to any auxiliary frame metric) crosses zero at nonzero speed along any transversal to $\Sig$. The following lemma packages the condition invariantly, without an auxiliary metric, and identifies the natural bundle in which the crossing speed lies; the identification is used again later, since the residue theorem of the section “The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue” is its inverse.
__notes__.note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed: In a local frame $(k, m_1, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of $T^*M$ along a transversal with parameter $\tau$, write the Gram matrix $G(\tau) = \begin{psmallmatrix} \lambda(\tau) & b(\tau)^{\mathsf T} \\ b(\tau) & G_1(\tau)\end{psmallmatrix}$ with $\lambda(0) = 0$, $b(0) = 0$ and $G_1(0)$ invertible (all because $k$ spans the radical at $\tau = 0$). Then $\delta(k \otimes k) = \lambda'(0)\, d\tau$, and (T3) reads $\lambda'(0) \neq 0$. Since a transversal derivative that is nonzero forces a sign change, the signatures on the two sides of $\Sig$ differ by one unit: $(p,q)$ on the side where $\lambda > 0$ against $(p{-}1, q{+}1)$ on the other. We fix notation once: $\Mp$ denotes the closure of the side on which $\lambda > 0$, the \emph{physical side} in the gravitational application, where the signature of $G$ is $(p, q)$ with $p \geq 1$; $\Mo := M \setminus \Sig$.
__notes__.note.sheaf.scope-tame-class: Tame degenerations include signature-change walls and the conformally regularised cosmological boundaries central to conformal cyclic cosmology \cite{Penrose2010}. Two important degenerations are \emph{not} tame, and the boundary of the class is a result rather than a caveat: the Schwarzschild singularity has a locus of codimension three (a worldline), so hypersurface methods apply only after a geometric blow-up of the worldline, and its degeneration is anisotropic, different directions degenerating at different rates, so the single rescaling of the section “The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue” must be replaced by direction-dependent weights. Both obstacles are cleared, for the exact Schwarzschild solution, in the section “The Schwarzschild composite”, where the composite of the two repairs is executed and the weights are shown to be forced and equal to the Kasner exponents; the section “The anisotropic class: variable weights and stability” then closes the diagonal anisotropic class at the algebraic level, with position-dependent exponents and stability under the relative errors of velocity-dominated asymptotics, the remaining analysis being assigned to the weighted-limit paper \cite{ButlerT6}.
__notes__.note.sheaf.dimension-signature-generalit: The gravitational application needs this material only for $4$-manifolds of Lorentzian signature. __notes__.note.sheaf.abstract: Let $M$ be a smooth manifold with a cometric $G$ on $T^*M$, degenerating tamely to corank one on a hypersurface $\Sig$. The Clifford sheaf of the pair meets an apparent contradiction: locally free fibre dimension cannot jump, yet the series' transport principle demands $\Cl(p,q)$ off $\Sig$ and $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ over it. The jump goes into structure, twice over. The degeneration sheaf has constant rank $2^n$; over $\Sig$ its fibres acquire a canonical square-zero ideal, generated by the radical line, that any nondegenerate completion converts into the unit ideal. The ambient sheaf has constant rank $2^{n+2}$ and signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ on the closed physical side; what fails on $\Sig$ is a splitting, the adjoined ladder pair supported exactly there. A conservation law follows: no completion standard off the wall is nondegenerate on both sides; the degeneracy reappears on a displaced shadow wall, tame for good couplings, and the construction iterates. The normal cone carries an exceptional algebra, and the metric's residue makes the dying line a canonical square root of the conormal bundle. The completion is canonically independent of the collar transversal, yet the wall admits no equivariant value and no canonical ladder partner: the no-repair theorem's analogue at the wall itself. Blown up and Kasner-weighted, the Schwarzschild singularity becomes a boundary-tame wall receiving the same completion, no shadow wall, the weights forced to the Kasner exponents; the weighted module is the unique rain-bounded boundary-tame extension, and the theory extends, stably, to position-dependent exponents. Complete proofs; imports stated as facts with provenance.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-introduction:
The root paper of this series operates at a single fibre. Given a real quadratic space of mixed signature, the null vectors of its Clifford algebra admit no equivariant element-level repair in any extension, while the space of points is repaired totally and uniquely by the Witt completion $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$; the full taxonomy of zero-divisor obstructions, with the transport rule and minimality theorem belonging to each type, is settled in the same paper \cite{ButlerT1}. It treats one algebra at a time.

Geometry does not. In the gravitational application that motivates the series, the metric degenerates on a \emph{locus} $\Sig$ inside a manifold $M$: the algebra that needs completion is over $\Sig$, while the algebra away from $\Sig$ is nondegenerate and must be left unchanged. The natural demand is therefore a sheaf of Clifford algebras whose fibre is $\Cl(p,q)$ on the nondegenerate region and $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ over $\Sig$. Stated naively this is impossible, and the impossibility is instructive: $\Cl(p,q)$ has dimension $2^n$ and $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ has dimension $2^{n+2}$ (sixteen against sixty-four in the spacetime case), and the rank of a locally free sheaf is locally constant. The fibre dimension cannot jump. The subject of this paper is the resolution of that tension: the jump must be relocated into \emph{structure}, and there are exactly two natural places for it to go.

The first is a sheaf of constant rank $2^n$, the \emph{degeneration sheaf}: the Clifford sheaf of the degenerate cometric itself. Its fibres over $\Sig$ remain $2^n$-dimensional but degenerate as algebras, acquiring a canonical two-sided ideal that squares to zero. The singular locus registers as non-reducedness, in precise parallel with the appearance of nilpotents in the special fibres of algebraic-geometric degenerations, and the ideal is exactly the kind of object a blow-up is performed along: a canonical sheaf of ideals supported on the singular locus. The second is a sheaf of constant rank $2^{n+2}$, the \emph{ambient sheaf}, whose fibre is $\Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ at every point of the closed physical region; the metric-level description survives inside it as a distinguished subalgebra attached to a splitting, and on $\Sig$ it is the splitting, not the sheaf, that fails. Nothing jumps in the completion. The two sheaves are related by a global embedding, and the embedding is the localised transport.

Two further phenomena complete the picture, and both are theorems rather than constructions. First, a conservation law: the one-sided completion cannot be two-sided; no completion that is standard away from the wall is nondegenerate on both sides. The ambient form necessarily degenerates on a displaced hypersurface on the unphysical side, a \emph{shadow wall}, which for good couplings is itself a tame degeneration, so the completion iterates along an infinite wall sequence; degeneracy is moved, never destroyed. Second, an exceptional fibre: the anisotropic rescaling of the dying direction by $\sqrt{t}$ realises, fibrewise over $\Sig$, the deformation to the normal cone of algebraic geometry, and its special fibre is a genuine nondegenerate Clifford algebra whose metric in the dying direction is the \emph{rate} of the degeneration. The residue theorem then identifies the twist: the physical metric has a canonical simple pole at the wall, its residue induces an isomorphism $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ with $\shL$ the radical line bundle, so the dying line is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle and the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, canonically $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the normal bundle. The new dimension is not adjoined arbitrarily; it is constructed tautologically from the dying direction and the geometry of its degeneration.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-prior-art: Ambient constructions over conformal and degenerate structures have a substantial history, and this paper's ambient sheaf is a degenerate-locus-adapted relative of two of them. \emph{Tractor calculus}, going back to Thomas and formalised by Bailey, Eastwood and Gover \cite{BEG1994} with a modern treatment by Curry and Gover \cite{CurryGover2018}, packages a conformal manifold into a rank-$(n{+}2)$ bundle of signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ with canonical connection; its almost-Einstein and boundary variants are the closest existing geometry to the completion of the section “The ambient sheaf: one-sided completion”. The \emph{Fefferman-Graham ambient metric} \cite{FG1985, FG2012} realises the same increment $(+1,+1)$ as a nondegenerate metric on a thickened cone. The precise dictionary between those constructions and the present one is assembly-level material and is developed in the section “Dictionary, choices, and scope”, per the series' practice of keeping the points of contact with existing structures in the text. The algebraic input, the Clifford algebra of a \emph{degenerate} symmetric form with its $2^n$-dimensional blade basis, is due to Chevalley \cite{Chevalley1997}; the structure theory of the nondegenerate fibres is classical \cite{Porteous1995, Lounesto2001, Lam2005}. On the geometric side, the blow-up along an ideal sheaf and the non-reducedness of special fibres are standard algebraic geometry \cite{Hartshorne1977}, and the deformation to the normal cone realised fibrewise in the section “The exceptional algebra and the metric's residue” is Fulton's \cite[Ch.~5]{Fulton1998}. Signature-change hypersurfaces and conformally regularised cosmological boundaries, the tame class's physical exemplars, appear throughout the literature on signature change and on Penrose's conformal cyclic cosmology \cite{Penrose2010}. None of these sources, to our knowledge, treats the degenerating \emph{Clifford} sheaf itself, its nilpotent ideal, or the conservation-of-degeneracy phenomenon; those, together with the residue identification of the twist, are the contributions claimed.
__notes__.note.sheaf.setting-objects:
Throughout, $M$ is a smooth manifold of dimension $n \geq 2$, all data are $C^\infty$, and a \emph{cometric} on $M$ is a smooth symmetric bilinear form $G$ on the cotangent bundle $T^*M$, i.e.\ a smooth section of $S^2 TM$. We work on the cotangent side because that is where the gravitational application delivers the data: in gauge theory gravity it is the gauge field's induced cometric that crosses the singular locus smoothly while metric components diverge. Nothing below depends on that origin, and the tangent-side theory is identical under $T^*M \leftrightarrow TM$.

At a point $x$, the \emph{radical} of $G_x$ is $\rad(G_x) = \{\alpha \in T^*_xM : G_x(\alpha, \cdot) = 0\}$, and the \emph{corank} of $G_x$ is its dimension. The degenerate locus of $G$ is $\Sig = \{x : \rad(G_x) \neq 0\}$. On $M \setminus \Sig$ the form is nondegenerate and its signature is locally constant.
