__notes__.note.singularity.setting-introduction:
The information paradox is usually posed as a conflict between two theories. This paper poses it as a comparison of entropies computed in two algebras, and computes them.

The setting is gauge theory gravity (GTG), the formulation of general relativity in the spacetime algebra $\Cl(1,3)$ due to Lasenby, Doran and Gull \cite{LDG1998}, in which gravity is a gauge field $\hb$, a position-dependent linear map on vectors, and every metrical statement is built from $\hb^{-1}$: the theory's geometric content exists exactly where $\hb$ is invertible. the section “Step 1: locate the failure” sets the theory out exactly, field equations, connection bivector and gauge laws included, because the chain's first step is a statement about those equations and must be made in them. For Schwarzschild in the Newtonian gauge, $\hb$ is invertible in closed form at every $r > 0$, horizon included, and is unimodular there, so nothing determinant-like ever degenerates: the divergence is carried entirely by the connection bivector, and at $r = 0$ the description fails in every gauge, through a null kernel, in the exact rescaled-limit sense of Proposition \claimref{singularity.degeneration-exactly}. The singularity is a division-by-zero locus in the literal, algebraic sense, and the transport principle of this series, the root paper T1 \cite{ButlerT1}, is a general theory of exactly such loci: it classifies the obstruction, forces a minimal completion, and quantifies what any return to the original level must lose. Its operational form is the six-step transport algorithm of \cite[\S 8.1, Table 1]{ButlerT1}, and this paper is that algorithm run end to end on the black hole; the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} gives the step-by-step correspondence.

The paper runs the resulting chain from the classical field to the Page curve, numbered by the transport algorithm of the root paper with the physics expanded where it lies (Steps 1 to 3, 4a to 4e, 5, 6a and 6b), each step carrying its declared status (proved, or proved from named premises). The steps are summarised in the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.imported-equivalence-einstein-equations} and constitute the paper's outline. Steps 1 through 5 are theorems, at their stated scopes: the location and type of the failure, the forced ascent to $\Cl(2,4)$, the installation of canonical anticommutation relations where classical repair is barred, on the approach by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-c-number-repair} and at the boundary itself by Fact \claimref{singularity.imported-no-equivariant-value-wall}, the selection of the boost plane and its rate, the identity of boost and number operator, single-mode thermality at exactly $\TH$ with the state's marginals fixed by univalence and one regularity premise rather than assumed, the bosonic Planck sector by bosonisation in the s-wave-reduced sector under the named joint quasi-freeness premise (Q), and the lossy descent with its exact multi-mode cost (Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}). Steps 6a and 6b remain conditional in substance, but every condition is a \emph{named postulate}: the boundary-mode capacity is a theorem from three axioms (curvature cutoff, cell density, counted epoch, the causal-epoch integral computed exactly in Lemma \claimref{singularity.causal-epoch-computed-exactly}), the radiation entropy of the rate model is an exact identity from localisation, purity, capacity, injection and boundary-mode locality, with the Page envelope its corollary and exact saturation confined to the zero-frequency idealisation, of which the linear weights supply exactly one mode, the sea level, so no window of two or more members ever saturates, the no-attic condition is derived rather than assumed, and the envelope with its endpoint needs no typicality and no assumption about where correlations are placed, boundary-mode locality being the one dynamical premise. The chain's conclusion on the paradox is a dissolution rather than a resolution: information is lost at the $\Cl(1,3)$ level and preserved at the $\Cl(2,4)$ level, these are the same physics read at two levels, and the discrepancy between the levels is not destruction but a fixed algebraic projection whose thermal output is the Hawking flux itself and whose size is an equation: the relative entropy of Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}, carried entirely by the correlations of the quanta (Corollary \claimref{singularity.deficit-carried-quanta-correlations}).

The paper also contains an exactly solvable finite-mode model (the section “The finite-mode model: the dissolution step by step”) in which the dissolution can be followed step by step, at both levels. In the model, every single radiated quantum is \emph{provably, exactly} thermal, by a parity-protection lemma stating that no encoding by phase scrambling can be visible to any single-quantum measurement; the joint radiation state is pure; the information is recoverable from inter-quanta correlations; the mutual-information computation per emission, together with the Page-shaped entropy sequence, is computed in exact arithmetic and machine-verified; and the multi-mode descent is applied to the radiation outright (the section “The descent, applied: the two levels in numbers”), so that the two-level conclusion is exhibited in exact numbers (the table accompanying \claimref{singularity.purity-correlation-transfer-recovery} and Proposition \claimref{singularity.two-levels-finite-model}) rather than argued. The model is a toy by construction and is offered as one: its value is that every claim in it is a computation, so the chain's conceptual endpoint (thermality as the record of what the projection cannot see; correlations as its carrier) is exhibited rather than argued.

A word on the standard of proof, binding throughout. The environments Theorem, Proposition and Lemma, with a Proof, are reserved for results proved \emph{in this paper}, at the standard of T1 \cite{ButlerT1}. Results proved elsewhere that the chain needs are stated as \textbf{Facts (imported)}, with their precise provenance; the typography tracks the epistemic content, so a reader can see at a glance which links of the chain this paper carries and which it inherits. Four links not previously proved are proved here outright: the finite-dimensional modular theory behind Step 4d; the state selection that completes it, the identification of the descent with the fermion parity average and the rigidity theorem that follows (Theorems \claimref{singularity.descent-parity-average}, \claimref{singularity.ascended-marginals-are-diagonal}, \claimref{singularity.rate-rigidity-temperature-not-algebra-intrinsic}); the curvature behind Step 4b, derived in the gauge formalism in the text (Theorem \claimref{singularity.curvature-gauge-field-exact-shape-decoupling}), with the appendix as an independent metric-picture cross-check; and the multi-mode descent behind Steps 5 and 6b, with its deficit theorem (Theorem \claimref{singularity.deficit-theorem-cost-descent-exactly}).

Throughout, the physics the chain touches is kept in the text deliberately: $\Cl(2,4)$ as the conformal algebra and the twistor connection (Step 3), Israel's thermofield double and the Bisognano-Wichmann-Sewell mechanism (Step 4d), the island dictionary and the Hayden-Preskill mirror (Step 6b). These points of contact frame what kind of object the chain produces at each stage; the derivations do not depend on them.

__notes__.note.three-routes.abstract: Three open items of the Transport Papers are addressed at the point where they were priced. First, the pointwise reading of the metric level: with collar data in place, the assignment sending an open piece of the singular boundary to the families of fibrewise parity-even elements is a genuine sheaf, its existence as an untwisted sheaf equivalent to the standing hypothesis $w_1(\shL) = 0$; its stalks are the pointwise metric-level algebras, its finite truncations are exactly the range of the multi-mode descent, and the rival reading, the algebra generated by the pointwise fixed algebras, has the wrong stalks and is the section object of no sheaf. The antecedent of T5's Proposition 9.6 thereby reduces to the locality of the metric level. Second, the boundary no-go: completions built from different collar transversals are canonically isomorphic over the degenerate base, by an explicit unipotent intertwiner whose closure uses the radical gauge freedom; the base unipotents extend to automorphisms of any fixed completion and act on the candidate classical values by translations, which have no fixed point. No equivariant classical partner value exists at the boundary itself. Third, the hopping exclusion: every generator the tame machinery supplies is function-linear, function-linear endomorphisms preserve supports, and support-preserving families second-quantise to sums of single-point bilinears; occupation hopping between points is therefore impossible within the supplied class, the true residual being a genuinely differential dynamics. Every computational identity is machine-verified in exact arithmetic.

dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-.technical:
Under the sheaf paper's tameness hypothesis, let $\Sigma$ be a tame corank-one wall of the derived cometric $G(a,b) = \hb^T(a) \cdot \hb^T(b)$ of a gravitational field on flat spacetime, with radical spanned by a covector $k$ and residue $\lim_{\tau\to 0}\tau\,G^{-1} = k\otimes k/T$, $T \neq 0$. Any coframe with $\eta_{ab}e^ae^b = G^{-1}$, that is the physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$ in components, then has a component of order $\tau^{-1/2}$ along $k$: the soldering form $\hb^{-1}$ acquires a half-power pole rather than a radical, it is the frame map $\hb : \R^{1,3} \to TM$ that degenerates, and the free-sector theorem for a soldering form of corank one does not apply in the physical chart. In the weighted chart the coframe is regular of full rank and it is the internal cometric that acquires the radical, $\eta^{ab}(0) = \mathrm{diag}(0,\eta_3)$; its algebra $\{A : A\eta + \eta A^{\mathsf T} = 0\}$ is seven-dimensional (three rotations, three null rotations and the dilation $k \mapsto \alpha k$), one more than the Lorentz algebra.

In the ambient fibre $\R^{2,4}$, with the Witt partner normalised by $\ip{k}{k^*} = 1$, the subalgebra of $\so(2,4)$ preserving the four-plane of covectors is eight-dimensional and restricts onto that seven-dimensional algebra, and the dilation lifts to the boost $k \mapsto \alpha k$, $k^* \mapsto -\alpha k^*$ of the ladder plane $\mathrm{span}(k, k^*)$. For the Einstein-Cartan dynamics there are three cases: a full-rank soldering form vacates nothing, a regular corank-one form has the symmetric free sector, and at this wall the tractor-chart soldering form has a pole so neither applies. Whether the datum extends regularly in the ambient chart is open in general; at the Schwarzschild wall it has a simple pole whose residues are the completion's weights.
dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-.lay: A gravitational field can degenerate at a wall in two different ways: the ruler for directions can lose a dimension, or the ruler for gradients can. At such a wall exactly one new symmetry appears, a stretching of the dying direction, and it is the same as the boost relating the dying direction to its partner in the completion.

dark-energy.wall-counterterm.formal:
Assume $\Lambda \neq 0$, so that the curvature-squared form (quadratic in the field strength) exists. Let $\omega^{ab}$ be the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ of the gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}), written as Lorentz-connection one-forms in an orthonormal physical frame, $R^{ab} = d\omega^{ab} + \omega^{a}{}_{e}\wedge\omega^{eb}$ its field strength in that frame, and let $Q(\omega) := \epsilon_{abcd}\bigl(\omega^{ab}\wedge d\omega^{cd} + \tfrac23\,\omega^{ab}\wedge\omega^{c}{}_{e}\wedge\omega^{ed}\bigr)$ be its Chern-Simons three-form for the invariant $\epsilon_{abcd}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(i)] $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ identically: the topological term of Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2) is exact, with $Q$ as primitive.
\item[(ii)] On a Kasner approach the restriction of $Q$ to the slice $\Sigma_\varepsilon = \{\tau = \varepsilon\}$ is
\[
Q\big|_{\Sigma_\varepsilon} \;=\; 8\,p_1p_2p_3\;\varepsilon^{-2}\, d^3x ,
\]
so that the divergent part of the curvature-squared action on $\{\tau > \varepsilon\}$ is $-\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q = -\tfrac{24}{\Lambda}\,p_1p_2p_3\,\varepsilon^{-2}\,\mathrm{Vol}_3$, exactly the integral of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(iii).
\item[(iii)] The functional $S_{\mathrm{ren}} := S + \tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q(\omega)$, the action with the Chern-Simons form of the connection restricted to the wall added on the wall, has the same interior field equations as $S$ (a boundary term changes the boundary conditions of the variational problem, not the Euler-Lagrange equations), is finite as $\varepsilon \to 0$ on the Kasner approach, and its limit is the Einstein-Cartan and cosmological contributions together with the value of $Q$ on the far boundary. The counterterm is local, but it is not intrinsic to the wall: on the Kasner approach the whole surviving value comes from the cubic term in the boost block $\omega^{i0}$, the extrinsic curvature of the slice, the quadratic term vanishing because every nonzero $\omega^{ab}$ carries the index $0$ and $\epsilon_{abcd}$ needs four distinct indices. And $Q$ is a Chern-Simons form, not gauge invariant: under a rotation-gauge transformation (a local Lorentz rotation of the frame) on the slice it shifts by an exact form and a Wess-Zumino term, so the counterterm is defined relative to a frame, here the exceptional frame of Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-weighted-limit-schwarzschild-singularity-matching}. The residual ambiguity of the renormalisation is that frame choice together with the $O(\Lambda)$ constant by which the finite part shifts under the corrections of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}.
\end{enumerate}
On the Kasner approach the counterterm's coefficient $8p_1p_2p_3$ is the third elementary symmetric function of the residue, the one Kasner invariant beyond the two relations.
dark-energy.wall-counterterm.technical:
Assume $\Lambda \neq 0$ and let $Q(\omega)$ be the Chern-Simons three-form, for the invariant $\epsilon_{abcd}$, of the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ of Gauge Theory Gravity written as a Lorentz connection in an orthonormal physical frame. Then $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ identically, with $R^{ab}$ the field strength, so the topological term of the frozen-point action is exact. On a Kasner approach the restriction of $Q$ to the slice $\Sigma_\varepsilon = \{\tau = \varepsilon\}$ is $8\,p_1p_2p_3\,\varepsilon^{-2}\,d^3x$, so the divergent part of the curvature-squared action is $-\tfrac{24}{\Lambda}\,p_1p_2p_3\,\varepsilon^{-2}\,\mathrm{Vol}_3$, the integral found for the frozen-point datum at a Kasner wall.

Adding $\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q$ on the wall leaves the interior field equations unchanged, being a boundary term, and makes the action finite as $\varepsilon \to 0$ on the Kasner approach, with limit the Einstein-Cartan and cosmological contributions plus the far-boundary value of $Q$. The counterterm is local but not intrinsic to the wall: its value comes entirely from the cubic term in the boost block, the extrinsic curvature of the slice. Since $Q$ is not gauge invariant, the counterterm is defined relative to a frame, here the exceptional frame, and the residual ambiguity is that frame choice together with an $O(\Lambda)$ constant from the cosmological corrections.
dark-energy.wall-counterterm.lay: Assume the cosmological constant is nonzero, so that the curvature-squared form of the frozen-point action exists. In that action one term grows without bound as a Kasner-type singularity is approached. This result shows that the troublesome term is a total derivative, so its divergence sits entirely on the boundary, and it can be cancelled by adding a matching term on the wall. Doing so leaves the field equations away from the wall unchanged. The cancellation is defined relative to a choice of frame and leaves a finite ambiguity of the size of the cosmological corrections.

proofs.main: Here $\omega^{ab}$ and $R^{ab}$ are the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ and its field strength written as forms in an orthonormal physical frame (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(ii) and (iv)), so every step is a computation in Gauge Theory Gravity on one flat chart. (i) is the transgression formula for a quadratic invariant polynomial, here $\epsilon_{abcd}$ on $\mathfrak{so}(1,3)$: $d(\omega\,d\omega) = d\omega\wedge d\omega$ and $d(\omega^3) = 3\,d\omega\wedge\omega^2$ under the invariant pairing, so $dQ = \epsilon(d\omega + \omega^2, d\omega + \omega^2)$ up to the term $\epsilon(\omega^2,\omega^2)$, which vanishes by the invariance of $\epsilon_{abcd}$ under the adjoint action (the Jacobi identity). The script confirms $dQ = \epsilon_{abcd}R^{ab}\wedge R^{cd}$ as an exact identity of forms on the Kasner connection. (ii) On the slice only the terms of $Q$ without a $d\tau$ leg survive. The quadratic term vanishes on the slice for two reasons, either sufficient: every $d\omega^{cd}$ carries a $d\tau$ leg (the connection depends on $\tau$ only and has tangential legs), and every nonzero $\omega^{ab}$ carries the index $0$ while $\epsilon_{abcd}$ needs four distinct indices; and the cubic term reduces to $\tfrac23\epsilon_{i0jk}\,\omega^{i0}\wedge\omega^{j}{}_{0}\wedge\omega^{0k}$ and its index rearrangements: with $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau)e^i$ each is a multiple of $p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-3}e^1\wedge e^2\wedge e^3 = p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}d^3x$, and collecting the signs and multiplicities gives the coefficient $8$; the script computes the $(x,y,z)$ component of $Q$ exactly and finds $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$. Then $\int_{\tau>\varepsilon}\epsilon RR = \int Q\big|_{\text{far}} - \int_{\Sigma_\varepsilon}Q$ by Stokes, and $-\tfrac3\Lambda\cdot 8p_1p_2p_3\varepsilon^{-2}$ integrates $-\tfrac{3}{\Lambda}\cdot 16 p_1p_2p_3\int_\varepsilon\tau^{-3}d\tau$, matching Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-datum-kasner-wall}(iii). (iii) A boundary term does not change the Euler-Lagrange equations in the interior. By (ii) the added term cancels the wall boundary contribution of the exact topological term identically on the Kasner approach, leaving the far-boundary value of $Q$ and the two remaining terms of the expansion in \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(2), the Einstein-Cartan term ($2\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^ae^bR^{cd}$, whose density is $-8\Lambda\tau$ on the Einstein region) and the cosmological term ($\tfrac{\Lambda}{3}\int\epsilon_{abcd}e^ae^be^ce^d$, whose density is $24\tau$ before the prefactor), all finite as $\varepsilon\to 0$. With the corrections of Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.cosmological-constant-does-not-change-residue}, $\omega^{i0} = (p_i/\tau + \tfrac{\Lambda}{2}(1-p_i)\tau + \dots)e^i$ and the cubic term of $Q$ on the slice acquires, beyond $8p_1p_2p_3\tau^{-2}$, a term of order $\Lambda\tau^0$ and higher: a finite constant, which is the only freedom in the subtraction.

dark-energy.walls-free-sector.formal:
Let $(\hb, \Omega)$ be a gravitational field on flat spacetime (Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields}) whose physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$, here taken as the regular variable and written in an orthonormal frame $\{\gamma_a\}$ as the soldering form $e^a(v) = \gamma^a \cdot \hb^{-1}(v)$, is of corank one at a point, so that $\hb$ fails there: $e$ is a regular map $TM \to \mathbb{R}^{1,3}$ from background to physical vectors with a one-dimensional radical $r$ ($e^a(r) = 0$ for every $a$) and cokernel direction $n$ ($n_a e^a = 0$), so that the derived metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{ab}e^a_\mu e^b_\nu$ is finite and degenerate (this is the degeneration dual to the sheaf paper's; see Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}); the image $e(T_xM)$ is a three-dimensional subspace of the frame space, the wall's tangent space, and it may be of any type (Lorentzian, Riemannian, or null). The Einstein-Cartan equations \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west} are polynomial in $e$, in the rotation-gauge field written as connection one-forms $\omega$, and in their derivatives, so polynomiality (Theorem \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1)) keeps them meaningful at the point. Choose the normal form $e^a = dx^a$ for $a = 0,1,2$, $e^3 = 0$, so that $r = \partial_3$, $n = \delta^3$, and the wall's tangent space carries the frame indices $0,1,2$; write $K^{a}{}_{b} := \omega^{a}{}_{3\,b}$ and $M_{c\mu} := \tfrac12\,\epsilon_{cab}\,\omega^{ab}{}_{\mu}$ for $a, b, c, \mu \in \{0,1,2\}$, the boost components into the dying frame direction and the dualised tangential connection, and lower and raise their indices with the wall metric $\eta_{ab}$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item[(a)] \emph{(Torsion.)} Regarded as linear conditions on the $24$ components of the torsion, the connection equation has rank $24$ on the invertible region and rank $18$ at the point: three of its components are identities $0 = 0$ and six torsion components are freed, all tangential to the wall (every component with a leg along $r$, and the cokernel component $n_dT^d$, are forced to vanish). Regarded as conditions on the $36$ components of the curvature, the frame equation has rank $16$ in both cases: no curvature condition is lost, and the components of the frame equation along the radical do \emph{not} vanish identically.
\item[(b)] \emph{(Connection.)} Regarded as conditions on the $24$ components of $\omega$, the connection equation has rank $12$ at the point. The free sector is exactly two symmetric tensors on the wall's tangent space: $K_{ab}$ symmetric (six components), which is invisible to the torsion because it multiplies $e^3 = 0$, and $M_{c\mu}$ symmetric (six components), which is the connection image of the freed torsion of (a), $t = (\operatorname{tr}M)\,\mathbf{1} - M$. Forced to their Levi-Civita values are the antisymmetric parts of $K$ and $M$ and every component $\omega^{ab}{}_{3}$ along the radical leg.
\item[(c)] \emph{(Propagation.)} The frame equation contains no derivative of the symmetric part of $M$ in any direction. Its principal symbol in the radical direction determines the radial derivatives $\partial_3 K_{ab}$ of all six components of $K$, and its tangential symbols impose first-order conditions on $K$ along the wall. The field equations therefore cannot propagate $M$ across the wall.
\item[(d)] \emph{(The wall's Hamiltonian constraint.)} In the normal form with $de = 0$, on the free sector $K \oplus M$ the frame equation reduces to a single component, $E_3$ evaluated on $(\partial_0, \partial_1, \partial_2)$, which reads
\[
\sigma_2'(M) \;-\; \sigma_2'(K) \;-\; 2\Lambda \;=\; 0, \qquad \sigma_2'(A) := (\operatorname{tr}A)^2 - \operatorname{tr}(A^2),
\]
with traces taken on the mixed tensors $M^{c}{}_{\mu}$, $K^{a}{}_{b}$: $K$ and $M$ enter only there, only quadratically, and with no cross term; the other fifteen components of the frame equation vanish identically on the free sector. On a curved wall the Levi-Civita part of $\omega$ adds the wall's intrinsic curvature to this component and algebraic cross terms with $M$ and $K$ to the others.
\end{enumerate}
Consequently, on the flat model of (d), the field equations at a corank-one wall of the soldering form determine the connection up to a symmetric bilinear form $M$ on the wall's tangent space which they constrain by one scalar relation and never propagate: data on the wall that the bulk equations do not determine. On a wall with intrinsic curvature the statement that survives is (c): $M$ is never propagated; how much of $M$ the fifteen other components then fix algebraically, through their cross terms with the Levi-Civita part and with the first derivatives of the connection, is a jet computation not done here (successor problem (2)). \emph{Level:} proved, for the equations as imported in Fact \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}; the ranks and symbol ranks are invariant under the changes of frame and coordinates that preserve the normal form. The script confirms in exact arithmetic the counts of (a) to (c) and the single surviving component of (d) for all three types of dying direction, and the $K \oplus M$ description of (b) with the identity of (d) for the Lorentzian and Riemannian types, whose wall metric is nondegenerate; at the Riemannian type, where the boost is into a timelike direction, the cosmological term enters (d) with the opposite sign, $\sigma_2'(K) - \sigma_2'(M) - 2\Lambda = 0$. At the null type the dying direction lies in the wall, the wall metric is degenerate, and the twelve-dimensional free sector does not split as $K \oplus M$; (b) and (d) are stated for the Lorentzian normal form only. Which walls are of this type, and in particular that the sheaf paper's wall is not, is Proposition \claimref{dark-energy.sheaf-papers-wall-soldering-variables}.
dark-energy.walls-free-sector.technical:
Take a gravitational field on flat spacetime whose soldering form $e$, the physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$ in components, has corank one at a point, with radical $r$ and cokernel direction $n$, so that $\hb$ fails there and the derived metric $g_{\mu\nu} = \eta_{ab}e^a_\mu e^b_\nu$ is finite and degenerate; the Einstein-Cartan equations are polynomial in $e$ and in the rotation-gauge field $\omega$ and so still make sense there. In the normal form $e^a = dx^a$ ($a = 0,1,2$), $e^3 = 0$, the connection equation, as conditions on the torsion, drops from rank $24$ to rank $18$, freeing six tangential torsion components, while the frame equation keeps rank $16$ on the curvature. As conditions on the connection itself it has rank $12$, and the free sector is exactly two symmetric tensors on the wall's tangent space: $K_{ab}$, the boost components into the dying direction, and $M_{c\mu}$, the dualised tangential connection.

The frame equation contains no derivative of the symmetric part of $M$, so the field equations cannot propagate $M$ across the wall. On the flat model with $de = 0$ the only surviving component is $\sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K) - 2\Lambda = 0$, with $\sigma_2'(A) = (\operatorname{tr}A)^2 - \operatorname{tr}(A^2)$. So on the flat model the connection is fixed up to a symmetric form $M$ constrained by one scalar relation and never propagated; on a curved wall only the non-propagation is proved. The counts hold for all three types of dying direction, and the split $K \oplus M$ with its constraint is stated for the Lorentzian normal form.
dark-energy.walls-free-sector.lay: Suppose the gauge field that relates physical directions to directions in the flat background loses one direction at a wall of the ordinary (Lorentzian) type. Einstein-Cartan gravity then no longer fixes all of the connection there: a symmetric piece of data living on the wall is left free, and the equations never carry it across the wall. On a curved wall only this last point is proved. On the simplest flat model they constrain it by a single relation, so the wall holds information that the bulk equations do not determine.

proofs.main:
Throughout, $e$ is the physical-vector map $\hb^{-1}$ in components, $e^a(v) = \gamma^a \cdot \hb^{-1}(v)$, and $\omega$ the rotation-gauge field $\Omega$ in the frame $\{\gamma_a\}$, so the component computation is one of Gauge Theory Gravity (Fact \claimref{synthesis.imported-gtg-dictionary}(i) and (ii)). \emph{Normal form.} Both equations, the Einstein-Cartan equations of \claimref{dark-energy.imported-macdowell-mansouri-theorem-stelle-west}, are built from $\epsilon_{abcd}$, $e$, $\omega$ and $d$, without the metric, which is the polynomiality of \claimref{dark-energy.frozen-point-makes-stelle-west-vector}(1). Under $GL(4)$ on the coordinates and the Lorentz group on the frame, $\epsilon_{abcd}$ is invariant up to $\det$, so ranks and symbol ranks are invariant; a corank-one $e$ may be brought to $e^a = dx^a$ ($a = 0,1,2$), $e^3 = 0$ by a coordinate change and a Lorentz rotation whenever the image is Lorentzian, to $e^0 = 0$ when it is Riemannian, and to $e^0 = e^1 = dx^0$, $e^2 = dx^2$, $e^3 = dx^3$ when it is null; the script runs all three, with identical counts, and the argument below is written for the first. Throughout, a three-form in four variables has four components, one for each omitted coordinate.

\emph{(a) Torsion, pairs not containing $3$.} For $(a,b) \in \{01, 02, 12\}$ the only nonzero terms of $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^c\wedge T^d$ have $d = 3$, since $e^3 = 0$ removes the terms with $c = 3$; with $c$ the remaining index the equation reads $dx^c\wedge T^3 = 0$. So $T^3\wedge dx^0 = T^3\wedge dx^1 = T^3\wedge dx^2 = 0$. A two-form divisible by $dx^0$ and by $dx^1$ is a multiple of $dx^0\wedge dx^1$, and divisibility by $dx^2$ then forces it to vanish: $T^3 = 0$, six independent conditions. Each of the three equations has one component that is identically zero, the one omitting $c$: three vacated components. \emph{Pairs containing $3$.} For $(a, 3)$ with $\{b, c\} = \{0,1,2\}\setminus\{a\}$ the equation reads $dx^b\wedge T^c = dx^c\wedge T^b$. Split $T^b = \theta^b\wedge dx^3 + \tau^b$ with $\theta^b$ a one-form and $\tau^b$ a two-form in $dx^0, dx^1, dx^2$. The $dx^3$ parts give $dx^b\wedge\theta^c = dx^c\wedge\theta^b$ for all three pairs: writing $\theta^b = \theta^b_\mu dx^\mu$ and $\mu$ for the index other than $b, c$, the components are $\theta^c_\mu = 0$, $\theta^b_\mu = 0$ and $\theta^b_b + \theta^c_c = 0$; over the three pairs every off-diagonal component vanishes and $\theta^0_0 + \theta^1_1 = \theta^0_0 + \theta^2_2 = \theta^1_1 + \theta^2_2 = 0$, so $\theta = 0$: nine conditions, every radical-leg component gone. The $dx^3$-free parts give $dx^b\wedge\tau^c = dx^c\wedge\tau^b$, one condition per pair, three in all, on the nine components of $\tau$: six free, all tangential. Total rank $6 + 9 + 3 = 18$; on the invertible region the same argument with all four $dx^a$ present is the classical one and gives $T = 0$, rank $24$. \emph{Frame equation.} With $e^3 = 0$,
\[
\begin{aligned}
E_3 &= \epsilon_{3bcd}\,dx^b\wedge F^{cd} \qquad (b,c,d \in \{0,1,2\}),\\
E_a &= 2\sum_{b,c}\epsilon_{abc3}\,dx^b\wedge F^{c3} \qquad (a \in \{0,1,2\};\ b, c \in \{0,1,2\}\setminus\{a\}).
\end{aligned}
\]
The unknowns separate: $F^{01}, F^{02}, F^{12}$ enter only $E_3$, and $F^{03}, F^{13}, F^{23}$ enter only $E_0, E_1, E_2$. For $E_3$, the four choices $F^{12} = dx^1\wedge dx^2$, $dx^1\wedge dx^3$, $dx^2\wedge dx^3$ and $F^{02} = dx^2\wedge dx^3$ produce, one each, the four components of a three-form: rank $4$. For $E_0, E_1, E_2$ split $F^{c3} = \phi^c\wedge dx^3 + \psi^c$. The $dx^3$-leg components are $\epsilon_{abc}\,dx^b\wedge\phi^c$, nine from nine, and this map is the $\theta$ system above with the roles renamed, hence bijective; the $dx^3$-free components, one per $E_a$, are hit independently by $\psi^2_{02}$, $\psi^0_{01}$ and $\psi^1_{12}$. Rank $4 + 9 + 3 = 16$, the full target; on the invertible region rank can only be at least as large and the target is sixteen-dimensional. For the radical components, $\iota_r E_a = -\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^b\wedge\iota_r F^{cd}$ is not zero for generic $F$; the script exhibits an integer instance.

\emph{(b) Connection.} An inhomogeneous $de^a$ enters the connection equation only as a source term, which leaves the rank of the linear map $\omega \mapsto \epsilon\,e\wedge T(\omega)$ unchanged, so take $de = 0$: $T^a = \omega^{a}{}_{b}\wedge e^b$. The dying direction: $T^3 = \sum_{b<3}\omega^{3}{}_{b\mu}\,dx^\mu\wedge dx^b$, whose tangential components are the antisymmetric part of $\omega^{3}{}_{b\mu}$ in $(b,\mu)$ and whose radial-leg components are $\omega^{3}{}_{b3}$; $T^3 = 0$ therefore forces the antisymmetric part of $K$ and the three components $\omega^{a3}{}_{3}$ to vanish and leaves the symmetric part of $K$ free, six components; $K$ never enters $T^a$ for $a < 3$, because there it multiplies $e^3 = 0$. The tangential connection: for $a < 3$, $T^a = \omega^{a}{}_{b}\wedge dx^b$ over $b < 3$, so $T^a_{\,3n} = \omega^{a}{}_{n3}$ and the radical-leg condition $\theta = 0$ of (a) forces $\omega^{ab}{}_{3} = 0$, three components; and $T^a_{\,mn} = \omega^{a}{}_{nm} - \omega^{a}{}_{mn}$ for $m,n < 3$ is the classical three-dimensional torsion-contortion map, a bijection of nine-dimensional spaces. Dualising with $\omega^{ab}{}_{\mu} = \epsilon^{abc}M_{c\mu}$ and $t^{a}{}_{d} = \tfrac12\epsilon_{d}{}^{mn}T^a_{\,mn}$, the contraction $\epsilon_{dmn}\epsilon^{amc} = \delta^a_d\delta^c_n - \delta^c_d\delta^a_n$ gives $t = (\operatorname{tr}M)\mathbf{1} - M$, so $t$ is symmetric exactly when $M$ is: the three conditions of (a) are the vanishing of the antisymmetric part of $M$, and the free sector is the symmetric part, six components. Forced: three from each of the antisymmetric part of $K$, the radial-leg $\omega^{a3}{}_{3}$, the radial-leg $\omega^{ab}{}_{3}$ and the antisymmetric part of $M$: rank $12$, free $12$, as claimed.

\emph{(c) Propagation.} The derivative terms of the frame equation are $\epsilon_{abcd}\,e^b\wedge d\omega^{cd}$. For $a = 3$ and $b < 3$ the pair $(c,d)$ is the complement of $b$ in $\{0,1,2\}$, so $\omega^{cd}$ is $\pm M_{b\mu}$: the components of $E_3$ with a $dx^3$ leg are $\partial_3(M_{bx} - M_{xb})$ up to sign, the antisymmetric part only, and the component without a $dx^3$ leg is $\epsilon^{bmn}\partial_m M_{bn}$ up to sign, which vanishes on symmetric $M$. So no derivative of symmetric $M$ appears in $E_3$, and none appears in $E_a$ for $a < 3$, where only $\omega^{c3}$, that is $K$ and its forced complement, occurs. For $K$: the $dx^3$-leg components of $E_a$ ($a < 3$) are $\partial_3 K_{c y}$ with $c$ the index other than $a, b$ and $y \neq b$, which over the two choices of $b$ and the allowed $y$ reach all six components of symmetric $K$; the remaining components carry tangential derivatives of $K$. The script confirms the symbol ranks: $0$ on $M$ in every direction, $6$ on $K$ in the radial direction and $3$ in each tangential direction.

\emph{(d) The Hamiltonian component.} With $de = 0$ and the forced sector at its Levi-Civita value zero, $R^{cd} = \omega^{c}{}_{f}\wedge\omega^{fd}$ and the frame equation is quadratic in $(K, M)$. For $a < 3$ every term of $E_a$ carries $\omega^{c3}$ against $\omega^{3d}$ or a tangential $\omega$, and the $dx^3$-free components need three tangential legs from two one-forms and $dx^b$, which is impossible with $b$ fixed by $a$; the script confirms that all twelve components of $E_a$, $a<3$, vanish identically on the free sector. For $E_3$ on $(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$: the $f = 3$ terms give $\epsilon_{3bcd}\,dx^b\wedge\omega^{c}{}_{3}\wedge\omega^{3d} = -\epsilon_{bcd}\,\epsilon^{bxy}K^{c}{}_{x}K^{d}{}_{y} = -\bigl(\delta^x_c\delta^y_d - \delta^x_d\delta^y_c\bigr)K^{c}{}_{x}K^{d}{}_{y} = -\sigma_2'(K)$, and the $f < 3$ terms give, after dualising both factors with $\omega^{cd} = \epsilon^{cdg}M_{g\mu}$, the same contraction on $M$ with the opposite sign, $+\sigma_2'(M)$; cross terms vanish because $\omega^{c}{}_{3}\wedge\omega^{3d}$ and $\omega^{c}{}_{f}\wedge\omega^{fd}$ ($f<3$) lie in different terms. The cosmological term $\ell^{-2}\epsilon_{3bcd}\,e^b\wedge e^c\wedge e^d$ contributes $-6\ell^{-2} = -2\Lambda$ on $(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2)$. The script confirms the identity $E_3(\partial_0,\partial_1,\partial_2) = \sigma_2'(M) - \sigma_2'(K)$ on random elements of the free sector, the vanishing of the cross term, and the coefficient $-6$.

obj.sheaf.clifford-sheaf.formal: For a cometric $G$ on $M$, the \emph{Clifford sheaf} $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$ is the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-algebras ($\mathcal{O}_M$ the sheaf of smooth real functions) whose local sections are smooth sections of the bundle of algebras $\coprod_{x} \Cl(T^*_xM, G_x)$, with the local trivialisations induced by blade frames: a local frame $e_1, \dots, e_n$ of $T^*M$ induces the fibrewise blade bases $\{e_I(x)\}$ of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included}.
obj.sheaf.clifford-sheaf.technical: Given a cometric $G$ on $M$, possibly degenerate, the Clifford sheaf $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$ is the sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-algebras whose local sections are smooth sections of the bundle of fibre algebras $\Cl(T^*_xM, G_x)$. Smoothness is defined through blade frames: a local frame $e_1, \dots, e_n$ of $T^*M$ gives at each point the blade basis $\{e_I(x)\}$, which is a basis whether or not $G_x$ is degenerate, and these bases supply the local trivialisations.
obj.sheaf.clifford-sheaf.lay: At each point of a space one can build a Clifford algebra, an algebra of directions, from the way the geometry measures covectors. The Clifford sheaf gathers all of these algebras into one smoothly varying object over the whole space. Because the basis used to glue them together works even where the measurement degenerates, the construction does not stop where the geometry fails.

obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling.formal:
A choice of \emph{collar data} for the tame wall $\Sig$ consists of: a \emph{global} spanning section $k$ of $\shL$, extended to a covector field on a neighbourhood of $\Sig$; a vector field $u$ near $\Sig$ with $k(u) = 1$ (a transversal, in the sense that $u$ is not annihilated by the dying direction); a bump function $\beta$ supported in a collar neighbourhood of $\Sig$ and identically $1$ on a smaller collar; and real constants $\mu, \nu \neq 0$. Collar data exist exactly when the radical line bundle is trivial, $w_1(\shL) = 0$ (Fact \claimref{sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles}); this triviality is a standing hypothesis of the completion construction, and the section “Topology of tame walls, and the global choices” records why it is genuinely needed and what the twisted variant would be. Write $e \in TM$ for the field $u$ regarded as the evaluation functional $\alpha \mapsto \alpha(u)$ on $T^*M$. The \emph{coupling} is the symmetric form $\kappa$ on $T$ determined by
\[
\kappa(\alpha, \nO) = \nu\beta\,\alpha(u), \qquad \kappa(\alpha, \nInf) = \mu\beta\,\alpha(u) \qquad (\alpha \in T^*M),
\]
with $\kappa$ vanishing on $T^*M \times T^*M$ and on the adjoined plane. The \emph{ambient form} is
\[
h \;:=\; G \perp H + \kappa .
\]
Outside the support of $\beta$ the coupling vanishes and $h = G \perp H$; the restriction of $h$ to $T^*M$ is $G$ identically, everywhere, since $\kappa$ pairs $T^*M$ only with the adjoined plane.
obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling.technical:

u$. They exist exactly when $\shL$ is trivial, $w_1(\shL) = 0$, a standing hypothesis of the completion.

obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling.lay: To complete the geometry at a wall one adds a small extra plane of directions, and must then say how it is attached to the original ones. Collar data are the choices needed for that: a label for the dying direction, a direction pointing across the wall, a smooth switch that is on near the wall and off far from it, and two constants. The coupling uses them to link the extra plane to the original directions near the wall only, without changing how the original directions measure each other.

obj.sheaf.extensions.formal: An \emph{extension} is a locally free rank-four $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$-submodule $\mathcal{M}$ of the $u$-smooth one-forms which spans the full cotangent module over the interior and whose Gram $G|_{\mathcal{M}\times\mathcal{M}}$ extends smoothly to $E$. It is \emph{rain-bounded} if every element has bounded components in the infalling orthonormal frame, equivalently (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.rain-duality}(3)) if $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \shW$. The boundary-tameness conditions are those of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.boundary-tameness-stated}, with (T3$\partial$) read on the eigenvalue: the dying \emph{eigenvalue} of the Gram, with respect to any auxiliary frame metric, vanishes to exactly first order in the defining function $r$.
obj.sheaf.extensions.technical: An extension is a locally free rank-four $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$-submodule $\mathcal{M}$ of the $u$-smooth one-forms that spans the full cotangent module over the interior and whose Gram $G|_{\mathcal{M}\times\mathcal{M}}$ extends smoothly to the boundary $E$. It is rain-bounded if every element has bounded components in the infalling orthonormal frame, which is equivalent to $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \shW$. For boundary tameness the condition on the dying direction is read on the eigenvalue: the dying eigenvalue of the Gram, with respect to any auxiliary frame metric, vanishes to exactly first order in the defining function $r$.
obj.sheaf.extensions.lay: Near the black hole singularity there are many ways to decide which one-forms count as well behaved at the boundary. An extension is any such choice that agrees with ordinary geometry inside, has the right size, and keeps the geometry's measurements smooth up to the boundary. It is called rain-bounded if everything in it stays finite as seen by observers falling freely inwards.

obj.sheaf.log-completion.formal: $\mathcal{A}^{\log}$ is the algebra of sums $\sum_{j,\ell} f_{j,\ell}(x,\tau)\,\tau^{e_j(x)}(\log\tau)^{\ell}$ over admissible exponent families (Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data}), with $f_{j,\ell}$ smooth up to $\tau = 0$ and the log powers $\ell$ locally bounded (the index letter avoiding the radical section $k$).
obj.sheaf.log-completion.technical: The log completion $\mathcal{A}^{\log}$ enlarges the variable-order algebra by allowing powers of $\log\tau$. Its elements are sums $\sum_{j,\ell} f_{j,\ell}(x,\tau)\,\tau^{e_j(x)}(\log\tau)^{\ell}$ over admissible exponent families $\{e_j\}$, with coefficients $f_{j,\ell}$ smooth up to $\tau = 0$ and the log powers $\ell$ locally bounded.
obj.sheaf.log-completion.lay: Near the boundary, functions are described as sums of powers of the distance to it, with exponents that may vary from point to point. The log completion also allows each power to be multiplied by a power of the logarithm of that distance, with only a bounded number of logarithms in any region.

obj.sheaf.relatively-admissible-perturba.formal: Let $G$ be the weighted Gram of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced}, dying slot $1$, nondegenerate slots $\{0,2,3\}$. A symmetric $\mathcal{A}$-bilinear perturbation $\Xi_\bullet$ (the letter avoiding the boundary $E$) is \emph{relatively admissible} if, for some $\delta > 0$: the entries on the nondegenerate slots lie in $\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$; the mixed entries (dying slot against a nondegenerate slot) lie in $\varrho^{1/2}\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$ (note $\varrho^{1/2} = \tau^{-p_1(x)} \in \mathcal{A}$); and the dying entry lies in $\varrho\,\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$.
obj.sheaf.relatively-admissible-perturba.technical: Take the weighted Gram $G$ of the variable-weight theory, with dying slot $1$ and nondegenerate slots $0, 2, 3$. A symmetric $\mathcal{A}$-bilinear perturbation $\Xi_\bullet$ is relatively admissible if, for some $\delta > 0$, each entry carries a factor $\tau^\delta$ beyond the weight of its slots: entries on the nondegenerate slots lie in $\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$, mixed entries of the dying slot against a nondegenerate slot lie in $\varrho^{1/2}\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$, and the dying entry lies in $\varrho\,\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$, where $\varrho^{1/2} = \tau^{-p_1(x)}$ belongs to $\mathcal{A}$.
obj.sheaf.relatively-admissible-perturba.lay: This definition says when a change to the weighted geometry near the singularity counts as small. Each entry of the change must be smaller, by a definite positive power of the distance to the boundary, than the natural size attached to its pair of directions. The dying direction carries a different natural size from the others.

obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-.formal:
Let $E$ be a smooth $3$-manifold and $\Mt = [0,\varepsilon)_\tau \times E$. An \emph{admissible exponent family} is a countable family $\{e_j\}$ of smooth nonnegative functions on $E$ such that, on each compact $K \subseteq E$ and for each level $N$, only finitely many $e_j$ have $\inf_K e_j \leq N$. The \emph{variable-order algebra} $\mathcal{A}$ is the algebra of sums $\sum_j f_j(x,\tau)\,\tau^{e_j(x)}$ over admissible exponent families, with $f_j$ smooth up to $\tau = 0$; on each compact and each interval $[0, \tau_0]$, the terms below any level are finitely many and the remainder is $O(\tau^{N})$ locally uniformly, so the sums converge locally uniformly and the class is closed under products (exponent families add, and the sum family is again admissible). Two conventions: an element is identified with the function it defines, and the representation-sensitive notions used later (exponent sets, log degree) rest on the non-membership statements of the section “The smooth structure of the variable-order algebra”, which are proved for exactly this class. \emph{Strict diagonal data} on $\Mt$ is a local coframe $(d\tau, \sigma^1, \sigma^2, \sigma^3)$ and a cometric whose Gram in it is
\[
\operatorname{diag}\bigl(1,\ -\tau^{-2p_1(x)}c_1,\ -\tau^{-2p_2(x)}c_2,\ -\tau^{-2p_3(x)}c_3\bigr),
\]
with $p_i$ smooth, $p_1 < 0 < p_2 \leq p_3$ pointwise, and $c_i(x,\tau)$ smooth and positive up to $\tau = 0$. The Kasner constraints are \emph{not} hypotheses of anything in this section: the sheaf theory is kinematic, and the constraints enter only through the Einstein-flow provenance of Fact \claimref{sheaf.kasner-data-interior}.
obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-.technical:
On $\Mt = [0,\varepsilon)_\tau \times E$, with $E$ a smooth $3$-manifold, an admissible exponent family is a countable family of smooth nonnegative functions $e_j$ on $E$ with only finitely many below any level on each compact. The variable-order algebra $\mathcal{A}$ consists of the sums $\sum_j f_j(x,\tau)\,\tau^{e_j(x)}$ with $f_j$ smooth up to $\tau = 0$; these converge locally uniformly and the class is closed under products, since exponent families add.

Strict diagonal data are a local coframe $(d\tau, \sigma^1, \sigma^2, \sigma^3)$ and a cometric with Gram $\operatorname{diag}(1, -\tau^{-2p_1(x)}c_1, -\tau^{-2p_2(x)}c_2, -\tau^{-2p_3(x)}c_3)$, where the $p_i$ are smooth with $p_1 < 0 < p_2 \leq p_3$ and the $c_i$ are smooth and positive up to $\tau = 0$. The Kasner constraints are not assumed: the theory is kinematic.
obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-.lay: Near a singularity, geometric quantities often behave like powers of the time remaining, with exponents that change from place to place. The variable-order algebra is the class of functions built from such powers, restricted enough that they can be added, multiplied and summed reliably. Strict diagonal data describe, in this language, a geometry whose three spatial directions scale with their own powers of time, one exponent negative and two positive, allowed to vary across space.

obj.sheaf.weighted-coframe-module.formal:
Let $\Mt_u$ denote $\Mt$ with the quasihomogeneous smooth structure of order two at the boundary: smooth functions of $(u, t, \omega)$, $u = \sqrt{r}$. Define $\shW$ as the $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$-module with frame
\[
\rho := r^{1/2}\,dr \;(= 2u^2\,du), \qquad \dtPG, \qquad \mu_1 := r\,d\theta, \qquad \mu_2 := r\sin\theta\,d\phi ,
\]
where $t$ is Painlev\'e-Gullstrand time, the time label of the flat background in the gauge $\hb = 1 - \beta P$ of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric}, and $(r, \theta, \phi)$ are its spherical labels; the one-forms are background covectors, read against physical vectors through the coframe $g^\mu = \hb^{T}(e^\mu)$ of Definition \claimref{obj.synthesis.gtg-flat-spacetime-gauge-fields} (the angular pair is a chart expression; the module they generate is global over the sphere).
obj.sheaf.weighted-coframe-module.technical: Give $\Mt$ the quasihomogeneous smooth structure of order two at the boundary, in which smooth functions are smooth in $(u, t, \omega)$ with $u = \sqrt{r}$, and call the result $\Mt_u$. The weighted coframe module $\shW$ is the $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$-module with frame $\rho = r^{1/2}\,dr = 2u^2\,du$, $\dtPG$, $\mu_1 = r\,d\theta$ and $\mu_2 = r\sin\theta\,d\phi$, where $t$ is Painlev\'e-Gullstrand time, the time label of the flat background in the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand gauge field $\hb = 1 - \beta P$. The angular pair is a chart expression, but the module it generates is global over the sphere.
obj.sheaf.weighted-coframe-module.lay: Near the Schwarzschild singularity the ordinary one-forms behave badly. The weighted coframe module replaces them by rescaled versions: a radial one weighted by the square root of the radius, two angular ones weighted by the radius, and the time of freely falling observers. To make the rescaled radial form smooth, smoothness near the singularity is measured in the square root of the radius.

obj.three-routes.ladder-bundle-even-subb.formal:
With collar data fixed (Fact \claimref{three-routes.imported-collar-data-coupling}), the sections $k$ and $k^{*} = \nO/2\nu$ of the completed Clifford sheaf are global over $\Sig$, and at each $x \in \Sig$ they generate the fibre algebra $\Aa_x \cong \Mat_2(\R)$-type mode factor of \cite[Cor.~4.5]{ButlerT4}. Write $\sigma(x) := k^{*}(x)k(x) - k(x)k^{*}(x)$, a global section with $\sigma(x)^2 = 1$, and $\alpha_x := \operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(x))$ for the fibrewise parity. The \emph{ladder bundle} $\Aa \to \Sig$ is the bundle with fibres $\Aa_x$; the \emph{even subbundle} $\Aa^{+} \subseteq \Aa$ has fibres the fixed algebras $\Aa_x^{+} = \{a \in \Aa_x : \alpha_x(a) = a\}$. The \emph{metric-level presheaf} assigns to each open $U \subseteq \Sig$ the algebra
\[
\mathfrak{M}(U) \;:=\; \Gamma(U, \Aa^{+}) \;=\; \bigl\{\, s : U \to \Aa^{+} \ \text{smooth},\ s(x) \in \Aa_x^{+}\ \forall x \in U \,\bigr\},
\]
with the restriction maps of sections.
obj.three-routes.ladder-bundle-even-subb.technical: Fix collar data. Then the sections $k$ and $k^* = \nO/2\nu$ of the completed Clifford sheaf are global over $\Sig$, and at each wall point they generate the fibre algebra $\Aa_x$, a $\Mat_2(\R)$-type mode factor. The element $\sigma = k^*k - kk^*$ is a global section with $\sigma^2 = 1$, and $\alpha_x = \operatorname{Ad}(\sigma(x))$ is the fibrewise parity. The ladder bundle $\Aa \to \Sig$ has fibres $\Aa_x$; the even subbundle $\Aa^{+}$ has fibres the parity-fixed algebras $\Aa_x^{+}$; and the metric-level presheaf assigns to each open $U \subseteq \Sig$ the algebra $\mathfrak{M}(U) = \Gamma(U, \Aa^{+})$ of smooth sections, with the restriction maps of sections.
obj.three-routes.ladder-bundle-even-subb.lay: At each point of the wall, the dying direction and its partner generate a small algebra of two-by-two matrices, a ladder that steps between them. Collecting these over the whole wall gives a bundle of algebras. A natural reflection splits each algebra into even and odd parts, and the even parts, assembled smoothly over regions of the wall, define the metric-level presheaf.

history.text: About added from the no-hopping proposition, stated for endomorphisms of the ladder bundle; the T5 appendix assembly has its own definition and keeps that link.

odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-resid.technical:
For the tame wall at $\Lambda = 0$ on the $\Lambda$ line, the rescaling $w_\Lambda \mapsto w_\Lambda/\sqrt{|\Lambda|}$ of the dying direction is proportional, by the factor $\sqrt 3$, to the normalisation $e_V = V/|V|$ of the Stelle-West vector, both normalising the same line. The exceptional algebra is $\Cl(1,3) \perp \langle +\tfrac13\rangle \cong \Cl(2,3)$ from $\Lambda < 0$ and $\Cl(1,3) \perp \langle -\tfrac13\rangle \cong \Cl(1,4)$ from $\Lambda > 0$, the rescaled family being exactly block diagonal. The residue of the inverse form is $-3\,w_0\otimes w_0$, which is the Stelle-West norm $\Lambda\,Q(V) = -3$; the dying direction carries the weight of $|\Lambda|^{1/2}$, and for $\Lambda > 0$ the weightless normalisation $\sqrt{\Lambda/3}$ is the de Sitter rate $H$.

The rung, with its tractor metric of constant signature $(2,4)$, completes the family nondegenerately on both sides with rank one more, the completing direction being the partner $\varphi$ at the wall and the frozen point $I_\Lambda$ away from it. This is a case of a general model in which hyperplanes $\mathrm{span}(f_1, \dots, f_n, u + \tfrac t2 v)$ of $\R^{p,q} \perp H$ are completed on both sides by the fixed $(p+1, q+1)$. There is no conflict with conservation of degeneracy: the complement $\mathrm{span}(I_\Lambda)$ has $Q(I_\Lambda) = \Lambda/3$, which changes sign across the wall, so the completion is not standard in the sense that theorem requires.
odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-resid.lay: Treating the cosmological constant as a dial, the algebra built from the frozen point degenerates exactly when the dial reads zero, and this result describes that degeneration in detail. On the two sides the limiting algebras are the anti-de Sitter and de Sitter ones, and the strength of the blow-up at the wall is fixed by the same number that sets the length of the Stelle-West vector. One fixed six-dimensional space completes the family on both sides. That looks like a clash with a conservation law for degeneracy, but it is not, because the extra direction changes type across the wall, a case the law excludes by hypothesis.
odd-extensions.exceptional-algebra-resid.typing_note: Edges kept as extracted, all used in the proof; the frozen-point fact at Lambda = 0 is named in (ii) only as the identity the pole is one step from, while the proof draws the norm from the other frozen-point fact, so it was not added. Levels pass: conditions already kept; per review item 14 the technical level now writes Q(V) and Q(I_Lambda) for the vector squares.

proofs.main: (i) $V$ is the multiple of $w_{\Lambda}$ with $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.are-ascents-pair-signed}), and $w_{\Lambda}/\sqrt{|\Lambda|}$ has norm $\mp 1/3$, so it is $e_{V}/\sqrt 3$; the rescaled Gram's dying entry is $(-\Lambda/3)/t$ with $t = \mp\Lambda$, and the off-diagonal entries are zero for every $\Lambda$ by Proposition \claimref{odd-extensions.line-tame-wall}(i), so the sheaf paper's limit is attained identically; the signatures are by inspection. (ii) The inverse Gram's dying entry is $-3/\Lambda$, so $\Lambda$ times it is $-3$; the sheaf paper's residue formula gives $\lim \Lambda\, G^{-1} = (1/T)\,w_{0} \otimes w_{0}$ with $T = -1/3$; and $Q(V) = -3/\Lambda$ is Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-frozen-point}. The weight statement is the sheaf paper's reading of $L^{\otimes 2} \cong N^{*}\Sigma$, and $H^{2} = Q(I) = \Lambda/3$ is \cite[Fact~2.5]{ButlerT12} (\claimref{standard-model.imported-frozen-point-dictionary}), the form the Standard-Model paper uses for its $N = M_{P}/H$ \cite[Obs.~7.1]{ButlerT12}. (iii) The rung's metric has signature $(2,4)$ for every $\Lambda$; at $\Lambda = 0$ the five vectors of $I_{0}^{\perp}$ together with $I_{0}$ span only five dimensions, $I_{0}$ being the radical, and the sixth direction is $\varphi$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(i)); for $\Lambda \neq 0$ the sixth direction is $I_{\Lambda}$; the rank count $5 + 1 = 6$ is the projective-to-conformal paper's $m + r$ (Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-minimal-completion-degenerate-algebra-rule}). For the general model, $Q(u + \tfrac{t}{2}v) = t$, the complement is spanned by $u - \tfrac{t}{2}v$ of norm $-t$, and the total is the fixed $(p+1,q+1)$; the $\Lambda$ family is the case $u = I_{0}$, $v = \varphi$ with $\ip{I_{0}}{\varphi} = 1$ and $t = -\Lambda/3$ up to the gauge. (iv) $Q(I_{\Lambda}) = \Lambda/3$ changes sign at the wall; Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue}'s conservation theorem requires $\operatorname{sig} K$ constant across it, and its proof states that the clause is necessary because a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature can match the two sides, which is what happens here. The script verifies (i) to (iv) on the same rational instances: the rescaled dying entries, the two exceptional signatures, $\Lambda\,(G^{-1})_{ww} = -3$ for every $\Lambda \neq 0$, the total signature $(2,4)$ on both sides with the sign of $K$ switching, the five-dimensional span at $\Lambda = 0$, and the signature $(2,4)$ of the Lorentz frame with $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$.

odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-excep.formal: A pair $(M,G)$, $G$ a smooth symmetric form on a bundle over $M$, is a tame corank-one degeneration if (T1) the degenerate locus $\Sigma$ is a smooth closed hypersurface, (T2) the corank is exactly one on $\Sigma$ with the radical lines a smooth line bundle spanned locally by $k$, and (T3) the dying eigenvalue crosses zero at nonzero speed along every transversal, invariantly: the section $\delta(k \otimes k) = dg_{k}|_{\Sigma}$ of $\operatorname{Hom}(L^{\otimes 2}, N^{*}\Sigma)$ is nowhere zero. The signatures on the two sides differ by one unit, $(p,q)$ where the dying eigenvalue is positive against $(p-1, q+1)$. Rescaling the dying direction by $t^{-1/2}$ along a transversal gives a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through the wall whose special fibre, the exceptional algebra, is the Clifford algebra of the surviving form orthogonal to the rate of degeneration, of signature $(p,q)$ on the side approached. The inverse form has a canonical simple pole at the wall whose residue is $\delta^{-1}$, giving $N^{*}\Sigma \cong L^{\otimes 2}$: the dying line is a square root of the conormal bundle and the adjoined partner line a square root of the normal bundle. Conservation, absolute form: for a tame wall with both sides nonempty, any symmetric form on any bundle containing the original, standard outside a neighbourhood of the wall in the sense of being $G \perp K$ there with $K$ nondegenerate of the \emph{same} signature on both exterior regions, degenerates somewhere; the constancy of $\operatorname{sig} K$ across the wall is necessary, a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature being able to match the two sides. \emph{Provenance:} \cite[Hyp.~2.1, Lem.~2.2, Rem.~2.3, Prop.~6.1, Thm.~6.2, Thm.~5.1]{ButlerT4}.
odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-excep.technical:
A smooth symmetric form $G$ on a bundle over $M$ is a tame corank-one degeneration when its degenerate locus $\Sigma$ is a smooth closed hypersurface, the corank there is exactly one with radical lines forming a smooth line bundle $L$ spanned locally by $k$, and the dying eigenvalue crosses zero at nonzero speed, invariantly $\delta(k\otimes k) = dg_k|_\Sigma \neq 0$. The signatures on the two sides are $(p,q)$ and $(p-1,q+1)$. Rescaling the dying direction by $t^{-1/2}$ gives a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras whose special fibre, the exceptional algebra, is the Clifford algebra of the surviving form orthogonal to the rate of degeneration, of signature $(p,q)$ on the side approached. The inverse form has a canonical simple pole with residue $\delta^{-1}$, so $N^*\Sigma \cong L^{\otimes 2}$.

Conservation, absolute form: if both sides are nonempty, any symmetric form on a larger bundle that equals $G \perp K$ away from the wall, with $K$ nondegenerate of the same signature on both exterior regions, degenerates somewhere. The constancy of the signature of $K$ is necessary. Everything here holds for walls satisfying this tameness hypothesis, which the series takes as a premise.
odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-excep.lay: This imports the basic theory of the mildest kind of degeneration, assuming the wall is tame in the series' sense: a geometry that loses exactly one direction along a smooth wall, and does so at a steady rate. On each side the geometry is regular, with one direction changing its sign across the wall, and a suitable rescaling gives a well-defined limiting algebra on the wall. If the wall has regions on both sides, the degeneracy cannot be removed by adding extra directions that look the same on both sides; it reappears somewhere.

odd-extensions.line-tame-wall.technical:
Fix a smooth nowhere-vanishing gauge $a(\Lambda)$ and write the frozen point as $I_\Lambda = aI_0 + b\varphi$ with $2ab = \Lambda/3$; set $w_\Lambda = aI_0 - b\varphi$. Then $I_\Lambda^\perp$ with its induced form is a tame corank-one family over the $\Lambda$ line. In the frame $(e_1, \dots, e_4, w_\Lambda)$ its Gram is $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1,-\Lambda/3)$ for every $\Lambda$ and every gauge, so the degenerate locus is the point $\Lambda = 0$, the radical there is spanned by $I_0$, and the dying eigenvalue $-\Lambda/3$ crosses zero at speed $-\tfrac13$.

The signatures are $(2,3)$ for $\Lambda < 0$ and $(1,4)$ for $\Lambda > 0$, so the wall separates the anti-de Sitter and de Sitter intermediate algebras: a signature-change wall in a parameter rather than in spacetime. The gauge $a = b$ is not smooth at the wall and not defined for $\Lambda < 0$; the scalar invariants do not depend on which smooth gauge is used, but the identification $w_0 = a(0)\,I_0$ does.
odd-extensions.line-tame-wall.lay: If the cosmological constant is treated as a dial, the algebra of directions orthogonal to the frozen point degenerates exactly when the dial reads zero. This result checks that, once the leftover scale freedom is fixed smoothly, the degeneration is of the mildest, well-behaved kind. On the negative side the algebra is the anti-de Sitter one and on the positive side the de Sitter one, so passing through zero flips the sign of one direction, as a signature-changing wall does in spacetime.
odd-extensions.line-tame-wall.typing_note: Added the imported tame-wall fact, whose conditions (T1) to (T3) are what the proposition verifies, and the theorem supplying the null-frame form of the frozen point with 2ab = Lambda/3 that the hypotheses rest on. Levels pass: the lay and one-liner now say tameness needs a smooth dilation gauge.

proofs.main: (i) With $2ab = \Lambda/3$ (Theorem \claimref{odd-extensions.transport-constrains-frozen-point-only-through}(ii)), $Q(w_{\Lambda}) = -2ab = -\Lambda/3$, $\ip{w_{\Lambda}}{I_{\Lambda}} = ab - ab = 0$, and both are orthogonal to the Lorentz frame; the Gram is block diagonal because $I_{0}$ and $\varphi$ are. The radical at $\Lambda = 0$ is spanned by $w_{0} = aI_{0}$. The crossing speed is $d(-\Lambda/3)/d\Lambda = -1/3 \neq 0$, so (T1) to (T3) of Fact \claimref{odd-extensions.imported-tame-walls-exceptional-algebra-residue} hold. (ii) is the sign of $-\Lambda/3$ read against Corollary \claimref{odd-extensions.four-extensions-oriented-pair}. (iii) $a = b = \sqrt{\Lambda/6}$. The script verifies the Gram, the corank at $\Lambda = 0$ only, the gauge independence of the dying eigenvalue, the exact slope $-1/3$ at six nonzero rational values of $\Lambda$, and the two signatures.

sheaf.base-unipotents-wall.formal: For $\lambda \in \ker k := \{v : k(v) = 0\}$ define $g_\lambda(\alpha) := \alpha + \alpha(\lambda)\,k$ on $T^*M$ at the wall point. Then $g_\lambda$ is a $G$-isometry, fixes $k$, and $g_\lambda g_{\lambda'} = g_{\lambda+\lambda'}$; the dual action on vectors is $u' \mapsto u' - k(u')\lambda$, hence on transversals ($k(u') = 1$) the translation $u' \mapsto u' - \lambda$, a free and transitive action of $(\ker k, +)$.
sheaf.base-unipotents-wall.technical: At a wall point let $k$ span the radical of $G$ on $T^*M$. For each vector $\lambda$ with $k(\lambda) = 0$, the map $g_\lambda(\alpha) = \alpha + \alpha(\lambda)\,k$ is a $G$-isometry fixing $k$, and $g_\lambda g_{\lambda'} = g_{\lambda+\lambda'}$. Dually it acts on vectors by $u' \mapsto u' - k(u')\lambda$, so on transversals, the vectors with $k(u') = 1$, it is the translation $u' \mapsto u' - \lambda$, and $(\ker k, +)$ acts on them freely and transitively.
sheaf.base-unipotents-wall.lay: At a point of the wall the geometry cannot see the dying direction, and this gives it extra symmetries: shears that add a multiple of the dying direction to any covector. These shears combine like ordinary addition. Acting on the directions that cross the wall, they move any one crossing direction to any other in exactly one way.
sheaf.base-unipotents-wall.typing_note: Self-contained lemma with no premises; no edges changed.

proofs.main: $G(g_\lambda\alpha, g_\lambda\alpha') = G(\alpha, \alpha')$, every correction term carrying a factor $G(\cdot, k) = 0$, $k$ spanning the radical; $g_\lambda(k) = k + k(\lambda)k = k$; the composition law is immediate. Dually, $(g_\lambda^{-1}\alpha)(u') = \alpha(u') - \alpha(\lambda)k(u') = \alpha(u' - k(u')\lambda)$; freeness and transitivity on transversals are affine-space statements over $\ker k$.

sheaf.basic-properties-operational-chara.formal: $\shW$ is locally free of rank four. Away from $E$ it coincides with the full cotangent module, so nothing in the interior is altered. A $u$-smooth one-form lies in $\shW$ if and only if all four of its components in the infalling orthonormal frame are bounded up to $E$ (the rain characterisation, proved as Proposition \claimref{sheaf.rain-duality}(3)); in particular the module is attached to the geometry and the blow-up, not to the chosen frame. The order two of the quasihomogeneous structure is minimal for $\shW$ to admit a smooth frame, being forced by the half-integer growth of $\beta$: at order one (smooth in $r$) the generator $\rho = r^{1/2}\,dr$ is not smooth.
sheaf.basic-properties-operational-chara.technical: The weighted coframe module $\shW$ is locally free of rank four, and away from the boundary $E$ it coincides with the full cotangent module, so nothing in the interior is altered. A $u$-smooth one-form lies in $\shW$ exactly when its four components in the infalling orthonormal frame are bounded up to $E$, so the module is attached to the geometry and the blow-up, not to the chosen frame. Order two is the least order of the quasihomogeneous structure for which $\shW$ has a smooth frame: at order one the generator $\rho = r^{1/2}\,dr$ is not smooth.
sheaf.basic-properties-operational-chara.lay: This result lists the basic properties of the rescaled set of one-forms used near the Schwarzschild singularity. It has the right size, changes nothing away from the singularity, and can be described without any choice of frame: among the forms smooth in the rescaled sense, it consists exactly of those that freely falling observers measure as finite. Measuring smoothness in the square root of the radius is the least change that makes this work.

sheaf.boundary-units-invert.formal: If $a \in \mathcal{A}$ has every exponent bounded below by some $\delta > 0$ on the relevant compact (so $a = O(\tau^\delta)$ locally uniformly), then $1 + a$ is invertible in $\mathcal{A}$ after shrinking $\varepsilon$: the Neumann series $\sum_{k \geq 0} (-a)^k$ has exponent families adding to $\{k\delta + \cdots\}$, admissible since only finitely many products fall below any level, and it converges locally uniformly where $|a| \leq \tfrac12$. More generally any $c + a$ with $c$ smooth, positive and bounded away from zero near $E$ is invertible in $\mathcal{A}$.
sheaf.boundary-units-invert.technical: Let $a \in \mathcal{A}$ have every exponent bounded below by some $\delta > 0$ on the relevant compact, so that $a = O(\tau^\delta)$ locally uniformly. Then, after shrinking $\varepsilon$, $1 + a$ is invertible in $\mathcal{A}$, with inverse the Neumann series $\sum_{k \geq 0}(-a)^k$: its exponent family is admissible, because only finitely many products fall below any level, and it converges locally uniformly where $|a| \leq \tfrac12$. More generally $c + a$ is invertible whenever $c$ is smooth, positive and bounded away from zero near $E$.
sheaf.boundary-units-invert.lay: In the algebra of functions built from varying powers of time, it matters which elements can be divided by. This result shows that a positive smooth quantity plus a correction that vanishes at the boundary can always be inverted near the boundary. The inverse is given by the usual geometric series.
sheaf.boundary-units-invert.typing_note: Self-contained lemma with no premises; no edges changed.

proofs.main: Admissibility of the summed family: a product of $k$ factors from $a$'s family has exponent at least $k\delta$ on the compact, so for each level $N$ only the terms with $k \leq N/\delta$, finitely many products each, can lie below $N$. Local uniform convergence is the geometric bound. The general case is $c + a = c(1 + a/c)$, with $a/c \in \mathcal{A}$ of the same positive lower order ($1/c$ is smooth up to the boundary).

sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite.formal:
Let $n_\pm := k/\sqrt r \pm \dtPG$. Then, at every interior radius, exactly: $n_\pm$ are $G$-null; they are $\shW_{\mathrm{exc}}$-sections with \emph{constant unit} rain components, $n_\pm(V) = \pm 1$ and $n_\pm(e_{\hat r}) = 1$; and the gauge field of Fact \claimref{sheaf.gauge-field-cometric} carries the flat radial null dyad onto them,
\[
L^{-1}(\dtPG + dr) \;=\; n_+, \qquad L^{-1}(\dtPG - dr) \;=\; -\,n_- ,
\]
where $L$ is the covector action of the gauge field, fixed internally by the identity $\eta(L a, L b) = G(a,b)$ on all coordinate pairs. Hence the s-wave sector's physical null dyad, the radial structure on which the chain of \cite{ButlerT5} runs, is exactly finite in the infalling frame all the way to the wall, even though the individual coordinate legs are not.
sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite.technical: Set $n_\pm = k/\sqrt r \pm \dtPG$. At every interior radius, exactly, the $n_\pm$ are $G$-null sections of $\shW_{\mathrm{exc}}$ with constant unit rain components, $n_\pm(V) = \pm 1$ and $n_\pm(e_{\hat r}) = 1$. The covector action $L$ of the gauge field, fixed by $\eta(La, Lb) = G(a,b)$, carries the flat radial null dyad onto them: $L^{-1}(\dtPG + dr) = n_+$ and $L^{-1}(\dtPG - dr) = -n_-$. So the physical radial null dyad of the s-wave sector, on which the chain runs, is exactly finite in the infalling frame all the way to the wall, although its coordinate legs are not.
sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite.lay: The chain construction for black holes runs along the two light directions pointing inwards and outwards along the radius. This result shows that, as measured by an observer falling freely inwards, these light directions stay exactly finite all the way to the wall, even though the coordinates used to write them blow up. They are precisely the images of the flat-space light directions under the gauge field.
sheaf.chains-radial-dyad-rain-finite.typing_note: Kept rain duality, used for nullity and the components; the gauge-field fact names the map L, but the proof fixes L internally from the identity eta(La, Lb) = G(a, b), so it was not added (doubtful). Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: Nullity: $G(n_\pm, n_\pm) = -1 + 1 = 0$ by Proposition \claimref{sheaf.rain-duality}(2). Components: clause (1) of the duality. The gauge map $L(\dtPG) = \dtPG$, $L(dr) = dr - \beta\,\dtPG$, angular fixed, satisfies $\eta(La, Lb) = G(a,b)$ on all coordinate pairs, which fixes the conventions internally; inverting, $L^{-1}(\dtPG \pm dr) = (1 \pm \beta)\dtPG \pm dr = \pm\bigl(dr + (\beta \pm 1)\dtPG\bigr) = \pm\,n_\pm$. All identities exact, at two masses (the section “Machine verification”).

sheaf.characterisation-forced-within-rai.formal: Within the rain-bounded class the characterisation of $\shW$ is not a choice of definition but a consequence of tameness: every rain-bounded boundary-tame extension is automatically the maximal one. The completion, the ladder pair, and the exceptional algebra of this section are therefore attached to the geometry together with the infalling congruence, whose finiteness class picks the module; Example \claimref{note.sheaf.rain-boundedness-essential-null-mixing-extension} shows some anchoring class must be named.
sheaf.characterisation-forced-within-rai.technical: Within the class of rain-bounded extensions, the characterisation of $\shW$ is a consequence of tameness rather than a choice of definition: every rain-bounded boundary-tame extension equals $\shW$, which is the maximal rain-bounded extension, since rain-boundedness means exactly $\mathcal{M} \subseteq \shW$. Consequently the completion, the ladder pair and the exceptional algebra built on $\shW$ are attached to the geometry together with the infalling congruence, whose finiteness class selects the module; some anchoring class of this kind has to be named.
sheaf.characterisation-forced-within-rai.lay: One might worry that the special set of one-forms used near the singularity was merely a convenient choice. This result shows that, once finiteness for freely falling observers and the mildest kind of degeneration are required, there is no other choice. The structures built from it are therefore fixed by the geometry together with the family of infalling observers.
sheaf.characterisation-forced-within-rai.typing_note: Kept all three premises: uniqueness gives the main step, rain duality the equivalence with inclusion in W, and the one-sided completion theorem the restated clause about the completion. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

sheaf.collision-census.formal: On the constraint variety: (i) triples with a repeated exponent are, up to permutation, exactly $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ and $(0,0,1)$; (ii) if any exponent vanishes the triple is $(0,0,1)$ up to permutation. An exponent cannot cross zero alone: zeros come in pairs.
sheaf.collision-census.technical: On the Kasner constraint variety, $p_1 + p_2 + p_3 = 1$ and $p_1^2 + p_2^2 + p_3^2 = 1$, the triples with a repeated exponent are, up to permutation, exactly $(-\tfrac13, \tfrac23, \tfrac23)$ and $(0,0,1)$, and any triple with a vanishing exponent is $(0,0,1)$ up to permutation. Hence an exponent cannot cross zero alone: zeros come in pairs.
sheaf.collision-census.lay: Kasner geometries near a singularity are labelled by three exponents obeying two fixed relations. This result finds every case in which two exponents coincide: up to reordering there are only two. It also shows that one exponent can never pass through zero on its own; whenever one is zero, another is too.
sheaf.collision-census.typing_note: Self-contained algebra on the Kasner constraints; no edges changed.

sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-f.formal: Let $M$ be connected, let $(M,G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration whose two open sides $\Mp \setminus \Sig$ and $M \setminus \Mp$ are both nonempty, let $E \to M$ be \emph{any} vector bundle containing $T^*M$ as a subbundle, carrying \emph{any} smooth symmetric form $h$ which is \emph{standard} outside some neighbourhood $U$ of $\Sig$ with $M \setminus U$ meeting both sides: there, $h = G \perp K$ for a nondegenerate form $K$ on a complement, with $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ the same on both exterior regions. Then $h$ is not nondegenerate everywhere: every completion of a signature-change cometric that is standard, in this sense, outside a neighbourhood of the wall degenerates somewhere. Degeneracy can be displaced, never destroyed.
sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-f.technical:
Assume $M$ is connected and $(M,G)$ is a tame corank-one degeneration (the tameness premise) whose two open sides are both nonempty. Take any vector bundle $E$ containing $T^*M$, with any smooth symmetric form $h$ that is standard outside a neighbourhood $U$ of $\Sig$ whose complement meets both sides: there $h = G \perp K$ with $K$ nondegenerate and $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ the same on both exterior regions. Then $h$ is degenerate somewhere.

The argument is a signature count. A continuous nondegenerate symmetric form on a connected base has constant signature. On the physical exterior $h$ has signature $(p,q) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$, and on the far exterior $(p-1,q+1) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$; these differ, so nondegeneracy must fail somewhere in $U$. The requirement that $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ agree on the two exterior regions is essential: a $K$ allowed to change signature across the wall could make up the difference.
sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-f.lay: When a geometry changes signature across a wall, one can try to repair the wall by placing it inside a larger structure. Assuming the wall is tame (the mildest kind of degeneration), the space is connected and there is geometry on both sides, this result shows that any such repair which looks standard away from the wall, with the same kind of extra piece on both sides, must itself break down somewhere. The breakdown can be moved, but not removed.
sheaf.conservation-degeneracy-absolute-f.typing_note: The statement assumes a tame corank-one degeneration, so the tameness postulate goes in assumes; the proof is a self-contained signature count and needs no other premise. Levels pass: the lay level now states the tameness premise, connectedness, both sides nonempty and the same complement signature on both sides, which it had dropped; the technical and one-liner now mark tameness as an assumption.

proofs.main: The signature of a continuous nondegenerate symmetric form on a connected base is constant: the eigenvalues of its Gram matrix with respect to any auxiliary frame metric vary continuously and never vanish, so their sign counts are locally constant, and $M$ is connected. Suppose $h$ nondegenerate everywhere. On the physical exterior $h = G \perp K$ has signature $(p,q) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$; on the far exterior it has $(p{-}1, q{+}1) + \operatorname{sig}(K)$ (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}, the wall being tame, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), with the \emph{same} $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ by the standardness hypothesis. The two totals differ in the first entry by one; a single form of constant signature cannot have both, so nondegeneracy must fail somewhere in $U$. The constancy clause on $\operatorname{sig}(K)$ is necessary: $M \setminus U$ is disconnected (the two sides lie in different components of $M \setminus \Sig$), and a completion allowed to switch $K$'s signature across the wall, say from $(1,1)$ to $(2,0)$, could match the two totals; ``standard'' means one exterior model, not two.
