sheaf.degeneration-sheaf.formal:
Let $(M, G)$ be a tame corank-one degeneration (Hypotheses \claimref{sheaf.tameness}), $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$, and write $A(x)$ for the fibre at $x$. Then:
\begin{enumerate}
\item Over $\Mo$, each fibre $A(x)$ is isomorphic to the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature; on the interior of $\Mp$ this is $\Cl(p,q)$, on the far side $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$. In the physical case these are $\Cl(1,3) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$ and $\Cl(0,4) \cong \Mat_2(\HH)$.
\item Over $x \in \Sig$, the two-sided ideal $J(x)$ of $A(x)$ generated by the radical line $\shL(x)$ is
\[
J(x) \;=\; A(x)\,k \;=\; k\,A(x), \qquad J(x)^2 = 0, \qquad \dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1},
\]
for any spanning $k \in \shL(x)$, and the quotient is canonically the Clifford algebra of the induced form:
\[
A(x)/J(x) \;\cong\; \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM / \shL(x),\ \overline{G}_x\bigr),
\]
where $\overline{G}_x$ is nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.
\item The fibrewise ideals assemble: the multiplication map $\shA|_\Sig \otimes \shL \to \shA|_\Sig$ has image a smooth subbundle $\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL$ of rank $2^{n-1}$, and its pushforward
\[
\shJ \;:=\; i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr) \qquad (i : \Sig \hookrightarrow M)
\]
is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules, supported exactly on $\Sig$, with fibre $J(x)$ at $x \in \Sig$ and fibre $0$ elsewhere. The associated ideal sheaf of $\shA$ is the kernel
\[
\shK \;:=\; \ker\bigl(\shA \longrightarrow i_*\bigl(\shA|_\Sig \,/\, \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL\bigr)\bigr),
\]
a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ whose restriction to $\Sig$ realises $J(x)$ fibrewise and whose quotient $\shA/\shK$ is the pushforward of the quotient bundle of (2).
\end{enumerate}
sheaf.degeneration-sheaf.technical:
Assume $(M, G)$ is a corank-one degeneration satisfying the tameness hypotheses, with wall $\Sig$ and $\shA = \Cl(T^*M, G)$. Off the wall each fibre is the nondegenerate Clifford algebra of the local signature: $\Cl(p,q)$ on the physical side and $\Cl(p{-}1,q{+}1)$ beyond the wall, both $\Mat_2(\HH)$ in the physical case. At $x \in \Sig$ a spanning radical covector $k$ anticommutes with every covector, so $k\,a = \hat a\,k$ for the grade involution, and the two-sided ideal it generates is $J(x) = A(x)\,k = k\,A(x)$, with $J(x)^2 = 0$ and $\dim_\R J(x) = 2^{n-1}$. The quotient is canonically $A(x)/J(x) \cong \Cl\bigl(T^*_xM/\shL(x), \overline{G}_x\bigr)$, nondegenerate of rank $n-1$ and signature $(p{-}1, q)$.

These fibrewise ideals form a smooth subbundle of rank $2^{n-1}$ over $\Sig$. Its pushforward $\shJ$ is a finitely presented sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules and of $\shA$-bimodules supported exactly on $\Sig$, and the kernel $\shK$ of restriction to $\Sig$ followed by projection is a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$ realising $J(x)$ fibrewise on $\Sig$, with quotient $\shA/\shK$ the pushforward of the quotient bundle.
sheaf.degeneration-sheaf.lay: Where the geometry degenerates along a wall, assuming it does so in the controlled way the paper calls tame (one direction losing its length, transversally, along a smooth wall), the algebra attached to each point changes character. Away from the wall it is an ordinary Clifford algebra. On the wall, the direction that has lost its length generates a part of the algebra whose products all vanish, an infinitesimal part of exactly half the size, and removing it leaves a smaller ordinary Clifford algebra. These parts fit together smoothly along the wall into a well-behaved algebraic object living only on the wall.

proofs.main:
(1) Over $\Mo$ the form is nondegenerate; diagonalising at $x$ gives $A(x) \cong \Cl(p', q')$ for the local signature $(p', q')$, which is $(p,q)$ on the physical side and $(p{-}1, q{+}1)$ across the wall (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}). The named isomorphisms are Fact \claimref{sheaf.imported-classification-values} (the coincidence of the two is the fusion phenomenon of \cite[Ex.~5.10]{ButlerT1}, both being ascents of $\Cl(0,3) \cong \HH \oplus \HH$; it plays no role here).

(2) Since $k$ spans the radical, $G_x(k, \alpha) = 0$ for \emph{every} $\alpha \in T^*_xM$, so $k$ anticommutes with every covector: $k\alpha + \alpha k = 2\,G_x(k,\alpha) = 0$ (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}). Hence for every $a \in A(x)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:kcommutation}
k\,a \;=\; \hat{a}\,k ,
\end{equation}
with $\hat{\cdot}$ the grade involution (the commutation rule \claimref{primer.commutation-rule}, for a $k$ orthogonal to everything): on a product of generators, $k\,(\alpha_1 \cdots \alpha_j) = (-1)^j (\alpha_1 \cdots \alpha_j)\, k = \widehat{\alpha_1 \cdots \alpha_j}\; k$ by $j$ anticommutations, and both sides of \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf} are linear in $a$ (nondegeneracy plays no role). The fibre statements of (2) are the case $r = 1$ of Theorem \claimref{std-algebra.radical-ideal-and-quotient}: its part (i) gives $J(x) = Ak = kA$ of dimension $2^{n} - 2^{n-1}$, its part (ii) gives $J(x)^{2} = 0$, and its part (iii) gives the quotient, the projection onto $T^*_xM/\shL(x)$ extending to a surjective homomorphism with kernel exactly $J(x)$. In the notation used below: $A k = k A$, and this common set is a two-sided ideal containing $k$; conversely any two-sided ideal containing $k$ contains $Ak$, so $J(x) = Ak$. It squares to zero:
\[
J(x)^2 \;=\; A\,k\,A\,k \;=\; A\,\hat{A}\,k^2 \;=\; 0 ,
\]
by \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf} and $k^2 = G_x(k,k) = 0$. For the dimension, choose a complement $V_1 \subset T^*_xM$ of $\shL(x)$ and take a basis of $V_1$ together with $k$; ordering $k$ last, the blade basis of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} splits $A(x) = \Cl'(V_1) \oplus \Cl'(V_1)\,k$, where $\Cl'(V_1)$ denotes the span of the blades in the $V_1$-letters (a subalgebra, since $V_1$ is closed under the rewriting against itself). Then $Ak = \Cl'(V_1)\,k$, of dimension $2^{n-1}$: indeed $(\,b\,k\,)k = \pm b k^2 = 0$ for $b \in \Cl'(V_1)$, so the $\Cl'(V_1)k$-part of $A$ contributes nothing new, and left multiplication by elements of $\Cl'(V_1)$ preserves $\Cl'(V_1)k$.

For the quotient: the projection $\pi : T^*_xM \to T^*_xM/\shL(x)$ intertwines $G_x$ with a well-defined form $\overline{G}_x$ ($G_x(\alpha + k, \beta + k') = G_x(\alpha, \beta)$ for $k, k'$ radical), which is nondegenerate of rank $n - 1$: any $\alpha$ with $\overline{G}_x(\bar\alpha, \cdot) = 0$ has $G_x(\alpha, \cdot) = 0$, hence $\alpha \in \shL(x)$, hence $\bar\alpha = 0$. Its signature is $(p{-}1, q)$: on the physical side the full form diagonalises with entries $(+^{p}, -^{q})$ degenerating so that one $+$ goes to zero on $\Sig$ (the dying eigenvalue is positive there, Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}), leaving $(p{-}1, q)$ on the quotient by continuity of the nondegenerate block. The composite $T^*_xM \xrightarrow{\pi} T^*_xM/\shL(x) \hookrightarrow \Cl(T^*_xM/\shL(x), \overline{G}_x)$ satisfies the Clifford relation for $G_x$, so by the universal property (\claimref{std-algebra.existence-uniqueness}) it extends to a surjective algebra map $\Pi : A(x) \to \Cl(\overline{G}_x)$ (surjective because the generators are in the image). Its kernel contains $k$, hence contains the two-sided ideal $J(x)$; and by dimensions the containment is equality:
\[
\dim A(x) - \dim J(x) \;=\; 2^n - 2^{n-1} \;=\; 2^{n-1} \;=\; \dim \Cl(\overline{G}_x),
\]
using Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} on the quotient form. So $A(x)/J(x) \cong \Cl(\overline{G}_x)$, canonically ($\Pi$ used no choices).

(3) Working locally on $\Sig$, choose a spanning section $k$ of $\shL$ (a smooth line subbundle by \claimref{sheaf.tameness}) and a local frame of $T^*M|_\Sig$ completing it; the sections $\{e_I\, k : k \notin e_I\}$ ($2^{n-1}$ of them, the blades in the complementary letters times $k$) are smooth and pointwise a basis of $J(x)$ by (2), so the image of the multiplication map is a smooth subbundle of rank $2^{n-1}$, independent of the choices (the fibre $J(x)$ is choice-free). Its pushforward $\shJ$ is finitely presented: locally, with $\tau$ a defining function of $\Sig$, the presentation $\mathcal{O}^{2^{n-1}} \xrightarrow{\ \tau\ } \mathcal{O}^{2^{n-1}} \to \shJ \to 0$ exhibits it (sections of the bundle over $U \cap \Sig$ are smooth functions modulo those vanishing on $\Sig$, componentwise in the displayed frame). It is supported exactly on $\Sig$, since its stalks vanish off $\Sig$ and are nonzero on it, and it is an $\shA$-bimodule because each fibre is a two-sided ideal and the module operations are the restrictions of the smooth multiplication of $\shA$. For $\shK$: the map $\shA \to i_*(\shA|_\Sig / \shA|_\Sig \cdot \shL)$ (restrict to $\Sig$, then project) is a morphism of $\shA$-bimodules, since each fibre quotient is a quotient by a two-sided ideal; its kernel is therefore a sheaf of two-sided ideals of $\shA$, its sections over $U$ are exactly the sections of $\shA$ whose restriction to $U \cap \Sig$ lies in the subbundle, and the stated fibre and quotient identifications follow from (2).

sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expan.formal:
On the collar minus $\Sig$ (where $G$ is invertible), set
\[
s \;:=\; G^{-1}(e, e) \qquad (e = \text{evaluation at } u) .
\]
Then, in any local frame of $T^*M$ extended by $(\nO, \nInf)$:
\begin{enumerate}
\item the Schur complement of the $G$-block in the Gram matrix of $h$ is
\[
\begin{pmatrix} 0 & -1 \\ -1 & 0 \end{pmatrix} - \beta^2 s \begin{pmatrix} \nu^2 & \mu\nu \\ \mu\nu & \mu^2 \end{pmatrix},
\qquad \det = -\bigl(1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s\bigr),
\]
and hence, exactly,
\[
\det h \;=\; \det G \cdot \bigl(-\bigl(1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s\bigr)\bigr) ;
\]
\item along any transversal with parameter $\tau$ as in Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed},
\[
s \;=\; \frac{1}{\lambda} + O(1),
\]
with the $O(1)$ term locally uniform on the collar. In particular $s \to +\infty$ on the side where $\lambda > 0$ and $s \to -\infty$ on the side where $\lambda < 0$, as the wall is approached.
\end{enumerate}

sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expan.lay: The enlarged geometry built around a degenerating wall has a determinant that factorises exactly into the original determinant times a simple correction factor. sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-co.technical:
Let $\mathcal{A}$ be the variable-order algebra of powers $\tau^{e(x)}$ with smooth exponents and $\mathcal{A}^{\log}$ its log completion. Then $\mathcal{A}^{\log}$ is a commutative algebra containing $\mathcal{A}$, stable under $\tau\partial_\tau$ and all tangential vector fields, so it contains the differential closure of $\mathcal{A}$, which is strictly larger than $\mathcal{A}$ once an exponent is nonconstant. $N$ tangential derivatives raise the log degree by at most $N$, with top log coefficient $(e')^N$ on $\tau^{e}$, while radial derivatives do not raise it.

No operation of the calculus lowers the exponent set, so every element is conormal: $V_1 \cdots V_k a = O(\tau^{e_{\min}(x) - \varepsilon})$ locally uniformly, for b-vector fields $V_i$ and every $\varepsilon > 0$. The log-free part with locally constant exponents is the smooth-coefficient polyhomogeneous ring of Melrose, and $\mathcal{A}$ is the log-degree-zero part: a subalgebra, but a module over the calculus only when the exponents are locally constant.
sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-co.lay: Functions that behave like a power of the distance to a boundary, with the power allowed to vary from point to point, form a natural algebra. Differentiating along the boundary produces logarithms, so the algebra has to be enlarged to include them. This result shows that the enlarged algebra is closed under all the relevant derivatives, that the logarithms build up in a controlled way, and that no element grows faster at the boundary than its powers allow.

sheaf.edge-wall.formal:
Let the exponents of strict diagonal data vary smoothly on the constraint variety.
\begin{enumerate}
\item \emph{Positive-pair collisions are interior to the theory.} A collision $p_2 = p_3$ occurs only on the orbit of the Schwarzschild triple, Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data} admits it, and Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} holds across it verbatim. The rational identity $p(1/u) = (p_1, p_3, p_2)(u)$ of the classical parametrisation exhibits the collision as the fixed locus of the positive-pair exchange, fixed point $u = 1$.
\item \emph{Ordering changes force Taub edges.} If the negative exponent changes axis across a locus $Z \subset E$, then on $Z$ the triple is the Taub triple: by the census, the exponent crossing zero forces a second exponent to zero with it. On the witness curve $q(v) := \bigl(-v,\, v(1+v),\, 1+v\bigr)/(1+v+v^2)$, which lies on the variety identically in $v$, axis $1$ is the dying axis for $v > 0$, axis $2$ for $v < 0$, $q(0)$ is the Taub triple, and $q_1q_2 = -v^2(1+v)/(1+v+v^2)^2$: the two crossing exponents vanish jointly to second order at the edge.
\item \emph{The wall ends on the edge.} On each side of $Z$ (each \emph{chamber}) the forced weights and the entire package of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} hold with the chamber's own dying axis; the dying order $d = -2p_{\min}$ obeys the exact identity
\[
d(1) - d(u) \;=\; \frac{2(u-1)^2}{3(1+u+u^2)},
\]
so it is \emph{maximal}, $d = \tfrac23$, exactly at the Schwarzschild triple, and tends to zero at the edge. On $Z$ itself the weighted Gram is $\operatorname{diag}(1,-c_1,-c_2,-c_3)$: nondegenerate Lorentzian, corank zero. The radical line bundle has rank one on the chambers and rank zero on $Z$ (the degeneration sheaf itself keeps its constant rank sixteen, by Proposition \claimref{sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank}; it is its ideal that vanishes): the wall ends on the edge, and no completion is needed there.
\item \emph{No module crosses the edge.} The two chamber modules coincide on $Z$, both weight assignments degenerating to $(0,0,0,1)$, but they are isomorphic over no neighbourhood of an edge point: the transition between them is diagonal with entries $\tau^{p_1}$ and $\tau^{-p_2}$, whose exponents are both negative on a chamber, so it is a unit over $\mathcal{A}$ on neither side. The forced weights jump as axis labels across $Z$; the invariant object is the wall complex of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.mixmaster-wall-complex}.
\end{enumerate}
sheaf.edge-wall.technical:
Let the exponents of strict diagonal Kasner data vary smoothly on the constraint variety. A collision $p_2 = p_3$ of the positive pair happens only on the orbit of the Schwarzschild triple, which the theory admits, and the variable-weight package holds across it. If the negative exponent changes axis across a locus $Z$, then on $Z$ the triple is the Taub triple $(0,0,1)$, because an exponent cannot cross zero alone. On each side of $Z$ (each chamber) the forced weights and the completion hold with that chamber's dying axis, and the dying order $d = -2p_{\min}$ satisfies $d(1) - d(u) = 2(u-1)^2 / (3(1+u+u^2))$, so it is maximal, $d = \tfrac23$, exactly at the Schwarzschild triple and tends to zero at the edge.

On $Z$ the weighted Gram is $\operatorname{diag}(1,-c_1,-c_2,-c_3)$, nondegenerate Lorentzian: the radical line has rank one on the chambers and rank zero on $Z$, so the wall ends there and needs no completion, while the degeneration sheaf keeps its constant rank. The two chamber modules coincide on $Z$ but are isomorphic over no neighbourhood of an edge point, since the transition between them has entries $\tau^{p_1}$ and $\tau^{-p_2}$, both with negative exponent on a chamber.
sheaf.edge-wall.lay: In an anisotropic singularity of the simplest, strictly diagonal kind, the rates at which different directions shrink can vary smoothly from place to place. Where two rates meet, either nothing special happens, or the wall of degeneration simply stops: on that edge the geometry is non-degenerate and needs no repair. On either side the repair works as before, but the two descriptions cannot be glued together across the edge.

Levels pass: lay and one-liner now keep the strict diagonal class.

proofs.main: (1) is the census (\claimref{sheaf.collision-census}) plus the admission of equality in Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data}; the parametrisation identity and its fixed point are exact rational arithmetic. (2) is the census applied along the change, with every stated property of $q(v)$ an exact rational-function identity in $v$; note $q(\tfrac12)$ is the $u=2$ triple and $q(-\tfrac14)$ is the $u=3$ triple with axes $1,2$ exchanged, so the curve traverses genuine Kasner data on both sides. (3) The proof of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} used the ordering only to name the dying axis, so it applies on each chamber with the axes relabelled; the script verifies the full relabelled package on the $v<0$ chamber at $q(-\tfrac14)$: forced weights $(0,q_1,0,q_3)$, weighted Gram $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-\varrho',-1)$ with $\varrho' = \tau^{-2q_2}$, boundary corank one with radical on axis $2$, coupling determinant $1+\varrho'$, completion signature $(2,4)$ with no shadow wall, and the two weight-forcing solves. On $Z$ the weights $(0,0,0,1)$ rescale only the third axis and the four Gram entries are read off directly; the signature $(1,3,0)$ is checked at two unit choices, while the degeneration sheaf keeps its rank sixteen there by \claimref{sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank}. (4) The coincidence and the two negative transition exponents are exact evaluations on the curve.

sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-no.formal: Fix $x \in \Sig$ and a transversal curve through $x$ with parameter $t$, so that $G(t) = G_0 + t\dot G + O(t^2)$ with radical of $G_0$ spanned by $k$ and $\dot G(k,k) \neq 0$ by (T3). Rescale anisotropically: fix a complement $V_1$ of the radical and send $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$. Then the rescaled forms converge as $t \to 0^+$ to the nondegenerate form $\hat G := G_0|_{V_1} \perp \dot G(k,k)$ on $V_1 \oplus \R k$: the cross terms are suppressed by $\sqrt{t}$, and the dying direction re-enters with its rate of degeneration as its metric coefficient. On the physical side the limit has signature $(p, q)$. The rescaled Clifford family is therefore a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through $t = 0$, and its special fibre $\shE(x) := \Cl(V_1 \oplus \R k, \hat G)$, the \emph{exceptional algebra} at $x$, is independent of the choice of complement and of the scales of $k$ and $t$ up to canonical isomorphism.
sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-no.technical:
At a wall point $x$, take a transversal curve with $G(t) = G_0 + t\dot G + O(t^2)$, the radical of $G_0$ spanned by $k$ and $\dot G(k,k) \neq 0$ by the transversality condition (T3) of the tameness premise. Fix a complement $V_1$ of the radical and rescale $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$. As $t \to 0^+$ the rescaled forms converge to the nondegenerate form $\hat G = G_0|_{V_1} \perp \dot G(k,k)$: the cross terms are $O(\sqrt t)$, and the dying direction returns with its rate of degeneration as its coefficient. On the physical side $\hat G$ has signature $(p,q)$.

So the rescaled Clifford algebras form a continuous family of nondegenerate algebras through $t = 0$, whose special fibre is the exceptional algebra $\shE(x) = \Cl(V_1 \oplus \R k, \hat G)$. Up to canonical isomorphism it does not depend on the complement, on the scale of $k$ or on the scale of $t$.
sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-no.lay: Assume the wall is tame, so that at the wall one direction of the geometry loses its length at a nonzero rate. If that direction is stretched at exactly the right rate as the wall is approached, the geometry has a well-behaved, non-degenerate limit. The algebra of this limit, the exceptional algebra, depends only on the wall point and not on the choices made to build it.
sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-no.typing_note: Both edges are real premises (the signature of the complement block and the polynomial structure constants); the statement invokes the transversality condition of tameness, so the tameness postulate was added to assumes. Levels pass: all three levels now state the tameness premise (its transversality condition (T3)), which the lay and one-liner had dropped.

proofs.main:
Compute the Gram matrix of the rescaled frame $(v_1, \dots, v_{n-1}, k/\sqrt{t})$, $v_i$ a basis of $V_1$, against $G(t)$:
\[
G(t)(v_i, v_j) = G_0(v_i,v_j) + t\dot G(v_i,v_j) + O(t^2) \;\longrightarrow\; G_0(v_i,v_j) ;
\]
\[
G(t)(v_i, k/\sqrt{t}) = \frac{G_0(v_i,k) + t\dot G(v_i,k) + O(t^2)}{\sqrt{t}} = \frac{0 + O(t)}{\sqrt{t}} = O(\sqrt{t}) \;\longrightarrow\; 0 ,
\]
using $G_0(v_i, k) = 0$ ($k$ is radical for $G_0$);
\[
G(t)(k/\sqrt{t},\, k/\sqrt{t}) = \frac{G_0(k,k) + t\dot G(k,k) + O(t^2)}{t} = \dot G(k,k) + O(t) \;\longrightarrow\; \dot G(k,k) \neq 0 .
\]
The inequality is (T3) of \claimref{sheaf.tameness}. The limit Gram is block-diagonal: $G_0|_{V_1}$, nondegenerate of signature $(p{-}1,q)$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}(2), via $V_1 \cong T^*_xM/\shL$), plus the $1 \times 1$ block $\dot G(k,k)$, positive on the physical side (Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed}); so $\hat G$ is nondegenerate of signature $(p,q)$ there. All rescaled Gram entries are continuous functions of $\sqrt{t}$ on $[0, \varepsilon)$, and by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} the structure constants of the corresponding Clifford algebras are polynomial in them: the rescaled Clifford family is continuous through $t = 0$, with nondegenerate special fibre $\shE(x)$.

Independence. Changing the complement, $v \mapsto v + c(v)k$: the $V_1$-block entries change by $c(v)G_0(k, w) + c(w)G_0(v,k) + c(v)c(w)G_0(k,k) + O(t) = O(t)$, and the cross terms remain $O(\sqrt t)$, so the limit is unchanged, and the two limit forms are literally equal under the isomorphism $v + \R k \mapsto v' + \R k$ of $V_1 \oplus \R k$ with $V_1' \oplus \R k$ fixing $k$ and matching complements through the quotient $T^*_xM/\shL$. Rescaling $k \mapsto ck$ multiplies the diagonal limit entry by $c^2$ and the generator by $c$: the map $v_i \mapsto v_i$, $k \mapsto ck$ is an isometry of the two limit forms, inducing a canonical isomorphism of the Clifford algebras. Reparametrising $t \mapsto at$ ($a > 0$) multiplies $\dot G$ by $a$ and the rescaled generator $k/\sqrt{t}$ by $1/\sqrt{a}$; the two effects compose to the isometry $k \mapsto k/\sqrt a$ against the $a$-fold entry, again canonical. In each case the displayed isometry is built from the change of data alone, with no further choices, and the isomorphism of Clifford algebras it induces by functoriality is the canonical identification meant in the statement. (Uniqueness among all isometries fixing the $V_1$-part fails, $k \mapsto -k$ being another; canonicality here means choice-freeness of the displayed maps, not uniqueness.)

sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant.formal: A change of boundary defining function within the smooth category, $\tau = \zeta(x,\sigma)\,\sigma$ with $\zeta$ smooth positive (the letter avoiding both the Kasner parameter $u$ and the section “The Schwarzschild composite”'s $u = \sqrt r$), carries $\tau^{e(x)}$ to $\zeta^{e}\sigma^{e(x)}$ with $\zeta^{e} = \exp(e\log \zeta)$ a smooth positive unit: the exponent functions are invariants of the smooth collar structure. Allowing quasi-homogeneous reparametrisations $\tau = \zeta(x,\sigma)\,\sigma^{a(x)}$, $a$ smooth positive, the exponents, assumed strictly positive where a reparametrisation is attempted, rescale by $a(x)$ and the \emph{ratios} $e_i/e_j$ are the absolute invariants. Consequently the strict diagonal data of Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.variable-order-algebra-strict-diagonal-data} admits a presentation with locally constant exponents if and only if all ratios $p_i/p_j$ are locally constant; on the Kasner constraint variety the ratio $-p_1/p_2 = u/(1+u)$ is strictly increasing in the Kasner parameter, so this happens exactly where $u$ is locally constant. For genuinely varying exponents the logarithms of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-conormality} are unavoidable: the variable-order structure is not a reparametrised constant-order structure.
sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant.technical:
A smooth change of boundary defining function, $\tau = \zeta\sigma$ with $\zeta$ smooth and positive, turns $\tau^{e(x)}$ into $\zeta^{e}\sigma^{e(x)}$ with $\zeta^{e}$ a smooth positive unit, so the exponent functions are invariants of the smooth collar structure. Under quasi-homogeneous changes $\tau = \zeta\sigma^{a(x)}$, with $a$ smooth and positive and the exponents strictly positive where this is attempted, the exponents scale by $a(x)$ and the ratios $e_i/e_j$ are the absolute invariants.

Hence strict diagonal data admit a presentation with locally constant exponents exactly when all ratios $p_i/p_j$ are locally constant. On the Kasner constraint variety $-p_1/p_2 = u/(1+u)$ is strictly increasing in the Kasner parameter $u$, so this happens exactly where $u$ is locally constant. For genuinely varying exponents the logarithms of the differential closure cannot be removed by reparametrisation.
sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant.lay: The rates at which directions shrink near a boundary depend on how the distance to the boundary is measured. Changing the measuring function in natural ways can stretch all the rates by a common factor but, provided the rates are positive, cannot change their ratios. So if the ratios genuinely vary from place to place, as they do for Kasner-type data wherever the Kasner parameter varies, no choice of coordinates makes the rates constant, and the logarithms they cause are unavoidable.
sheaf.exponent-ratios-are-invariant.typing_note: Added the differential-closure theorem, since the final clause that the logarithms are unavoidable rests on it; the Kasner parametrisation used for the ratio is classical arithmetic with no store claim to cite. Levels pass: the lay level and one-liner now keep the assumption that the exponents are strictly positive and the restriction to the Kasner constraint variety.

proofs.main: $\log \zeta$ is smooth since $\zeta$ is smooth and positive, so $\zeta^{e}$ is a smooth positive unit and the two transformation laws are read off $\tau^{e} = \zeta^{e}\sigma^{ae}$. Ratio invariance is $(a e_i)/(a e_j) = e_i/e_j$. To make one exponent $e$ locally constant requires $a = c/e$, well defined by the strict positivity of $e$, and then every other exponent becomes $c\,e_i/e$: locally constant iff the ratios are. The Kasner ratio and its strict monotonicity are exact rational arithmetic, checked in the script together with the separation statement: the ratio $p_1/p_2$ takes distinct values at distinct parameter values, so a nonconstant $u(x)$ forces nonconstant ratios. The final clause is \claimref{sheaf.differential-closure-filtration-conormality}(1) applied to the nonconstant exponents this leaves.

sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructi.technical:
Every construction of the sheaf framework (the degeneration sheaf and its ideal, the coupling and ambient form, the one-sided completion, the ladder pair, the exceptional rescaling and the weighted module) is obtained from the input data by operations that are linear over $C^\infty$ of the base, and none differentiates a coefficient function. This class of operations is closed under composition, sums and multiplication by functions, tensor operations and Clifford multiplication, and passage to the submodules and quotients the constructions form, so every composite of the constructions stays in the class.

Consequently every endomorphism supplied by the constructions is $C^\infty$-linear and hence tensorial: a bundle map, and on a line bundle multiplication by a function. The statement concerns only the endomorphisms the constructions supply; an arbitrary endomorphism of a bundle they build, such as a differential operator on its sections, need not be $C^\infty$-linear.
sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructi.lay: All the objects built in this paper are assembled point by point, without differentiating the input functions. This property survives every way the pieces are combined. As a result, any map these constructions produce acts point by point, which is what lets them be carried over unchanged to data that vary from place to place.
sheaf.function-linearity-tame-constructi.typing_note: Kept the blade-basis edge; the four context references name the constructions that are inspected rather than results the proof relies on, so they were not added. Levels pass: the lay said 'in this framework', wider than the paper's own constructions the formal quantifies over; it now says 'in this paper'.

proofs.main:
(1) By inspection of each construction. The ideal $J = \shA k$ is generated by multiplication; the coupling $\kappa$ and the ambient form $h$ are built pointwise from $G$, $k$, $u$, $\beta$, $\mu$, $\nu$ by tensor operations; the Clifford algebra of a quadratic module is a functor (\claimref{std-algebra.functoriality}) applied fibrewise, and Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included} shows its blade frames are frames over $C^\infty$; the ladder pair is a pair of sections of the ambient module; the exceptional rescaling multiplies sections by powers of a defining function; and the weighted module is spanned over $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$ by named one-forms. No derivative of a coefficient function enters at any stage: derivatives appear in this paper only in the analysis of the log obstruction (the section “The smooth structure of the variable-order algebra”), which concerns the function algebra, not the constructions over it.

(2) Composition: $(D \circ D')(fs) = D(fD's) = f(D \circ D')(s)$. Sums and function multiples: immediate. Tensor operations: a $C^\infty$-bilinear pairing of $C^\infty$-linear data induces a $C^\infty$-linear map on the tensor product over $C^\infty$; Clifford multiplication is $C^\infty$-bilinear because the structure constants in a blade frame are functions of the Gram entries (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.blade-basis-degenerate-forms-included}). Submodules and quotients: a $C^\infty$-linear map preserving a $C^\infty$-submodule restricts and descends $C^\infty$-linearly, and each named submodule (the ideal, the even part, $\shW$) is $C^\infty$-spanned, so preservation is checked on spanning sections.

(3) A $C^\infty$-linear endomorphism $D$ of a bundle is tensorial: if $s(x) = 0$ then locally $s = \sum_i f_i t_i$ with $f_i(x) = 0$ and so $(Ds)(x) = \sum_i f_i(x)(Dt_i)(x) = 0$, whence $(Ds)(x)$ depends only on $s(x)$ and $D$ is a bundle map; on a line bundle a bundle map is multiplication by a function. That the quantifier cannot be widened is shown by any nonzero derivation: $d$ composed with a contraction is an endomorphism of sections that differentiates coefficients, and nothing in this paper constructs one.

sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles.formal: A real line bundle is trivial exactly when its first Stiefel-Whitney class vanishes; $w_1$ is additive under tensor product of line bundles, so the square of any real line bundle has $w_1 = 0$; and a hypersurface is two-sided exactly when its normal bundle is trivial. \emph{Provenance:} classical bundle theory, \cite[\S 4]{MilnorStasheff1974}.
sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles.technical: A classical fact from bundle theory: a real line bundle is trivial exactly when its first Stiefel-Whitney class $w_1$ vanishes; $w_1$ is additive under tensor product of line bundles, so $w_1(\ell \otimes \ell) = 2w_1(\ell) = 0$ for every real line bundle $\ell$; and a hypersurface is two-sided exactly when its normal bundle is trivial. It is imported from the standard treatment of characteristic classes by Milnor and Stasheff.
sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles.lay: A line bundle attaches a line to every point of a space, and it may twist like a M\"obius band. A single invariant, the first Stiefel-Whitney class, detects whether it twists. Two twists cancel, so the square of any line bundle is untwisted, and a surface inside a space has two distinct sides exactly when its normal lines do not twist.

imported_from.citation: J. W. Milnor and J. D. Stasheff, Characteristic Classes, Annals of Mathematics Studies 76, Princeton University Press (1974).

sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles.typing_note: Imported classical fact with no derivation; only the levels were written. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence.formal: Let $\Sig$ be compact. For good couplings at every stage, there is an infinite sequence $\Sig = \Sig^{(0)}, \Sig^{(1)} = \Sig', \Sig^{(2)}, \dots$ of tame walls, each displaced from the last into the unphysical region, carrying Clifford sheaves of ranks $2^n, 2^{n+2}, 2^{n+4}, \dots$ whose physical-side fibres ascend the Witt tower $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1) \to \Cl(p{+}2,q{+}2) \to \cdots$, one Rule-1 rung per wall. Degeneracy is conserved along the entire sequence: each completion resolves its wall and produces the next, displaced successively further from the physical region.
sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence.technical:
Let $\Sig$ be compact and choose a good coupling at every stage. Then there is an infinite sequence of tame walls $\Sig = \Sig^{(0)}, \Sig^{(1)} = \Sig', \Sig^{(2)}, \dots$, each displaced from the last into the unphysical region, carrying Clifford sheaves of ranks $2^n, 2^{n+2}, 2^{n+4}, \dots$ whose physical-side fibres ascend the Witt tower $\Cl(p,q) \to \Cl(p+1,q+1) \to \Cl(p+2,q+2) \to \cdots$, one rung per wall.

The proof iterates the wall induction. Each new wall is compact, so a good coupling exists at the next stage, and the radical line of each shadow wall has an explicit global nowhere-zero spanning section, so collar data for the next coupling exist. Degeneracy is conserved along the whole sequence: each completion resolves its wall and produces the next.
sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence.lay: Provided the wall is compact and each repair is done gently enough (a good coupling at every stage), repairing a degenerate wall on one side creates a new wall a little further away, and that wall can be repaired in the same way. Repeating this forever gives an infinite chain of walls, each carrying an algebra built on two more dimensions than the last. The degeneracy is never destroyed, only pushed further from the physical region at each step.
sheaf.infinite-wall-sequence.typing_note: Both edges are real premises (the wall induction is iterated and the one-sided completion supplies ranks and signatures at each stage); tameness of the initial wall is carried through the induction lemma. Levels pass: lay now keeps compactness and good couplings at every stage.

proofs.main:
Induction on Lemma \claimref{sheaf.tame-wall-induction} via Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.setup-generalises-arbitrary-bundles}, choosing at each stage a good coupling (possible: each $\Sig^{(k)}$ is a closed subset of a compact collar of its predecessor, hence compact, so its $S$ is finite, and only an upper bound on $|\mu
u|$ is demanded). Each stage also needs its radical line trivial, so that collar data exist for the next coupling (Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling}); this is automatic, because the shadow wall's radical line carries an explicit global spanning section: writing $\alpha_0 := G^{-1}e$ for the metric dual of the transversal functional, so that $s = \alpha_0(u)$, the section
\[
x \;:=\; \alpha_0 \,+\, \mu eta s\, 
O \,+\, 
u eta s\, 
Inf
\]
satisfies $h(x, \alpha) = e(\alpha)\,(1 + 2\mu
u eta^2 s) = e(\alpha)\,F = 0$ on $\{F = 0\}$ for every $\alpha \in T^*M$, while $h(x, 
O) = 
u eta s - 
u eta s = 0$ and $h(x, 
Inf) = \mu eta s - \mu eta s = 0$: so $x$ spans $\ker h$ along $\Sig'$, globally and without zeros. sheaf.invariant-form-t3.technical:
Assume the wall $\Sig$ is a smooth closed hypersurface and the radical lines of $G$ along it form a smooth line bundle $\shL$ of corank one. Extend a local spanning section $k$ of $\shL$ off $\Sig$ and set $g_k = G(k,k)$, which vanishes on $\Sig$. Then $dg_k|_\Sig$ annihilates $T\Sig$, so it is a section of the conormal bundle; it does not depend on the extension of $k$; and under $k \mapsto ck$ it scales by $c^2|_\Sig$.

Hence $k \otimes k \mapsto dg_k|_\Sig$ is a well-defined bundle map $\delta : \shL \otimes \shL \to N^*\Sig$, canonically attached to the degeneration. Both sides are line bundles, so $\delta$ is nowhere zero exactly when it is an isomorphism $\shL^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sig$, and the transversality condition of tameness is precisely this demand.
sheaf.invariant-form-t3.lay: Suppose a geometry degenerates along a smooth wall, losing exactly one direction there in a smooth way (the first two tameness conditions). That direction loses its length as one crosses the wall, and how fast it does so can be measured without arbitrary choices, giving a canonical quantity on the wall. Asking that this quantity never vanish, so that the degeneration is first order, is the same as asking that the square of the dying direction match the direction across the wall.
sheaf.invariant-form-t3.typing_note: No edges: the lemma assumes only the first two tameness conditions, while the tameness postulate as a whole defines its third condition through this lemma, so the postulate was deliberately not added to assumes. Levels pass: the lay level now states the hypotheses (T1) and (T2), a smooth wall with a smooth corank-one radical line, which it had dropped.

proofs.main:
(1) $g_k$ vanishes identically on $\Sig$ (there $k$ spans the radical, so in particular $G(k,k) = 0$), so its differential at points of $\Sig$ vanishes on vectors tangent to $\Sig$.

(2) Two extensions differ by a covector field $m$ vanishing on $\Sig$; locally $m = \tau\, \tilde m$ for a defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$ and a smooth $\tilde m$. Then
\[
g_{k + m} - g_k \;=\; 2\,G(k, m) + G(m,m) \;=\; 2\tau\, G(k, \tilde m) + \tau^2 G(\tilde m, \tilde m).
\]
Differentiating at a point of $\Sig$ and using $\tau|_\Sig = 0$: the second term contributes $0$ (it vanishes to second order), and the first contributes $2\,G(k, \tilde m)\, d\tau|_\Sig$, which vanishes because $G(k, \cdot)|_\Sig = 0$. Hence $dg_{k+m}|_\Sig = dg_k|_\Sig$.

(3) $g_{ck} = c^2 g_k$, so $dg_{ck}|_\Sig = c^2\, dg_k|_\Sig + 2c\,g_k\,dc|_\Sig = c^2\, dg_k|_\Sig$, the second term vanishing because $g_k|_\Sig = 0$. Well-definedness of $\delta$ on the line bundle $\shL^{\otimes 2}$, whose local frames are exactly the $c^2 (k \otimes k)$ ($c$ nonvanishing), is (2) and (3) together.

sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank.formal: For any cometric $G$ on $M$, degenerate or not, $\shA$ is a locally free sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules of constant rank $2^n$, with multiplication given in any blade frame by structure functions polynomial in the components of $G$, hence smooth. In particular the rank of $\shA$ does not detect the degeneration: no dimension jump occurs, or can occur, in the Clifford sheaf of a degenerating cometric.
sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank.technical:
For any cometric $G$ on $M$, degenerate or not, the Clifford sheaf $\shA$ is a locally free sheaf of $\mathcal{O}_M$-modules of constant rank $2^n$. On any open set where $T^*M$ has a frame, the blades $e_I$ give a basis of each fibre, by the blade-basis lemma applied pointwise to $G_x$, so they form a frame of $\shA$; the structure functions are polynomials in the smooth functions $G(e_i, e_j)$, hence smooth.

In particular the rank of $\shA$ does not detect the degeneration: no dimension jump occurs, or can occur, in the Clifford sheaf of a degenerating cometric.
sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank.lay: Gluing together the Clifford algebras at all points of a space gives a smoothly varying family of algebras. This result shows that the family has the same size everywhere, even where the geometry degenerates. So degeneration cannot be detected by counting dimensions; it has to show up in the structure of the algebra instead.

sheaf.localised-transport.formal: The subalgebra of $\shC$ generated by $T^*M$ is canonically isomorphic to $\shA$, globally, including over $\Sig$, because $h$ restricted to $T^*M$ equals $G$ identically by construction. Over $\Mo \cap \Mp$ the inclusion $\shA \subset \shC$ is fibrewise the conformal embedding $\Cl(p,q) \subset \Cl(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ of Rule 1 \cite{ButlerT1}. Over $\Sig$ the very same elements change ideal-theoretic character: a radical covector $k$ satisfies $k^2 = 0$ in both algebras, but the two-sided ideal it generates is square-zero in $A(x)$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.degeneration-sheaf}) and is the whole algebra in $C(x)$ (Proposition \claimref{sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically}), where $k$ acquires a partner $k^*$ built from the coupling, with $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ and $(k^*)^2 = 0$. The completion does not modify the degenerate algebra; it re-embeds it where its infinitesimals cease to be infinitesimal. In particular the localised ladder pair $(k, k^*)$ exists exactly over $\Sig$: the CAR structure of the series' operator-algebraic reading is supported on the singular locus.
sheaf.localised-transport.technical:
The subalgebra of the ambient sheaf $\shC = \Cl(T, h)$ generated by $T^*M$ is canonically isomorphic to $\shA$ globally, the wall included, because $h$ restricts to $G$ on $T^*M$ identically. Over $\Mo \cap \Mp$ the inclusion $\shA \subset \shC$ is fibrewise the conformal embedding $\Cl(p,q) \subset \Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$. Over $\Sig$ a radical covector $k$ has $Q(k) = 0$ in both algebras, yet the two-sided ideal it generates is square-zero in $A(x)$ and is the whole of $C(x)$, where $k^* = \nO/(2\nu)$ satisfies $Q(k^*) = 0$ and $k k^* + k^* k = 1$.

So the completion does not modify the degenerate algebra; it re-embeds it where its infinitesimals cease to be infinitesimal. The ladder pair $(k, k^*)$ exists exactly over $\Sig$, so the canonical anticommutation structure of the series' operator-algebraic reading is supported on the singular locus.
sheaf.localised-transport.lay: When the degenerate algebra is placed inside the larger completed algebra, it sits there unchanged. What changes is its surroundings: on the wall, a direction of zero length that was a dead end in the small algebra finds a partner in the large one, and together they behave like the creation and annihilation operators of a single fermion. This pairing happens only on the wall, so the fermion-like structure lives exactly where the geometry is singular.

sheaf.log-obstruction.formal:
For $e$ smooth on $E$,
\[
\tau\partial_\tau\,\tau^{e(x)} \;=\; e(x)\,\tau^{e(x)},
\qquad
\partial_x\,\tau^{e(x)} \;=\; e'(x)\,\tau^{e(x)}\log\tau .
\]
Consequently $\mathcal{A}$ is a commutative algebra stable under $\tau\partial_\tau$; it is stable under tangential vector fields if and only if every exponent is locally constant; and the obstruction is genuine: if $e'(x_0) \neq 0$ then $\tau^{e(x)}\log\tau$ does not lie in $\mathcal{A}$ near $(x_0,0)$.
sheaf.log-obstruction.technical:
For a smooth exponent $e$, $\tau\partial_\tau\, \tau^{e(x)} = e(x)\,\tau^{e(x)}$ and $\partial_x\, \tau^{e(x)} = e'(x)\,\tau^{e(x)}\log\tau$. So the variable-order algebra $\mathcal{A}$ is a commutative algebra stable under $\tau\partial_\tau$, but it is stable under tangential vector fields only if every exponent is locally constant.

The obstruction is genuine: if $e'(x_0) \neq 0$ then $\tau^{e(x)}\log\tau$ does not lie in $\mathcal{A}$ near $(x_0,0)$. The proof supposes an expansion in an admissible family of powers, removes the negative powers one at a time, and reaches the contradiction that $\log\tau$ would be bounded near $\tau = 0$.
sheaf.log-obstruction.lay: Powers of the distance to a boundary, with the power varying from point to point, behave well when one differentiates towards the boundary. Differentiating along the boundary instead produces a logarithm, and that logarithm cannot be rewritten in terms of such powers. So the algebra of these powers is closed under all derivatives only when the powers are locally constant.
sheaf.log-obstruction.typing_note: No edges: the proof is the chain rule plus a self-contained exponent-raising argument. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main:
The displayed formulas are the chain rule on $\tau^e = \exp(e\log\tau)$. For the non-membership, fix $x = x_0$, write $e_0 := e(x_0)$, and suppose $\tau^{e_0}\log\tau = \sum_j g_j(\tau)\,\tau^{c_j}$ with $g_j$ smooth and $\{c_j\}$ an admissible exponent family evaluated at $x_0$: distinct reals, only finitely many below any level. Absorb the finitely many terms with $c_j = e_0$ into the left side and divide by $\tau^{e_0}$:
\[
\log\tau - g(\tau) \;=\; \sum_j g_j(\tau)\,\tau^{d_j}, \qquad d_j := c_j - e_0 \ \text{distinct and nonzero},
\]
with $g$ smooth. Split the right side into the positive part $P$ ($d_j > 0$: finitely many terms below level $1$ plus an $O(\tau)$ tail, so $P = o(1)$) and the negative part $R$ ($d_j < 0$: finitely many terms, by admissibility). Then $R = \log\tau + O(1)$, so in particular $R = o(\tau^{-\varepsilon})$ for every $\varepsilon > 0$. We raise the exponents of $R$ one at a time. Let $d_{\min} < 0$ be the least exponent present in $R$; every term of $\tau^{|d_{\min}|} R = \sum g_j \tau^{d_j + |d_{\min}|}$ has nonnegative exponent, so it extends continuously to $\tau = 0$ with limit $g_{j_0}(0)$, where $j_0$ is the (unique, exponents being distinct) index with $d_{j_0} = d_{\min}$. But $\tau^{|d_{\min}|} R = \tau^{|d_{\min}|}(\log\tau + O(1)) \to 0$; hence $g_{j_0}(0) = 0$, and $g_{j_0} \tau^{d_{\min}} = (g_{j_0}/\tau)\,\tau^{d_{\min}+1}$ with $g_{j_0}/\tau$ smooth: the term's exponent rises by one (merging with another term if the exponents now coincide). Each step raises the least exponent, and after finitely many steps every exponent in $R$ is nonnegative, making $R$ bounded near $0$. Then $\log\tau = g + P + R = O(1)$, contradicting $\log\tau \to -\infty$.

sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist.formal:
At a tame wall the physical metric (the inverse cometric) has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$,
\[
O \;:=\; \lim_{\tau \to 0}\, \tau\, G^{-1} \;=\; \frac{k \otimes k}{\delta(k \otimes k)/d\tau} ,
\]
a nowhere-vanishing section of $\shL \otimes \shL$ depending on $\tau$ through the weight of a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig$; invariantly, the residue is $\delta^{-1}$, the inverse of the transversality datum of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}, regarded as a section of $\shL \otimes \shL \otimes N\Sig = \operatorname{Hom}(N^*\Sig, \shL^{\otimes 2})$. It is a nondegenerate pairing between $\shL^* \otimes \shL^*$ and $N^*\Sig$, hence induces a canonical isomorphism
\[
N^*\Sig \;\cong\; \shL^{\otimes 2} :
\]
the conormal bundle is the square of the dying direction itself. Dually, $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$: the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, which the pairing normalisation $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ identifies with $\shL^*$, is a canonical square root of the \emph{normal} bundle, and the dying line $\shL$ is a canonical square root of the conormal bundle. (The reading of the blow-up rescaling $k \mapsto k/\sqrt{t}$ as the normalisation of a conormal square root is Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.blow-up-dictionary}.)
sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist.technical:
At a wall satisfying the tameness postulate, the physical metric, the inverse cometric, has a canonical simple pole: for any defining function $\tau$ of $\Sig$, $\lim_{\tau \to 0} \tau\, G^{-1} = (k \otimes k)/(\delta(k \otimes k)/d\tau)$, a nowhere-vanishing section of $\shL \otimes \shL$ that depends on $\tau$ only through the weight of a normal vector. Invariantly the residue is $\delta^{-1}$, the inverse of the transversality datum, viewed as a section of $\operatorname{Hom}(N^*\Sig, \shL^{\otimes 2})$.

Being nowhere zero, it gives a canonical isomorphism $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$: the conormal line is the square of the dying line. Dually $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$, and the Witt partner line adjoined by the completion, identified with $\shL^*$ by the normalisation $kk^* + k^*k = 1$, is a canonical square root of the normal bundle.
sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist.lay: Near a degenerate wall of the well-behaved kind the series assumes (a tame wall, where the degeneration is transverse), the ordinary metric blows up like one over the distance to the wall. The coefficient of this blow-up turns out to be the inverse of the canonical rate at which the geometry degenerates. It shows that the direction across the wall is, in a precise sense, the square of the direction that dies, so the extra direction added in the repair is a square root of the direction across the wall.
sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist.typing_note: The exceptional-rescaling proposition is invoked only in the closing interpretation of the rescaling, which the statement defers to a remark, so it was removed; the statement is made at a tame wall, so the tameness postulate was added to assumes. Levels pass: all three levels now name tameness as the assumed postulate; lay had dropped it.

proofs.main:
Work in the frame $(k, m_1, \dots, m_{n-1})$ of Remark \claimref{note.sheaf.coordinates-crossing-speed} along a transversal with parameter $\tau$, with Gram $G(\tau) = \begin{psmallmatrix} \lambda & b^{\mathsf T} \\ b & G_1 \end{psmallmatrix}$, $\lambda(0) = 0$, $b(0) = 0$, $G_1(0)$ invertible, and $\lambda'(0) =: T \neq 0$, so that $\delta(k \otimes k) = T\, d\tau$. The inverse cometric $G^{-1}$, a symmetric form on $TM$, has matrix $C := [\text{Gram}]^{-1}$ with respect to the covector basis, meaning $G^{-1} = \sum C_{ab}\, \kappa_a \otimes \kappa_b$ over the frame covectors $\kappa = (k, m)$. Block inversion:
\[
C_{00} = (\lambda - b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} b)^{-1} = \frac{1}{T\tau}\bigl(1 + O(\tau)\bigr), \qquad
C_{0i} = -C_{00}\, (b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1})_i = O(1),
\]
since $b = O(\tau)$ makes $b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} b = O(\tau^2)$ and $C_{00}\,O(\tau) = O(1)$; and the $m$-block of $C$ is $G_1^{-1} + G_1^{-1} b\, C_{00}\, b^{\mathsf T} G_1^{-1} = O(1)$. Multiplying by $\tau$ and letting $\tau \to 0$, every entry goes to zero except the top-left:
\[
\tau\, G^{-1} \;\longrightarrow\; \frac{1}{T}\, k \otimes k .
\]
Independence of the extension of $k$: by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}(2) the derivative $T = dg_k(\partial_\tau)|_\Sig$ is extension-independent. Dependence on the scale of $k$: $k \mapsto ck$ multiplies the numerator $k \otimes k$ by $c^2$ and $T$ by $c^2$ (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3}(3)); the limit is unchanged, so the residue does not depend on $k$ at all, only on the line $\shL$ and the degeneration. Dependence on $\tau$: replacing $\tau$ by $a\tau$ ($a > 0$ smooth) multiplies the limit by $a|_\Sig$, exactly the transformation of the $d\tau$-coefficient of a section of $N\Sig$; the assignment $d\tau \mapsto \lim \tau G^{-1}$ is therefore a well-defined homomorphism $N^*\Sig \to \shL^{\otimes 2}$, and the computation identifies it as $d\tau \mapsto (1/T)\,k \otimes k = \delta^{-1}(d\tau)$: the analytic residue \emph{is} the algebraic transversality datum, inverted. It is nowhere vanishing because $\delta$ is an isomorphism under (T3) (\claimref{sheaf.tameness}). A nowhere-vanishing homomorphism between line bundles is an isomorphism, giving $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ (equivalently, the nondegenerate pairing $(\shL^* \otimes \shL^*) \otimes N^*\Sig \to \R$ induced by $\delta^{-1}$, whence $N^*\Sig \cong (\shL^* \otimes \shL^*)^* = \shL^{\otimes 2}$); dualising gives $N\Sig \cong (\shL^*)^{\otimes 2}$. The partner identification: in the ambient completion, $k^* = \nO/(2\nu)$ satisfies $kk^* + k^*k = 1$ (Corollary \claimref{sheaf.localised-transport}), so rescaling $k \mapsto ck$ forces $k^* \mapsto k^*/c$: the partner line is canonically $\shL^*$, hence a square root of $N\Sig$. Finally, $\shL^{\otimes 2} \cong N^*\Sig$ says exactly that $k$ carries the weight of a half-power of a defining function, and $k/\sqrt t$ is weightless: the rescaling of Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-deformation-normal-cone} is the canonical normalisation.

sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall.formal:
At a point of $\Sig$ with the collar constants $\mu, 
u$ and the bump held fixed, call a vector $u'$ with $k(u') = 1$ a \emph{candidate value} for the dying direction $k$; the candidates form an affine space over $\ker k$. For every $\lambda \in \ker k$ the composite $	heta_\lambda := \hat g_\lambda \circ \Phi_\lambda^{-1}$, with $\hat g_\lambda := g_\lambda \oplus \id$ on $T = T^*M \oplus \operatorname{span}\{
O, 
Inf\}$, is an automorphism of the completed structure $(T, h_u, k)$: an $h_u$-isometry restricting to $g_\lambda$ on $T^*M$ and fixing $k$, hence an automorphism of the completed Clifford algebra preserving its grading and its degeneration subalgebra. Its contragredient action on vectors, $(	heta_\lambda|_{T^*M})^{-\mathsf{T}} = \id - \lambda \otimes k$, translates every candidate by $-\lambda$. A natural assignment of a candidate value, one per completed structure and commuting with automorphisms, would therefore be a fixed point of a free translation action of $(\ker k, +)$: none exists. Nor is a ladder partner for $k$ any more canonical than a value: for $\lambda 
eq 0$, $h_u(k, x) = 0$ for every $x \in \operatorname{Fix}(	heta_\lambda)$, whereas a ladder partner has $h_u(k, x) = 	frac12$; and the construction attaches to each candidate $u' = u + v$ the partner $\Phi_v(k^*) = k^* + 	frac12	ilde v$ of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.transversal-independence-wall}, injectively in $v$. An analogue of the no-repair theorem of \cite[Thm.~4.2]{ButlerT1} thus holds at the wall itself, where the base form carries no hyperbolic partner for $k$ and that theorem's hypotheses fail.
sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall.technical:
At a wall point, with the collar constants and bump fixed, a candidate value for the dying direction $k$ is a vector $u'$ with $k(u') = 1$; the candidates form an affine space over $\ker k$. For each $\lambda \in \ker k$ the composite $\theta_\lambda = \hat g_\lambda \circ \Phi_\lambda^{-1}$ is an automorphism of the completed structure $(T, h_u, k)$, hence of the completed Clifford algebra with its grading and degeneration subalgebra, and on vectors it acts by $\id - \lambda \otimes k$, translating every candidate by $-\lambda$.

A natural assignment of a candidate value, commuting with automorphisms, would be a fixed point of a free translation action of $\ker k$, so none exists. A ladder partner for $k$ is no more canonical: for $\lambda \neq 0$ every $x$ fixed by $\theta_\lambda$ has $h_u(k,x) = 0$, whereas a partner has $h_u(k,x) = \tfrac12$, and distinct candidates give distinct partners. This is an analogue at the wall of the fibre-level no-repair theorem, whose hypotheses fail there.
sheaf.no-equivariant-value-wall.lay: To repair the wall one has to pick a direction to pair with the dying one. This result shows that the repaired structure has symmetries that move any such choice to a different one, so no choice can be singled out naturally. The same holds for the partner element used in the repair: it is a choice, not something the geometry provides.

sheaf.one-sided-completion.formal: Assume (T1)-(T3), with signature $(p,q)$, $p \geq 1$, on the physical side $\Mp$, and assume the radical line bundle is trivial, $w_1(\shL) = 0$, so that collar data exist. Then there exists a smooth symmetric form $h$ on $T$ over $M$, equal to $G \perp H$ outside a collar of $\Sig$, which is nondegenerate of constant signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ at every point of $\Mp$, including $\Sig$ itself. Consequently $\shC := \Cl(T, h)$ restricted to $\Mp$ is a locally free sheaf of algebras of constant rank $2^{n+2}$ whose every fibre is isomorphic to $\Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$; in the physical case, $\Cl(2,4) \cong \Mat_4(\HH)$.
sheaf.one-sided-completion.technical:
Assume tameness (T1)-(T3), signature $(p,q)$ with $p \geq 1$ on the physical side $\Mp$, and a trivial radical line bundle, $w_1(\shL) = 0$, so that collar data exist. Then there is a smooth symmetric form $h$ on $T = T^*M \oplus \underline{\R}^2$, equal to $G \perp H$ outside a collar of $\Sig$, that is nondegenerate of constant signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ at every point of $\Mp$, the wall included.

The proof takes coupling constants with $\mu\nu > 0$: on $\Sig$ the wall Gram gives the signature directly; in the collar on the physical side, after shrinking the collar, $s > 0$ and so $1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s \geq 1$ in the determinant identity; outside the collar $h = G \perp H$. Consequently $\shC = \Cl(T, h)$ restricted to $\Mp$ is locally free of rank $2^{n+2}$ with every fibre isomorphic to $\Cl(p{+}1, q{+}1)$, which is $\Mat_4(\HH)$ in the physical case.
sheaf.one-sided-completion.lay: Assume a geometry degenerates along a wall in the tame way, with at least one positive direction on the physical side and with the dying direction's line consistently orientable along the wall. Then it can be repaired on that side by adding two extra dimensions and coupling them to the direction that is dying. This result shows that the coupling can be chosen so that the enlarged geometry is non-degenerate, with the same signature everywhere on the physical side, the wall itself included. The resulting family of algebras is then uniform: in the physical case every member is the algebra of four-by-four quaternion matrices.
sheaf.one-sided-completion.typing_note: the statement assumes (T1)-(T3) explicitly, so the tameness postulate is added to assumes; the existence of collar data from w_1 = 0 is carried by the collar-data definition and its imported line-bundle fact, so no edge was added for it Levels pass: the lay level now states tameness, $p \geq 1$ and the triviality of the radical line bundle, all of which it had dropped.

proofs.main:
Take collar data with $\mu\nu > 0$ (Definition \claimref{obj.sheaf.collar-data-coupling}; they exist because the radical line bundle $\shL$ of \claimref{sheaf.tameness} is trivial) and $h = G \perp H + \kappa$; the equality $h = G \perp H$ outside the collar is built in. Nondegeneracy on $\Mp$, in three regions.

\emph{On $\Sig$}: Lemma \claimref{sheaf.wall-gram}(4) gives nondegeneracy with signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$ directly.

\emph{In the collar, physical side}: here $\lambda > 0$, so by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(2) there is a locally uniform constant $C$ with $s \geq 1/\lambda - C$; shrinking the collar (to a possibly variable-width collar, using local uniformity) until $1/\lambda \geq 2C$ on its physical side gives $s \geq 1/(2\lambda) > 0$ there. Then $1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s \geq 1$, so by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(1) $\det h \neq 0$: nondegenerate.

\emph{Outside the collar}: $h = G \perp H$, nondegenerate of signature $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ since $G$ is nondegenerate of signature $(p,q)$ on $\Mo \cap \Mp$.

For the signature on all of $\Mp$: the signature of a continuous nondegenerate form is locally constant, and every point of $\Mp$ is connected within the nondegeneracy region $\Mp$ to either $\Sig$ or the exterior of the collar (follow the transversal), where the signature is $(p{+}1,q{+}1)$ by the first and third cases. The final sentence of the theorem is then Proposition \claimref{sheaf.local-freeness-constant-rank} applied to $(T, h)$ over $\Mp$: a locally free sheaf of algebras of rank $2^{n+2}$ with every fibre the Clifford algebra of a form of signature $(p{+}1, q{+}1)$.

sheaf.rain-duality.technical:
At every interior radius of the Schwarzschild composite, the coframe $(\dtPG, k/\sqrt r, \mu_1, \mu_2)$ is exactly dual to the infalling (rain) orthonormal frame, and its Gram is the Minkowski form $\operatorname{diag}(1,-1,-1,-1)$ at every radius, horizon and collar included; $\dtPG$, the Painlev\'e-Gullstrand time differential, is the rain's proper-time differential. A $u$-smooth one-form lies in the weighted module $\shW$ exactly when its rain-frame components are bounded up to the singularity; the norm identity $|\alpha|_G^2 = \alpha(V)^2 - \sum_i \alpha(e_{\hat\imath})^2$ holds, but a bounded norm alone does not imply membership.

The module $\shW_{\mathrm{exc}}$ spanned by the rain coframe is the exceptional-regime module, rain-frame components are exactly its coefficients, and $\shW \subset \shW_{\mathrm{exc}}$ via $\rho = \sqrt r\,(k/\sqrt r) - m\,\dtPG$, with transition determinant $-\sqrt r$. So the weighted module is the $u$-smooth shadow of the rain observer's covector space.
sheaf.rain-duality.lay: An observer falling freely into a black hole, often called the rain observer, carries measuring directions that never degenerate, even at the horizon. This result shows that the module used to describe the degeneration at the singularity consists exactly of the smooth one-forms whose components, as the rain observer measures them, stay finite. The degenerate description and the non-degenerate one thus correspond to the smooth structure of the blow-up and to the rain frame.
sheaf.rain-duality.typing_note: Kept both edges; the closing reading of the forced-weights dichotomy is interpretive, so that context reference was not added, though it is arguable. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main: All clauses are exact rational-function identities, verified at two masses, the angular clauses at the equator; general position is literally the same algebra, since $\sin\theta$ enters $\mu_2$ and $e_{\hat\phi}$ reciprocally and cancels identically in every pairing and Gram entry used (the section “Machine verification”). (1) is the pairing table: $\dtPG(V) = 1$, $(k/\sqrt r)(e_{\hat r}) = 1$, $\mu_i(e_{\hat\imath}) = 1$, all others zero. (2): $G(\dtPG,\dtPG) = 1$, $G(\dtPG, k/\sqrt r) = 0$, $G(k/\sqrt r, k/\sqrt r) = g_k/r = -1$ exactly, by Theorem \claimref{sheaf.schwarzschild-degeneration-boundary-tame}. (3): membership in $\shW$ gives bounded components by (1) applied to the frame. Conversely, write $\alpha = A\,du + B\,dt + C'\,d\theta + D'\sin\theta\,d\phi$ with $u$-smooth coefficients: boundedness of $\alpha(e_{\hat r}) = A/(2u)$ forces $A = O(u)$, then boundedness of $\alpha(V) = B - mA/(2u^2)$ forces $A = O(u^2)$, and boundedness of the angular components $C'/u^2$, $D'/u^2$ forces $C', D' = O(u^2)$; a $u$-smooth function that is $O(u^2)$ is $u^2$ times a $u$-smooth function (Taylor division), so $\alpha$ is a $C^\infty(\Mt_u)$-combination of $\rho$, $dt$, $\mu_1$, $\mu_2$: $\alpha \in \shW$. The norm identity itself is the statement that the frame of (1) is $G$-orthonormal, i.e.\ clause (2). (4): the displayed transition and its determinant $\det\begin{psmallmatrix} -m & \sqrt r\\ 1 & 0\end{psmallmatrix} = -\sqrt r$; the frame comparison with Proposition \claimref{sheaf.exceptional-algebra-black-hole} replaces the timelike leg $\rho$ by $\dtPG$ through the same transition.

sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically.formal: Let $x \in \Sig$ and let $(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ be any nondegenerate quadratic space containing $(T^*_xM, G_x)$ as a subspace with the restricted form (a fibrewise completion, in the sense of the series). Then in $\Cl(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ the image of the radical line $\shL(x)$ generates the \emph{unit} ideal: the two-sided ideal generated by $k$ contains $1$. Resolution therefore converts a square-zero ideal into the unit ideal: it turns an infinitesimal into a dimension.
sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically.technical:
At $x \in \Sig$, embed $(T^*_xM, G_x)$ with its form into any nondegenerate quadratic space $(\mathbb{W}, Q)$. The radical covector $k$ stays null but is no longer radical, so there is $v$ with $Q(k, v) = \tfrac12$, and $k^* = v - Q(v)\,k$ is a null partner with $k k^* + k^* k = 1$ in $\Cl(\mathbb{W}, Q)$.

Both summands lie in the two-sided ideal generated by $k$, so that ideal contains $1$. Resolution therefore converts the square-zero ideal of the degenerate fibre into the unit ideal: an infinitesimal becomes a dimension.
sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically.lay: On the wall, the zero-length direction generates only an infinitesimal part of the algebra, one whose products all vanish. Once the geometry is enlarged to a non-degenerate one, in any way at all, that same direction finds a partner, and together they produce the number one. So the infinitesimal turns into a genuine new dimension.
sheaf.resolution-ideal-theoretically.typing_note: no edges in the draft and none needed; the hyperbolic-pair construction is reproved inline and the series citation is context only

proofs.main:
In $(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ the vector $k$ is null but no longer radical ($Q$ is nondegenerate), so there is a null partner: pick $v$ with $Q(k, v) \neq 0$, rescale so that $Q(k,v) = \tfrac12$, and set $k^* := v - Q(v,v)\,k$; then $Q(k^*, k^*) = Q(v,v) - 2\,Q(v,v)\,Q(k,v) = 0$ and $Q(k, k^*) = Q(k,v) = \tfrac12$ (this is the hyperbolic-pair construction of \cite[\S 2.2]{ButlerT1}, reproved here in one line). The Clifford relation (\claimref{std-algebra.vector-squares}) then gives in $\Cl(\mathbb{W}, Q)$ the identity
\[
k\,k^* + k^*\,k \;=\; 1 .
\]
Both summands lie in the two-sided ideal generated by $k$; hence so does $1$.

sheaf.solve-closed-radical-gauge.technical: At the wall the cometric $G$ has radical $\R k$, so the map $\alpha \mapsto G(\alpha, \cdot)$ has image exactly $\ker k$. Hence for every $v \in \ker k$ there is a covector $\tilde v$ with $G(\alpha, \tilde v) = \alpha(v)$ for all $\alpha$, unique up to adding multiples of $k$. Under $\tilde v \mapsto \tilde v + tk$ the quantity $G(\tilde v, \tilde v) + 2\tilde v(u)$ changes by $2t\,k(u) = 2t$, so exactly one representative meets the normalisation $G(\tilde v, \tilde v) + 2\tilde v(u) = 0$.
sheaf.solve-closed-radical-gauge.lay: At the wall the geometry cannot be inverted in the usual way, because one direction has no length. Still, for directions compatible with the dying one, an inverse exists up to an ambiguity along the dying direction. A single extra condition removes that ambiguity uniquely.
sheaf.solve-closed-radical-gauge.typing_note: No edges: the proof is a rank count and a one-line gauge computation.

sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagona.formal: For every relatively admissible $\Xi_\bullet$, the perturbed pair $(\shW, G + \Xi_\bullet)$ is congruent, by a transition in $GL_4(\mathcal{A})$ which is the identity on the exceptional boundary, to diagonal data over $\mathcal{A}$ with the \emph{same} exponents and perturbed unit entries $c_i' = c_i(1 + O(\tau^\delta))$, boundary units of $\mathcal{A}$ in the sense of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.boundary-units-invert} (smoothness of the units is not preserved, membership in $\mathcal{A}$ is). Consequently every conclusion of Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} holds verbatim for the perturbed data: the same module, corank one with the same radical, dying eigenvalue of exactly first order in $\varrho$ with the unperturbed leading unit, the $(2,4)$ completion with no shadow wall, and the same pointwise-forced weights.
sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagona.technical:
Perturb strict diagonal data by a relatively admissible error $\Xi_\bullet$. Then $(\shW, G + \Xi_\bullet)$ is congruent, by a transition in $GL_4(\mathcal{A})$ that is the identity on the exceptional boundary, to diagonal data over $\mathcal{A}$ with the same exponents and unit entries $c_i' = c_i(1 + O(\tau^\delta))$; these are boundary units of $\mathcal{A}$, though not necessarily smooth.

The proof diagonalises the nondegenerate block by symmetric Gaussian elimination with invertible pivots, then removes the dying-slot cross terms, leaving the Schur complement $\tilde d = -\varrho c_1 (1 + O(\tau^\delta))$. Since the variable-weight theorem used only that the units are positive boundary units, all its conclusions hold verbatim: the same module, corank one with the same radical, a first-order dying eigenvalue with the unperturbed leading unit, the $(2,4)$ completion with no shadow wall, and the same forced weights.
sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagona.lay: The results for the anisotropic singularity were first proved for an idealised, perfectly diagonal geometry. This result shows that perturbations of the admissible size can be undone by a change of frame, leaving data of the same idealised form. So every conclusion of the idealised case survives such perturbations unchanged.
sheaf.stability-reduction-strict-diagona.typing_note: Kept both edges: unit inversion for the pivots and the variable-weight theorem whose conclusions are transferred. Levels pass: conditions already kept.

proofs.main:
The nondegenerate $3\times3$ block $H' = H + \Xi_H$ has determinant a boundary unit, so symmetric Gaussian elimination diagonalises it congruently over $\mathcal{A}$ with a unit transition: each pivot is a boundary unit plus $\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$, invertible in $\mathcal{A}$ by Lemma \claimref{sheaf.boundary-units-invert}. The dying-slot cross column $b$ has entries in $\varrho^{1/2}\tau^\delta\mathcal{A}$, so $x := H'^{-1}b$ lies in the same class, and the block congruence by $\mathrm{id}$ minus the column $x$ into slot $1$ eliminates it exactly, leaving the Schur complement
\[
\tilde d \;=\; G_{11} + \Xi_{11} - b^{\mathsf T}H'^{-1}b \;=\; -\varrho c_1 + \varrho\,\tau^\delta(\cdots) + \varrho\,\tau^{2\delta}(\cdots) \;=\; -\varrho\,c_1\bigl(1 + O(\tau^\delta)\bigr),
\]
the last term because the cross column's square carries $(\varrho^{1/2}\tau^\delta)^2 = \varrho\tau^{2\delta}$. The total transition is a product of unit transitions, hence a unit, and the result is diagonal data over $\mathcal{A}$ with perturbed unit entries; every conclusion quoted from Theorem \claimref{sheaf.variable-weight-boundary-tameness-completion-forced} used only that the units are positive boundary units of $\mathcal{A}$, never their smoothness. The congruence is executed explicitly in the verification script at a rational Kasner point with a concrete relatively admissible perturbation: cross-term elimination, the Schur identity, the preserved first-order eigenvalue with leading unit $-1$, corank and radical, and the perturbed completion's determinant identity, nonvanishing boundary determinant, and $(2,4)$ signatures.

sheaf.tame-wall-induction.technical:
Take $\Sig$ compact with a fixed collar. Near the wall on the far side, $s = 1/\lambda + O(1)$ is strictly monotone along transversals; outside this monotone zone, on the far part of the collar, $|s|$ is bounded by a finite $S$. Call the coupling good if $|\mu\nu| < 1/(2S)$. Then every far-side zero of $F = 1 + 2\mu\nu\beta^2 s$ lies in the monotone zone, and the shadow wall $\Sig' = \{F = 0\}$ is a smooth closed hypersurface across which $\det h$ has a simple zero.

Along $\Sig'$ exactly one eigenvalue of $h$ vanishes, to first order, and the radical line is a smooth line bundle, spanned locally by a column of $\operatorname{adj}(h)$. By Jacobi's formula the simplicity of the zero of $\det h$ is the nonvanishing of the transversality datum. So $(T,h)$ is again a tame corank-one degeneration along $\Sig'$, and the completion iterates for every good coupling, not merely generically.
sheaf.tame-wall-induction.lay: Repairing a degenerate wall on one side creates a new shadow wall on the other. This result shows that, for a compact original wall that degenerates in the well-behaved (tame) way, if the repair is done gently enough, the shadow wall is just as well behaved as the original. So the same repair can be applied to it, and the process can be repeated.
sheaf.tame-wall-induction.typing_note: Both edges are real premises; the proof uses the transversality condition of the original wall to bound the derivative, so the tameness postulate was added to assumes. Levels pass: lay now keeps compactness and tameness of the original wall; one-liner phrased as an assumption.

proofs.main:
\emph{The monotone zone, and finiteness of $S$.} By Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(2), $s = 1/\lambda + b$ with $b$ smooth up to the wall, locally uniformly; so $s' = -\lambda'/\lambda^2 + b'$, and since $\lambda \to 0$ while $\lambda'$ is bounded away from zero near $\Sig$ (T3, \claimref{sheaf.tameness}) and $b'$ is bounded (compactness of $\Sig$ makes all these bounds uniform along the wall), there is a one-sided collar neighbourhood on which $|\lambda'|/\lambda^2 > |b'|$: the monotone zone. Its far-side complement within the collar has compact closure disjoint from $\Sig$, on which the smooth function $s$ is bounded: $S < \infty$.

(1) Outside the collar $F = 1$; on the far collar side outside the monotone zone, $|2\mu\nu\beta^2 s| \leq 2|\mu\nu| S < 1$, so $F > 0$: no zeros in either region, whatever $\beta$ does there. All far-side zeros therefore lie in the monotone zone. Approaching the wall $F \to -\infty$ (Lemma \claimref{sheaf.determinant-identity-blow-up-expansion}(2)) and at the zone's outer edge $F > 0$, so each transversal carries a zero; where $\beta \equiv 1$ (shrink the zone into the inner collar if necessary), $F = 1 + 2\mu\nu s$ is strictly monotone along each transversal with a single simple zero, and $dF = 2\mu\nu\, ds$ has nonvanishing transversal component $2\mu\nu s' \neq 0$: $\{F = 0\}$ is a regular level set, a smooth closed hypersurface $\Sig'$, and $\det h = \det G \cdot (-F)$ has a simple zero across it ($\det G \neq 0$ there).

(2) At a simple zero of $\det h = \prod_i \mu_i$ (eigenvalues with respect to the auxiliary metric), exactly one eigenvalue $\mu_1$ vanishes and to first order: two vanishing eigenvalues would force a second-order zero. For the smoothness of the radical line, no spectral theory is needed: the adjugate $\operatorname{adj}(h)$, polynomial in the entries of $h$, is smooth; at a point of corank one it has rank exactly one (some $(d{-}1)$-minor is nonzero, and $h \cdot \operatorname{adj}(h) = \det(h)\,1 = 0$ puts every column of $\operatorname{adj}(h)$ in $\ker h$, which is a line). A nonvanishing column of $\operatorname{adj}(h)$ is therefore a smooth local spanning section of the radical line along $\Sig'$.

(3) Jacobi's formula, $\partial_\tau \det h = \operatorname{tr}\bigl(\operatorname{adj}(h)\, \partial_\tau h\bigr)$ (differentiate the determinant column by column and expand each along its differentiated column), evaluated at a point of $\Sig'$: in an auxiliary-orthonormal eigenbasis there, $\operatorname{adj}(h) = \bigl(\prod_{i \geq 2} \mu_i\bigr)\, \tilde k\, \tilde k^{\mathsf T}$ with $\tilde k$ the unit kernel vector, so
\[
\partial_\tau \det h \;=\; \Bigl(\prod_{i \geq 2} \mu_i\Bigr)\, (\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k) .
\]
The left side is nonzero (the zero of $\det h$ is simple, by (1)) and the nonvanishing eigenvalues $\mu_i$, $i \geq 2$, are nonzero; hence $(\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k) \neq 0$. This is exactly the nonvanishing of the datum $\delta'$ of Lemma \claimref{sheaf.invariant-form-t3} for $(T, h)$ along $\Sig'$: for any extension of $\tilde k$, $d\,h(\tilde k, \tilde k)|_{\Sig'} = (\partial_\tau h)(\tilde k, \tilde k)\, d\tau$, the cross term vanishing because $\tilde k$ is radical on $\Sig'$, and the lemma's proof uses only the symmetric form and the radical, not the cotangent origin of the bundle. So (T3) holds, (T1) and (T2) being parts (1) and (2).

sheaf.tame-walls-are-two-sided.formal: For any tame corank-one degeneration, the conormal bundle of $\Sig$ satisfies $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ (Theorem \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist}), hence has vanishing first Stiefel-Whitney class: $w_1(N^*\Sig) = 2\,w_1(\shL) = 0$. So $N\Sig$ is trivial, $\Sig$ is two-sided in $M$, and a global side choice (a co-orientation, hence the meaning of ``the physical side'') always exists. Tameness itself forbids one-sided walls: a hypersurface with M\"obius normal bundle admits no corank-one degeneration satisfying (T1)-(T3) along it.
sheaf.tame-walls-are-two-sided.technical: Under the tameness hypothesis (T1) to (T3), for any tame corank-one degeneration the residue theorem gives $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$, so $w_1(N^*\Sig) = 2w_1(\shL) = 0$. By the imported facts on real line bundles, $N\Sig$ is therefore trivial and $\Sig$ is two-sided in $M$. A global choice of side, and with it a meaning for the physical side, always exists, and no hypersurface with M\"obius normal bundle carries a corank-one degeneration satisfying the tameness conditions.
sheaf.tame-walls-are-two-sided.lay: Some surfaces, like a M\"obius band, have only one side. This result shows that, if a geometry degenerates along a wall in the tame way, as the tameness hypothesis requires, the wall can never be one-sided. So it always makes sense to speak of the physical side of the wall and the other side.
sheaf.tame-walls-are-two-sided.typing_note: Added the residue theorem, which supplies the isomorphism the corollary starts from, and the tameness postulate the statement assumes. Levels pass: the tameness condition was kept only as the adjective "tame"; all three plain levels now name it as the hypothesis.

proofs.main: A square of a real line bundle has trivial $w_1$ and a real line bundle is trivial exactly when its $w_1$ vanishes (Fact \claimref{sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles}); an isomorphism, here $N^*\Sig \cong \shL^{\otimes 2}$ of \claimref{sheaf.metrics-residue-square-root-twist} at a tame wall (\claimref{sheaf.tameness}), preserves $w_1$, and $N\Sig \cong (N^*\Sig)^*$ shares triviality. Two-sidedness of a hypersurface is triviality of its normal bundle (Fact \claimref{sheaf.imported-real-line-bundles}).

sheaf.tameness.technical: A pair $(M, G)$ is a tame corank-one degeneration if: (T1) the wall $\Sig$ is a smooth closed hypersurface of $M$; (T2) $G$ has corank exactly one at every point of $\Sig$, and the radical lines form a smooth line subbundle $\shL \subset T^*M|_\Sig$, locally spanned by a covector field $k$; and (T3) the degeneration is first order, meaning that the canonical transversality section $\delta$ is nowhere vanishing on $\Sig$.
sheaf.tameness.lay: This is the standing assumption on how a geometry is allowed to degenerate. The places where it degenerates must form a smooth closed wall, exactly one direction must lose its length at each point of the wall, and these directions must vary smoothly along it. In addition, the length must vanish at a linear rate as the wall is reached, not to higher order.
sheaf.tameness.typing_note: postulate with no derivation, so the context reference to the invariant-form lemma defining delta cannot be recorded as an edge; (T3) does depend on that lemma's definition
